I am submitting this complaint because Wells Fargos servicing of my auto loan, delinquency calculations, notice practices, and credit reporting contain material inconsistencies that can not all be accurate simultaneously. These inconsistencies have resulted in continued negative credit reporting, inability to obtain vehicle financing, and financial harm. The issues outlined below reflect a pattern of unreliable account servicing, inconsistent explanations, and unsupported reporting. 1. Reinstatement Payment Cured the Default, Yet Delinquency Was Improperly Continued Wells Fargo acknowledges that I made a reinstatement payment of {$1200.00} on XX/XX/year>, after a repossession event. Reinstatement is intended to cure the default and restore the account to good standing. Following reinstatement, the next contractual payment due date was XX/XX/year>, meaning any subsequent delinquency could not have begun until that date. However, Wells Fargo later asserted that I was 178 days delinquent at the time of the XX/XX/year> repossession. This calculation is inconsistent with the timeline following reinstatement. The period from XX/XX/year> to XX/XX/year> is approximately 89 days, not 178 days. This raises concerns that Wells Fargo improperly included pre-reinstatement delinquency in its calculation, despite the reinstatement curing the prior default. 2. Payment Misapplication Contrary to Wells Fargos Own Policy Wells Fargos documentation states that payments are applied in the following order : Accrued interest Principal balance Principal variance Unapplied balance adjustments Other charges However, when my {$1200.00} reinstatement payment was received, Wells Fargo separated approximately {$460.00} as an unapplied increase/decrease and applied it toward repossession-related charges before applying the remainder of the payment to the loan. This appears inconsistent with their stated payment application order and directly impacted whether : my XX/XX/year> obligation was satisfied the account would have remained current following reinstatement 3. Inconsistent and Unreliable Right-to-Cure Notice Production Wells Fargo previously stated that it had provided all relevant notices in prior correspondence, including in earlier regulatory responses. Those document productions did not include any Right-to-Cure notice dated XX/XX/year>. Wells Fargo has now produced a XX/XX/year> Right-to-Cure notice that was not included in prior disclosures, despite representing that all notices had already been provided. This raises concerns regarding the completeness, timing, and reliability of Wells Fargos document production. If Wells Fargo maintains that this XXXX notice was generated and sent at the time, it should provide verifiable proof of mailing, including vendor mailing records, system logs, or other contemporaneous evidence demonstrating that the notice was actually created and sent in XX/XX/year>. 4. Inconsistent Credit Reporting Across Consumer Reporting Agencies This account is reported inconsistently across the major credit bureaus, including : differing repossession designations conflicting delinquency histories inconsistent Date of First Delinquency reporting Additionally, reporting has changed during and after disputes and regulatory complaints, raising concerns regarding the reliability of prior investigations. These inconsistencies have resulted in : multiple credit denials inability to obtain vehicle financing increased insurance costs It seems to me the more I review this account, the more errors come up.

narrative: I am submitting a complaint regarding Wells Fargos handling of fraud claims involving XXXX transactions. My concern is that Wells Fargo is failing to properly evaluate fraud-induced transactions and is incorrectly categorizing them as no error, rather than addressing whether the transactions were obtained through deception. Through Wells Fargo, I sent a total of {$10000.00} via XXXX to a contractor as part of a home project. Timeline of events : XX/XX/year> : Contractor provided XXXX payment information and directed payment Approximately {$10000.00} was successfully sent via Wells Fargo ( an additional attempted payment was blocked as fraud ) Contractor confirmed receipt of funds ( Yes is all in ) and scheduled the job to begin XX/XX/XXXX : Contractor failed to appear ( no-show ) XX/XX/XXXX : Phone call with contractor, who recommitted to start the following day XX/XX/XXXX : Contractor failed to appear again ( second no-show ) XX/XX/year> : No communication despite multiple attempts to contact him XX/XX/XXXX : Written demand for return of funds sent XX/XX/XXXX : Fraud reported to Wells Fargo ; claims opened XXXX XXXX and XXXX ) XX/XX/XXXX : Report made to XXXX XXXX Sheriffs Office ; case opened and investigation initiated XX/XX/XXXX : Wells Fargo issued determinations on both claims, stating that no error occurred XX/XX/XXXX : I contacted Wells Fargo after receiving the denial and case closure notice ; I was informed the decision would not be changed, the case would not be reopened, and Wells Fargo stood by its no error determination The contractor confirmed receipt of the funds, set a start date, and then ceased all communication. He performed no work whatsoever and provided no materials. This was not a partially completed job or a dispute over qualityno work was performed and no materials were delivered. These Wells Fargo XXXX payments were not independent transactions. They were multiple installments tied to a single agreement, made under the belief that work would be performed. The contractors actions constitute deception : funds were obtained under false pretenses with no intent to perform. Wells Fargo has relied on a narrow interpretation of error and has not meaningfully addressed whether these transactions were induced through deception. While the transactions were processed through XXXX, that does not resolve the issue of fraud-induced payment. Authorization obtained through misrepresentation should not be treated as a valid, error-free transaction. While I understand XXXX transactions are typically considered authorized and irreversible, this situation involves authorization obtained through deception. This is not a dispute over servicesit is a case of complete non-performance and misrepresentation. XXXX framework does not eliminate a banks responsibility to evaluate whether a transaction was induced by fraud. Wells Fargo has relied solely on the fact that the transaction was authorized, without addressing whether that authorization was obtained under false pretenses. Classifying this as no error ignores the underlying fraud and effectively shifts all risk of deception to the customer, even where no services were provided and the recipient ceased communication entirely. This matter has been reported to the XXXX XXXX Sheriffs Office and is currently an active investigation. The contractor was contacted by law enforcement and indicated he would reach out to resolve the matter, but failed to do so and has continued to avoid communication. Wells Fargo has stated that it attempted to recover the funds from the receiving bank but was unsuccessful, and that no further action can be taken. I was also informed that I am not eligible for any goodwill reimbursement or credit. I have supporting documentation, including : Written estimate and agreement Payment confirmations Text messages confirming receipt of funds Evidence of complete non-performance Wells Fargo denial letters Despite clear evidence of deception and complete non-performance, Wells Fargo has classified the matter as involving no error and has assigned the full loss to me. To reiterate, my concern is that Wells Fargo is failing to properly evaluate fraud-induced transactions and is incorrectly categorizing them as no error, rather than addressing whether the transactions were obtained through deception. I am requesting : A full review of these claims as fraud by deception rather than a standard no error determination Reconsideration of reimbursement or account credit for the full amount of {$10000.00} A clear explanation of Wells Fargos policy regarding transactions induced by fraud and how they are evaluated under error determinations I am seeking a fair resolution consistent with the facts of this case.

I had approximately {$30000.00} in a savings account deposited at Wells Fargo with a promotional interest rate which was set to expire on XX/XX/XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, I went into my local branch in XXXX NC and was told in person that to receive a new, 12 month promotional interest rate that I would need to bring {$10000.00} of new cash to the bank. Thus, I went home and immediately transferred {$10000.00} from a XXXX XXXX account into my Wells Fargo checking account. On XX/XX/XXXX, I went back into a local branch in XXXXXXXX XXXX to confirm that the {$10000.00} had indeed cleared into my checking account and was available for any transaction. The teller confirmed that this new cash did qualify me for the new, 12 month promotion. To be clear : I was told in person on XX/XX/XXXX, that I had met the requirements for the new promotional rate. Thus, I authorized the immediate transfer of the new {$10000.00} into my savings account. Since this money had already cleared, and was at Wells Fargo, my assumption was that this would qualify me immediately for the new promotion which would start immediately. Thus, I was shocked and disappointed that I actually received 0 interest from XX/XX/XXXX until XXXX. Not only did I not receive any interest on the new {$10000.00} over this time, but my pre-existing savings account with a balance of {$30000.00} was reset from 4 % to 0 % on XX/XX/XXXX despite the fact that I still had an active promotional rate guaranteed until XXXX. The Wells Fargo Promotional Interest Rate Disclosure form states : " The promotional rate will be applied within15 calendar days of meeting the balance requirement. '' Thus, Wells Fargo 's contention is that they have met their contractual obligations and can refuse to pay any of the interest. My opinion, however, is that the contract wording is intentionally deceptive. A reasonable lay person reading this contract language would assume that if there is a hold it will because of a legitimate purpose -- for example, time needed to insure that the new money requirement has been satisfied. If the bank 's intension is to hold ALL new deposits without interest for 15 days then it should specify this in plain English. My understanding on XX/XX/XXXX was that my new cash had cleared into my bank account and that I was thus qualified to receive the promotion immediately ( that was, after all, the whole reason that I made two in person trips to the bank ). If this was not the case, I think it should have been incumbent on the bank teller to inform me that I would receive NO interest on the {$10000.00} for 15 days. He should also have been obligated to inform me that by signing a new contract that I would also lose all the interest on the {$30000.00} from XXXX. Interest that I was already entitled to by my old contract. Had I known these facts, I would never have agreed to the terms. I would have put the minimum ( {$10000.00} ) in a new Wells Savings account and then transferred the {$30000.00} back into my XXXX XXXX XXXX to prevent losing the 15 days worth of interest on this cash. I believe the contract ambiguity and the lack of any clear explanation by multiple bank tellers is an intentional practice by Wells Fargo so that they can hold funds without paying interest for extended periods. In the modern world, there are very rarely any legitimate reasons why a funds hold of 15 days should be needed. This practice is deceptive and unethical. And when extended over millions of accounts, it also is making the bank an enormous amount of money.

narrative: I am filing this complaint against Capital One for failure to conduct a lawful investigation of a billing dispute in violation of the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ), 15 U.S.C. 1666 et seq., and Regulation Z, 12 C.F.R. 1026.13. I. NATURE OF THE UNDERLYING DISPUTE On XX/XX/XXXX, I was charged {$2100.00} by XXXX * XXXX XXXX on my Capital One Venture X card ( a Visa Infinite product ). The basis of my dispute is that the hotel failed to deliver services as represented and billed me at a premium room rate for an inferior replacement room. Specifically : 1. My original room contained a pillow with visible XXXX staining and a couch with visible unknown staining. I have photographs documenting both conditions. XXXX XXXX 's own published policy XXXX XXXX XXXX expressly represents that guests receive " luxury linens '' as an included amenity. XXXX XXXXstained pillow does not satisfy that representation. XXXX. I was moved to a smaller replacement room. Staff made two separate commitments to thoroughly clean the replacement room. Both promises were broken. I have photographs of the uncleaned room taken after the second cleaning assurance. XXXX. The hotel billed me at the original higher room rate despite placing me in an inferior replacement room and agreeing via text message to bill me at the lower rate, this is a documented billing discrepancy supported by an invoice I provided to Capital One. XXXX. The property exhibited multiple life-safety code failures, including an unmounted fire extinguisher with an inspection tag dated XX/XX/XXXX, a locked door marked " EXIT, '' and a window labeled " ESCAPE WINDOW '' opening directly onto HVAC equipment. I have photographs of each condition. XXXX. I sent the hotel a written complaint requesting resolution within five business days. The hotel never responded. The reservation was made through XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ). XXXX 's own Terms and Conditions expressly identify chargebacks arising from a supplier 's failure to deliver services consistent with its product description as a cognizable dispute category. II. CAPITAL ONE 'S CONDUCT I timely initiated a chargeback dispute with Capital One. I submitted a detailed written narrative and supporting documentation, including photographs of the conditions described above, the hotel 's published policy, XXXX 's Terms and Conditions, and my unanswered written complaint to the hotel. Capital One subsequently requested one specific additional item : an invoice demonstrating the billing discrepancy between my booked room rate and the inferior replacement room I received. I again provided the requested invoice. Despite my submission, Capital One closed my case citing that I had failed to provide " previously requested information. '' That statement is factually inaccurate. I contacted Capital One and requested the case be reopened. Capital One closed the case a second time on the same stated basis. I submitted substantial documentation, including another copy of the invoice showing that I was overcharged. Capital One again closed the case stating that I had not provided requested documentation. That statement again is factually inaccurate. On XX/XX/XXXX, I called Capital One again to escalate. My first call was disconnected. On my second call, I spoke with a representative named Rain, who told me that Capital One had concluded its investigation and would not reopen the dispute. I then spoke with a supervisor identified as XXXX, a fraud account manager, who provided the following explanation for Capital One 's denial : that the merchant had a no-refund policy and Capital One would therefore honor the merchant 's position and not issue a refund. This explanation is legally untenable for two independent reasons. First, a merchant 's internal no-refund policy does not extinguish a cardholder 's federal chargeback rights under the FCBA. The FCBA creates a statutory right to dispute billing errors that exists independently of any merchant policy. A card issuer can not lawfully deny a chargeback solely on the ground that the merchant declines to issue a refund. That reasoning would render the FCBA meaningless in every case where a merchant refuses to cooperate. Second, and critically, this dispute is not solely a service quality complaint. I provided Capital One with an invoice demonstrating that I was billed at a higher room rate than was appropriate for the inferior replacement room I received. That is a billing error ( an overcharge ) independent of any service quality judgment. Capital One acknowledged receipt of that invoice, was provided documentary proof of the overbilling, and has nonetheless declined to act on it. XXXX 's statement that Capital One is deferring to the merchant 's no-refund policy confirms that Capital One did not conduct any substantive analysis of the billing discrepancy I documented. Capital One chose to accept the merchant 's position wholesale without engaging the evidence submitted by the cardholder. XXXX. LEGAL BASIS FOR COMPLAINT Under the FCBA and Regulation Z, Capital One is required to conduct a reasonable investigation of a billing dispute and may not simply adopt the merchant 's position as its own without engaging the cardholder 's evidence. Capital One 's conduct here of two procedural closures citing missing documentation that were in fact provided, followed by a substantive denial based entirely on the merchant 's no-refund policy while ignoring documentary proof of overbilling, does not satisfy the reasonable investigation standard. Capital One 's handling of this dispute has resulted in my being held liable for {$2100.00} for services not delivered as represented, including a documented overcharge that Capital One has refused to address. IV. RELIEF REQUESTED I request that the CFPB : XXXX. Require Capital One to reopen dispute case no. XXXX and conduct a substantive investigation ; XXXX. Require Capital One to explain in writing why the invoice documenting the billing discrepancy was not treated as evidence of a billing error independent of the merchant 's no-refund policy ; XXXX. Require Capital One to explain what, if any, investigation was conducted beyond soliciting and accepting the merchant 's position ; 4. Issue a full chargeback of {$2100.00} ; and 5. Review Capital One 's dispute handling practices for compliance with FCBA and Regulation Z obligations. Supporting documentation available : photographs ( original room staining, replacement room, life-safety failures ), invoice showing overbilling, hotel written complaint, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX Terms and Conditions, Capital One closure correspondence )

narrative: I am filing a complaint regarding an unauthorized transfer from my Bank of America account that was denied as a valid transaction. An unknown individual impersonated me over the phone, gained access to my account, transferred {$4900.00} internally, and then sent {$3500.00} externally through a third-party service. I did not authorize this transaction and did not benefit from it. Bank of America denied my claim, stating that the transaction benefited a valid signer. This is incorrect and ignores the fact that the account was accessed fraudulently through impersonation. Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( Regulation E ), this qualifies as an unauthorized electronic fund transfer. I am requesting that Bank of America : 1. Reopen and properly investigate this claim as fraud 2. Provide provisional credit 3. Comply with Regulation E protections I reported this promptly and have taken all appropriate steps to secure my accounts. Here is a full account of the events that happened : On XX/XX/year>, an unknown individual called Bank of America, impersonating me. This unknown individual was able to access my savings account via telephone and transfer {$4900.00} to my checking account. Then they were able to set up a recurring payment of {$3500.00} to my checking account to a wire transfer company, XXXX. Bank of America allowed this transaction to take place during the middle of the night. I received an email from the bank the following morning confirming that this transfer of funds took place. I immediately accessed my banking online and was able to see the transfer of funds from my savings to checking, and see the pending transaction from my checking account to XXXX for {$3500.00}. I called Bank of America to dispute these transactions and filed fraud claims on both the savings and checking accounts. I also went to my local Bank of America location and spent the entire day there with XXXX different individuals. I opened up XXXX new accounts, froze my checking account, and closed my savings account. They gave me a new debit card and set up a digital wallet with the new debit card number. Later, I tried to use my digital wallet to make a purchase, only to find out that Bank of America had associated this card with the old frozen account. I had to wait on hold with the bank for an hour before I could get the digital debit card issue resolved. Now I have received a letter dated XX/XX/year>, just XXXX business days later, determining that the fraud claim on my savings account was denied. Here I will quote the letter from Bank of America : " Our investigation found that the transfer in question was made to an account that provided a benefit to a valid signer on the account. In this case, the funds were made available to XXXX or more valid signers on the account for personal use, or for use to pay an obligation that's owed. We based our decision on our records and the information you provided when you contacted us about your account. Case closed. '' This is completely incorrect. I gave very detailed information to Bank of America customer service, along with two different people at a local Bank of America. I did not request this transfer, nor did I receive any benefit from it. The funds were moved and sent externally without my knowledge or consent. The determination states that the transaction benefited a valid signer on the account. This is incorrect. I did not authorize this transaction, and any access the third party obtained resulted from identity theft and an account takeover. I would also like to mention that every time I called customer service, they only use caller ID and ask your name to verify who you are. I asked all of them how this is an acceptable verification, including the individuals at the bank. They respond that this is their process, and a lot of people have a hard time remembering passwords or PIN numbers. I have sent an additional letter to the bank 's " check and digital recovery '' disputing this determination and requesting a prompt reopening of the fraud claim and a FULL re-investigation into the fraud.

This complaint is a continuation of CFPB Case # XXXX and concerns U.S. Banks failure to refund the full escrow balance on a now-closed mortgage account ( Account XXXX, property at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX. I. U.S. BANK ISSUED AN INCOMPLETE ESCROW REFUND On XX/XX/XXXX, U.S. Bank issued an escrow refund check ( Check # XXXX ) in the amount of {$2200.00}, payable to XXXX XXXX. This amount corresponds exactly to the real estate taxes paid from escrow in XXXX, as documented on the XXXX IRS Form 1098 for this account ( Box XXXX : Real Estate Taxes Paid {$2200.00} ). However, XXXX Banks own XXXX Annual Tax & Interest Statement for this account shows an escrow ending balance of {$2200.00} that remains unrefunded. This balance represents insurance premiums that were collected from the previously confirmed Successor in Interest and previous owner of the property, XXXX XXXX, through monthly escrow deposits throughout XXXX but were never disbursed by U.S. Bank. The XXXX escrow reconciliation on U.S. Banks own statement reads as follows : Beginning Balance : ( {$1200.00} ) Deposits : {$5900.00} Insurance Paid : {$120.00} Taxes Paid : {$2200.00} Additional Assessments Paid : {$0.00} Escrow Disbursement : {$100.00} Ending Balance : {$2200.00} II. THE MISSING FUNDS ARE IDENTIFIABLE AND DOCUMENTED A comparison of insurance disbursements across the three most recent tax years makes the shortfall unmistakable : XXXX : Insurance paid from escrow {$2000.00} XXXX : Insurance paid from escrow {$2200.00} XXXX : Insurance paid from escrow {$120.00} U.S. Bank collected escrow deposits throughout XXXX at a rate of {$440.00} per month a rate calculated to cover both taxes and insurance. The taxes were paid ( {$2200.00} ) and subsequently refunded via the XX/XX/XXXX check. The insurance premium was never disbursed ( only {$120.00} of an expected ~ $ XXXX was paid ), and the resulting escrow surplus of {$2200.00} was retained by U.S. Bank XXXX U.S. Bank has provided no accounting, no explanation, and no refund of this {$2200.00} balance. III. RESPA REQUIRES RETURN OF THE FULL ESCROW BALANCE Under the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ), 12 CFR 1024.34 ( b ), when a mortgage loan is paid in full, the servicer is required to return any amounts remaining in the escrow account to the previously confirmed Successor in Interest and previous owner of the property, XXXX XXXX, within 20 business days of the loan being paid off. The statute does not permit a servicer to return only a portion of the escrow balance. It does not permit a servicer to selectively refund taxes while retaining insurance reserves. The obligation is to return the entire remaining escrow balance every dollar held in escrow that has not been disbursed for its intended purpose. U.S. Banks refund of {$2200.00} covered only the tax component. The remaining {$2200.00} in escrow documented on U.S. Banks own annual statement has been withh eld in violation of 1024.34 ( b ). IV. U.S. BANK HAS ALREADY ACKNOWLEDGED ESCROW OBLIGATIONS ON THIS ACCOUNT In its XX/XX/XXXX response to CFPB Case # XXXX, U.S. Bank made a business decision to issue an escrow refund check. The check issued, however, accounts for only approximately half of the escrow funds held at the time of loan payoff. U.S. Bank did not provide any written accounting explaining why {$2200.00} in escrow reserves was excluded from the refund, nor did it identify any outstanding disbursement obligation that would justify retention of those funds. To be clear : U.S. Banks own 2025 Annual Tax & Interest Statement documents the {$2200.00} ending balance. This is not a disputed figure. It is U.S. Banks own number, on U.S. Banks own statement, for an account U.S. Bank has confirmed is closed and paid off. V. THIS CONTINUES A DOCUMENTED PATTERN OF MISHANDLING This incomplete refund is the latest in a multi-year pattern of escrow and account mismanagement by U.S. Bank on this account, documented across two prior CFPB complaints and multiple U.S. Bank response letters. CFPB XXXX # XXXX ( filed XX/XX/XXXX ) : This initial complaint addressed U.S. Banks refusal to issue any escrow refund whatsoever following loan payoff. At that time, U.S. Banks position was that XXXX XXXX had not been established as Successor in Interest and therefore was not entitled to escrow funds despite U.S. Bank having issued a formal written XXXX confirmation on XX/XX/XXXX, and having addressed its own XX/XX/XXXX settlement letter to XXXX XXXX ( Deceased ) and Successor In Interest XXXX XXXX before accepting {$11000.00} in certified funds from XXXX XXXX in that capacity. CFPB Case # XXXX ( filed XX/XX/XXXX ) : This follow-up complaint identified specific federal regulatory violations including : ( a ) U.S. Banks lack of legal authority under Regulation X to unilaterally revoke a confirmed SII designation ; ( b ) violation of 12 CFR 1024.34 ( b ) requiring return of escrow funds within 20 business days of loan payoff ; ( c ) promissory estoppel based on five years of conduct consistent with confirmed SII status ; and ( d ) a demand for a full written accounting of all escrow funds held. U.S. Banks own admissions across its XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX response letters confirm the following errors : On XX/XX/XXXX, U.S. Bank issued a formal XXXX confirmation letter to XXXX XXXX that U.S. Bank now claims was sent in error On XX/XX/XXXX, a U.S. Bank representative mistakenly discussed payoff information with XXXX XXXX without proper verification because the representative did not realize a death certificate was on file On XX/XX/XXXX, U.S. Bank incorrectly confirmed XXXX XXXX XXXX status by phone during the exact period he was completing the {$11000.00} settlement based on XXXX Banks own settlement letter designating him as SII On XX/XX/XXXX, U.S. Bank issued a settlement letter explicitly addressed to XXXX XXXX ( Deceased ) and Successor In Interest XXXX XXXX, accepted {$11000.00} in certified wired funds on that basis, and only after receiving those funds claimed the XXXX designation was invalid On XX/XX/XXXX, a U.S. Bank representative assisted XXXX XXXX on the account despite acknowledging he was not yet verified as XXXX and not authorized on the account at that time In its XX/XX/XXXX response, U.S. Bank stated that an administrative error does not establish Successor in Interest status and reliance on an administrative error does not substitute for documentation while simultaneously making a business decision to issue an escrow refund check, effectively acknowledging the obligation while disputing the legal basis The escrow refund itself was only issued under regulatory pressure. U.S. Bank refused to return any escrow funds until compelled to respond to the second CFPB complaint. Even then, U.S. Bank issued only a partial refund of {$2200.00} covering the tax component while retaining {$2200.00} in insurance escrow reserves without explanation or accounting. This is now the third time XXXX XXXX has been forced to seek regulatory intervention to compel U.S. Bank to meet basic servicing obligations on this closed account. The pattern is consistent : U.S. Bank withholds funds it is legally obligated to return, provides no accounting, and releases funds only under regulatory pressure and even then, incompletely.

narrative: I am filing a complaint against Capital One regarding their refusal to process a dispute involving a fraudulent transaction. On XX/XX/year>, I was charged {$990.00} by a merchant identified as XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. This transaction was later determined to be part of a fraudulent scheme involving a fake prop firm management service. The merchant represented that they would manage trading accounts and issue payouts after certain performance targets were met. These types of programs typically require 6090 days before a payout is expected. In my case, the expected completion window was between late XXXX and late XX/XX/year>. It was only after this periodwhen no payout was issued and the platform became unresponsivethat I discovered the fraudulent nature of the transaction. Additionally, the merchant has since become completely unreachable and removed all communication channels. I submitted a dispute with Capital One and provided extensive documentation demonstrating : * The service was misrepresented and could not be fulfilled * The merchants own materials confirm that no real trading accounts or funds existed * Multiple independent reports ( including Better Business Bureau XXXX XXXX ) identify this as a scam operation * The merchant is no longer reachable, preventing resolution Despite this, Capital One declined to process my claim, stating that the dispute fell outside of the 60-day billing dispute window. This reasoning is inappropriate for a fraud claim. The fraudulent nature of this transaction was not reasonably discoverable within 60 days because the service itself was structured to delay payout beyond that period. Applying a strict 60-day billing error rule to a case of delayed fraud discovery effectively denies consumer protection in situations where fraud is intentionally concealed over time. I believe Capital Ones handling of this matter is inconsistent with consumer protection principles and unfairly shifts the burden of a sophisticated scam onto the consumer. narrative: I am a XXXX individual residing in California, subsisting on a limited income, and maintaining a consumer deposit account with Wells Fargo Bank , N.A . ( Account XXXX. XXXX ). The circumstances giving rise to this complaint reflect not merely a dispute over fees, but a pattern of institutional conduct that is demonstrably inconsistent with Wells Fargo 's own written contractual disclosures, its regulatory obligations under federal and California law, and its fundamental duty of fair dealing toward a vulnerable consumer who exercised every available remedy in good faith. I. The Assessment of Fees and the Current Negative Account Balance Beginning in XX/XX/XXXX and continuing through XX/XX/XXXX, Wells Fargo assessed a series of fees against my account that, in combination with recurring automatic payments, caused my account balance to deteriorate to its current negative position of {$80.00}. The following complete ledger of all charges, credits, and transactions reflects the full financial impact of this matter : Date Type Description Amount XX/XX/XXXX OVERDRAFT FEE Affirm.com automatic payment {$32.00} - {$35.00} XX/XX/XXXX MONTHLY FEE Monthly service fee Everyday Checking - {$15.00} XX/XX/XXXX OVERDRAFT FEE Affirm.com automatic payment {$47.00} ( posted XX/XX/XXXX ) assessed DURING account conversion to Clear Access Banking - {$35.00} XX/XX/XXXX SUBSCRIPTION XXXX XXXX recurring plan - {$17.00} XX/XX/XXXX SUBSCRIPTION XXXX XXXX recurring charge - {$5.00} XX/XX/XXXX MEMBERSHIP XXXX membership fee - {$1.00} XX/XX/XXXX TRANSACTION Affirm.com payment XXXX - {$47.00} XX/XX/XXXX TRANSACTION Affirm.com payment XXXX - {$32.00} XX/XX/XXXX TRANSACTION Purchase authorized XX/XX/XXXX - {$1.00} XX/XX/XXXX REVERSAL Overdraft fee courtesy reversal + {$35.00} XX/XX/XXXX CREDIT Provisional credit XXXX XXXX claim + {$5.00} XX/XX/XXXX REVERSAL Monthly service fee reversal + {$15.00} TOTAL CHARGED Bank fees + subscriptions + transactions - {$180.00} TOTAL CREDITED All reversals and provisional credits + {$55.00} CURRENT BALANCE Account is currently NEGATIVE as of XX/XX/XXXX - {$80.00} BANK FEES OUTSTANDING Unreversed overdraft fee XX/XX/XXXX primary subject of this complaint - {$35.00} Of the charges reflected above, the fees for which I hold Wells Fargo directly responsible and for which I am seeking relief are the bank-imposed overdraft fees and monthly service fee totaling {$85.00}. Wells Fargo has to date reversed only {$50.00} of that amount, leaving {$35.00} in bank-imposed fees outstanding and unaddressed. The negative account balance of {$80.00} reflects the cumulative impact of those unresolved fees compounded by the recurring automatic payments that continued to post while my account remained in dispute and while Wells Fargo 's representative had falsely informed me that I had no ability to prevent further overdraft charges. II. My Original Request and What I Was Seeking When I first contacted Wells Fargo on XX/XX/XXXX, I was seeking the reversal of two overdraft fees totaling {$70.00} the XX/XX/XXXX fee of {$35.00} and an additional {$35.00} fee. Wells Fargo granted one {$35.00} courtesy reversal on XX/XX/XXXX, reducing my immediate demand to {$35.00}. However, because Wells Fargo failed to resolve my complaint promptly and because a representative affirmatively misrepresented my rights telling me it was not possible to disable overdraft service when it unequivocally was an additional {$35.00} overdraft fee was assessed on XX/XX/XXXX during my active account conversion. My complaint therefore encompasses not only the original unresolved fee but the institutional conduct that caused additional harm to accumulate while my complaint sat unanswered. III. My Initial Escalation Efforts On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted Wells Fargo 's second-level escalation support and spoke with a representative identified as Char. Despite presenting my account history which reflects only three total overdraft occurrences across the entire life of the account, the most recent of which had preceded this complaint by more than one year my request for full reversal of the outstanding fees was categorically denied. Representative XXXX authorized only a single {$35.00} courtesy reversal, which was credited to my account on XX/XX/XXXX, and declined to reverse the remaining balance. That same day, XX/XX/XXXX, I submitted a formal written complaint to Wells Fargo XXXX XXXX XXXX office at XXXX, demanding immediate reversal of all outstanding fees and providing explicit written notice of my intention to escalate this matter to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency should the matter remain unresolved. Wells Fargo 's Board Communications office responded exclusively with automated acknowledgment replies on XX/XX/XXXX and again on XX/XX/XXXX providing no substantive engagement with the merits of my complaint whatsoever. IV. My XXXX Accommodation Request On XX/XX/XXXX, I submitted a follow-up written communication to Wells Fargo XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX which I explicitly declined to proceed with a recorded telephone call and formally requested, on the basis of my XXXX, that all future correspondence be provided to me exclusively in writing. I reiterated this accommodation request in my XX/XX/XXXX written communication as well. Wells Fargo failed entirely to honor this request at any point in the course of this dispute, responding instead with automated replies and an unsolicited telephone call that I was compelled to decline. This failure constitutes not merely a breach of customer service protocol, but a violation of my rights under XXXXitle III of the Americans with Disabilities Act, 42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq., and California 's Unruh Civil Rights Act, Civil Code 51 et seq. V. Wells Fargo 's Formal Acknowledgment and Failure to Resolve On XX/XX/XXXX, Wells Fargo 's Enterprise Complaints Management Office acknowledged my complaint under Case No. XXXX, assigned the matter to XXXX XXXX Representative XXXX XXXX, and expressly committed to providing a substantive written response within XXXX business days of the date of my initial contact. As of the date of this statement XX/XX/XXXX no substantive written resolution has been provided. Wells Fargo has allowed its own self-imposed response deadline to lapse without meaningful action, leaving my complaint unresolved, my rights unaddressed, and my account balance negative. VI. The Misrepresentation of My Consumer Rights During the course of my communications with Wells Fargo regarding the account conversion, I was affirmatively told by a Wells Fargo representative that it was not possible to disable overdraft coverage on my account. According to my own contemporaneous notes of that conversation, when I specifically requested to have overdraft service turned off so that my account would no longer incur overdraft fees, I was categorically informed by the representative that doing so was not an available option. This representation is demonstrably and unequivocally false. Wells Fargo 's own Consumer Account Fee and Information Schedule, its Deposit Account Agreement, and its Important Information About Overdrafts disclosure each of which I have retained expressly state that standard overdraft coverage and Debit Card Overdraft Service are optional services that consumers may remove from their accounts at any time. Moreover, 12 C.F.R. 1005.17, promulgated pursuant to the Electronic Fund Transfer Act, mandates that financial institutions permit consumers to revoke Debit Card Overdraft Service consent at any time without condition. The representative 's categorical denial of a right that is simultaneously guaranteed by federal regulation and by Wells Fargo 's own written contractual disclosures constitutes a deceptive act or practice of the most straightforward variety one that caused me direct and quantifiable financial harm in the form of fees I had every legal right to prevent, and that contributed directly to my account 's current negative balance of {$80.00}. VII. The Financial Hardship This Has Caused I am a XXXX individual on a limited income. The negative account balance of {$80.00} that I am now carrying is not the result of reckless financial management it is the direct consequence of Wells Fargo 's failure to honor its own written disclosures, its failure to timely resolve my formal complaint, its representative 's misrepresentation of my consumer rights, and its assessment of an overdraft fee at the precise moment I was actively converting my account to a fee-free product. Each of these failures compounded upon the last. Had Wells Fargo reversed my fees when I first requested it on XX/XX/XXXX, had its representative accurately informed me of my right to disable overdraft service, or had it simply honored its commitment to respond within ten business days, my account would not be in the position it is in today. The cumulative financial impact of this matter extends beyond the {$35.00} outstanding bank fee. My account 's negative balance has subjected me to potential additional fees, has impaired my ability to conduct ordinary financial transactions, and has caused material hardship to a XXXX individual already operating on a constrained budget. I raise this context not to dramatize my circumstances, but because it is directly relevant to the proportionality of the relief I am requesting and to the regulatory significance of Wells Fargo 's conduct toward this category of consumer. VIII. The Relief I Am Seeking I am not a litigious individual, nor do I seek anything beyond what is rightfully mine under the terms of my own account agreement and applicable federal and state law. I sought to resolve this matter through every internal channel Wells Fargo made available to me. I contacted front-line customer service. I escalated to second-level support. I submitted formal written complaints to the Board Communications office. I cooperated with the Enterprise Complaints Management Office. At every juncture, I was met with either denial, misrepresentation, or silence. I have been left with no recourse other than to invoke the regulatory protections that exist precisely for circumstances such as these. I respectfully request that each regulatory agency to which this statement is submitted compel Wells Fargo Bank , N.A . to provide the following relief : 1. Monetary Relief : Immediate reversal and refund of the outstanding {$35.00} overdraft fee assessed on XX/XX/XXXX, during my active account conversion to Clear Access Banking. 2. Account Confirmation : Written confirmation that my account has been successfully and permanently converted to Clear Access Banking, and that no overdraft coverage, Debit Card Overdraft Service, or overdraft fees of any kind are applicable to my account going forward. XXXX. XXXX Accommodation : Written acknowledgment of Wells Fargo 's failure to honor my XXXX accommodation request and immediate implementation of a written-communication-only protocol for all future correspondence with me. 4. Hardship Recognition : Formal recognition of the financial hardship caused by Wells Fargo 's conduct including the negative account balance of {$80.00} and consideration of any additional relief the agency deems appropriate given the circumstances of this complaint. 5. Systemic Relief : A regulatory directive requiring Wells Fargo to retrain its customer service representatives regarding consumers ' rights under Regulation E to disable Debit Card Overdraft Service at any time, and to review its policies governing the assessment of overdraft fees against customers who are actively converting to fee-free account products.

narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding XXXX handling of a {$5000.00} charge on my account and its subsequent collection of {$4900.00} while the charge was under active dispute, in violation of the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), 15 U.S.C. 1666. On XX/XX/2026, I was induced into what was represented as a {$10.00} charitable donation by individuals in XXXX. During the transaction, my device was briefly handled by third parties, and a {$5000.00} charge was processed without my knowledge or authorization. A verification email was accepted during that time without my control of the device. Upon regaining control, I contacted XXXX within approximately ten minuteswhile the charge was still pendingto report that the amount was not authorized. I immediately took protective actions, including contacting XXXX, reporting the incident to law enforcement, closing my XXXX account, contacting my other financial institutions, and freezing my credit reports. Despite my immediate notice, XXXX allowed the transaction to proceed. XXXX denied my initial fraud claim without providing any substantive explanation, relying solely on the assertion that I had furnished my card. On XX/XX/2026, I submitted a formal written billing dispute under TILA, clearly identifying the charge and explaining that the {$5000.00} amount did not reflect what I authorized. XXXX responded on XX/XX/2026 with a conclusory statement that it was unable to change the outcome and that the transaction was valid, without providing documentation, evidence, or a description of any reasonable investigation. Despite the pending dispute and its failure to comply with TILAs procedural requirements, XXXX proceeded to collect {$4900.00} from my account on XX/XX/2026 ( reflecting the {$5000.00} charge less a prior {$51.00} payment ). This collection occurred without first conducting a reasonable investigation or providing a substantive written explanation, as required by law. Under 15 U.S.C. 1666 ( a ), a creditor may not take any action to collect a disputed amount until these obligations are satisfied. Additionally, this transfer was executed through an automatic payment mechanism, but any prior authorization for such transfers was effectively revoked upon submission of my billing dispute. The debit therefore constitutes an unauthorized transfer of funds under 15 U.S.C. 1693a ( 12 ), as it was initiated without actual authority and after explicit notice of non-authorization. XXXX has failed to : Conduct a reasonable investigation Provide a substantive, evidence-based explanation of its determination Refrain from collecting the disputed amount during the investigation All supporting documentation, including my billing dispute, demand letter, transaction records, communications with XXXX, and evidence of immediate reporting and law enforcement involvement, are attached. I am currently represented by counsel and issued a formal demand letter to XXXX on XX/XX/2026, outlining these violations and requesting resolution. The demand letter is attached. I am requesting that the CFPB investigate XXXX noncompliance with TILA, require correction of the billing error, and ensure reimbursement of the improperly collected {$4900.00}, along with any associated interest or charges.

CFPB Complaint Bank of America Wire Fraud Case Company : Bank of America Issue : Fraud / Unauthorized Transfers/ Scam ( XXXX XXXX ) Complaint : On XX/XX/year>, at approximately XXXXXXXX XXXX, I received a phone call from individuals impersonating Bank of Americas fraud department. The call lasted nearly three hours. During this time, I was manipulated through sophisticated social engineering tactics into initiating three wire transfers totaling {$40000.00}. This incident did not occur in isolation. In the three weeks leading up to this event, I had already been in direct contact with Bank of Americas legitimate fraud department on two separate occasions due to unauthorized debit card activity. A replacement card had been issued, yet fraudulent activity continued even before I received it. During one of those legitimate calls, a Bank of America representative advised that changing my account number might be necessary to secure my funds. The scammers used this exact context to gain my trust. They referenced fraudulent activity, asked security-style questions, and demonstrated knowledge of my account balances. I was then transferred to another individual who instructed me, step-by-step, within my Bank of America mobile app , to move my funds into what I was told were secure accounts while new account numbers were being generated. The caller explained that the account names appearing during the transfers were temporary internal designations and that the system would update within 48 hours. He also stated he would follow up with me to confirm completion. Before each transfer, he read disclosures that sounded consistent with legitimate bank procedures. Based on my recent legitimate interactions with Bank of Americas fraud department, the callers apparent knowledge of my accounts, the use of Bank of Americas own mobile platform, and the urgency tied to ongoing fraud on my account, I reasonably believed I was acting under the direction of Bank of America to protect my funds. Additionally, shortly after completing the transfers, I contacted Bank of America directly to confirm that the transactions had been completed, as I had been instructed that the process would take a couple of days and that I would receive a follow-up call that Friday. During this call, I asked the representative to verify the status of the transfers. The representative appeared alarmed and informed me that Bank of Americas fraud department does not schedule or conduct outbound follow-up calls of that nature. However, I had been told during the earlier interaction that a callback was scheduled, and my call records reflected a scheduled follow-up. That follow-up call did occur on the expected day, but when I answered, there was no response on the line. Later that same day, I contacted Bank of America directly and was informed that no such call had taken place and that the wire transfers were fraudulent. I immediately reported the incident and fully cooperated with the bank. However, Bank of America has since closed my claims after recovering only {$2200.00} total, leaving the vast majority of the {$40000.00} unrecovered. I am disputing this outcome. This was not a voluntary transaction in the traditional sense. I was deceived into acting under the belief that I was securing my funds through Bank of Americas fraud department during an active fraud situation on my account. Requested Resolution : A full reinvestigation of my claim A detailed explanation of how these transactions were determined to be authorized Documentation of any wire recall attempts and recovery efforts Consideration of reimbursement due to the fraudulent inducement and impersonation involved A review of whether adequate safeguards were in place given my recent fraud alerts and account activity I believe this situation warrants further review, as it involves impersonation of the bank, exploitation of an active fraud case, and manipulation through the banks own systems.

Across multiple merchant types ( travel, retail, clothing ), the card never appeared in my XXXX XXXX to even attempt a purchase. Their phone representatives confirmed I had added the card correctly to my wallet. It did appear in the wallet for tap to pay only, not online purchases, as advertised. A second tier Chase representative confirmed that online wallet functionality would not work until the physical card was received, while stating that certain merchants may not be supported, without disputing that it failed for all online merchants. Tier 3 escalation was due to a time-sensitive purchase. No other option to complete the purchase was provided. Chases Digital Wallet Terms confirm that the issuer controls eligibility and can block transactions, meaning this limitation is the responsibility of Chase, not XXXX or XXXX. narrative: In XX/XX/XXXX, I financed an HVAC system through Wells Fargo using a promotional financing plan. I continued making the same payment amount that was sufficient to pay off the first promotion on time. When the first promotion was paid off, Wells Fargos system automatically reduced my payment to the minimum amount without notifying me. This minimum payment was not enough to keep the second promotional purchase on track. As a result, the second promotional purchase fell behind even though I had never missed a payment and had never lowered my payment amount. Wells Fargo did not inform me that the payment schedule needed to change after the promotions were blended, nor did they provide a combined payoff schedule showing the amount required to protect both promotions. I have never missed a promotional payoff in the past and have consistently paid off promotional balances early. My credit score has remained above XXXX for years, and I have always made more than the minimum payment. In XX/XX/XXXX, Wells Fargo began charging interest on the second promotional purchase because the promotional period expired. Wells Fargo also applied retroactive interest, even though the promotional failure occurred solely because the system lowered my payment to the minimum without my knowledge or consent. During this time, I had recently lost my job and was taking care of family responsibilities, but I still continued making consistent payments. Wells Fargos failure to notify me of the payment change made it impossible for me to know the promotional schedule had been disrupted. During the dispute, Wells Fargo asked me to resign XXXX paperwork. The merchant confirmed this should not have been required. I contacted Wells Fargo multiple times to request an explanation, documentation of how payments were allocated, and a breakdown of how interest was calculated. I waited until the end of the week to give them additional time before filing this complaint. Because the interest charges were caused by Wells Fargos system lowering my payment without notice, I am requesting that Wells Fargo reverse the interest and refund the approximately {$1900.00} in overpayment that resulted.

For the past six months, Wells Fargo has willfully misinterpreted federal law to illegally threaten the acceleration of my mortgage loan. Despite submitting multiple Notices of Error ( NOE ), the most recent dated XX/XX/year>, the servicer continues to assert that a protected transfer of the property into an inter-vivos trust triggered a " due-on-sale '' clause. They are demanding that I formally " assume '' the loan as a condition to avoid acceleration, which is a direct violation of the Garn-St Germain Depository Institutions Act of 1982.1. Willful Misinterpretation of " Borrower '' ( 12 CFR 190.2 ( b ) ) Wells Fargo 's refusal to rectify this error stems from a narrowed definition of " Borrower '' that they claim only applies to the original signer of the note. However, federal regulations under 12 CFR 190.2 ( b ) which implements the Garn-St Germain Actexplicitly state : '' Borrower means a person who is a mortgagor, trustor, or other obligor of a real property loan, or any successor or assignee of such person. '' As the confirmed Successor in Interest to the late XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX, I legally " step into the shoes '' of the borrower for the purposes of these protections.2. Violation of Protected Transfer Safe HarborsUnder 12 U.S.C. 1701j-3 ( d ) ( 8 ), a lender is prohibited from exercising a due-on-sale option for a transfer into an inter-vivos trust in which the borrower is and remains a beneficiary.XXXX XXXX ( the Successor/Borrower at the time ) transferred the property to the trust while remaining the primary beneficiary.Upon his passing, I became the Successor in Interest.Because I am a named beneficiary in the trust, the " borrower '' ( myself, by federal definition ) remains a beneficiary.This transfer is federally protected and preempts any conflicting contract language or bank " approval '' requirements.3. Failure to Comply with Regulation XWells Fargo is also in violation of 12 CFR 1024.30 ( d ). The Official Interpretations ( Comment 30 ( d ) -1 ) clarify that a confirmed successor in interest must be considered a borrower for the purposes of mortgage servicing protections, regardless of whether they formally assume the loan obligation under state law. By continuing to demand an assumption under threat of foreclosure, Wells Fargo is engaging in unfair and deceptive servicing practices.Desired ResolutionI request that the CFPB compel Wells Fargo to : Cease all acceleration activities related to the transfer of the property to The XXXX XXXX Trust.Formally acknowledge my status as " Borrower '' pursuant to the definitions in 12 CFR 190.2 ( b ) and 12 CFR 1024.30 ( d ) .Withdraw the demand for loan assumption as a prerequisite for recognizing the federal safe harbor protections of the Garn-St Germain Act.Correct their internal records to show the loan is in good standing and not in violation of the mortgage contract.

I am filing a complaint regarding a fraud claim with Wells Fargo involving {$14000.00}. I was a victim of impersonation fraud. I was contacted by an individual who was posing as Wells Fargo and who had knowledge of my account information. I believed I was speaking with the bank and was instructed to take immediate action to 'protect ' my funds. Following those instructions, I went into a Wells Fargo branch and withdrew cash from my account. Although I did not write a check, the transaction appears to have been processed internally as a withdrawal with a check number. I was then instructed to deposit the funds using what I was told was a secure method. This involved a digital debit card that appeared temporarily on my phone. That digital card is not associated with my account, is not in my name, and is no longer accessible to me. The Funds were deposited and then immediately removed. Wells Fargo has stated that they do not see a digital card associated with my account, which is exactly the issue. The account or card used to receive the funds was not mine and not under my control. This supports that the transaction was part of a fraudulent scheme and not a legitimate or authorized transfer. I reported the fraud and initially filed a claim. That claim was denied. However Wells Fargo then reopened the matter under a new claim number and transferred it to their check fraud department, focusing on the withdrawal itself rather than the fraudulent circumstances that caused it. This reclassification is the core issue. The withdrawal was not a normal or voluntary transaction, it was performed under deception by someone impersonating the bank. The entire sequence of events, including the withdrawal and subsequent deposit, was part of a coordinated fraud. Despite reporting this promptly and fully cooperating, I have not received provisional credit. I was informed that an expedited request has been submitted, but I have already waited the standard XXXX business days typically associated with fraud investigations. I am concerned that my claim is being improperly evaluated as a check or withdrawal issue rather than as impersonation fraud involving unauthorized activity. The focus on how the withdrawal was processed is ignoring the fact that I was deceived into making that transaction. I am requesting that this case be reviewed as fraud involving impersonation and unauthorized activity, and that provisional credit be issued while the investigation continues. I am also requesting a full review of how this claim has been handled, including the denial of the original claim number, and the failure to provide timely provisional credit. This situation has caused significant financial hardship and stress, and I am seeking a fair resolution consistent with consumer protection standards. XXXX XXXX

Capital One Case Number : XXXX Account Type : XXXX XXXX Card Disputed Transaction : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX | {$3700.00} | XX/XX/XXXXXXXX OVERVIEW I am filing this complaint against Capital One , National Association for failure to conduct a reasonable investigation of a billing dispute as required under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ), 15 U.S.C. 1666, and Regulation Z, 12 C.F.R. 1026.13. Capital One closed my dispute case ( No. XXXX ) on XX/XX/XXXX, stating in their closure letter that my response lacks ALL of the previously requested information a statement that is demonstrably false. I submitted a comprehensive seven-exhibit documentation package directly responding to every item Capital One specified. Capital Ones failure to properly consider that evidence and their issuance of a factually inaccurate closure statement constitutes a violation of their obligations under federal law. BACKGROUND : THE UNDERLYING DISPUTE On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX, XXXX charged {$3700.00} to my Capital One XXXX card ( XXXX ending in XXXX ) under Order # XXXX for multi-year XXXX XXXX license renewals and add-on services. This charge occurred while my business ( XXXX, XXXX ) was closed for the holidays from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX. I contacted XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX within their own published 30-day annual plan refund window. XXXX own refund department issued an official written email on XX/XX/XXXX formally approving Out-of-Policy Refund case XXXX. A XXXX support agent confirmed the same day that the refund had been initiated and was processing. No refund was ever issued. I filed a chargeback dispute with Capital One on XX/XX/XXXX. CAPITAL ONES INVESTIGATION FAILURES Failure 1 : Capital One accepted XXXX chargeback response without adequately weighing contradictory evidence already in the file. XXXX submitted a chargeback response to Capital One claiming services were as described and received in good condition. However, XXXX own XXXX Resolve Online questionnaire which Capital One had in their possession as part of the chargeback file contained the following statement : They agreed to a refund but never refunded of XXXX cents and they never issued it. This is a direct admission by XXXX, within their own submission to Capital Ones dispute system, that they agreed to a refund and did not issue it. A reasonable investigation would have identified this internal contradiction within XXXX own filing and weighed it accordingly. Capital One does not appear to have done so. Failure 2 : Capital Ones XX/XX/XXXXXXXX letter requested specific documentation. I provided all of it. Capital Ones XX/XX/XXXXXXXX closure letter falsely states the response lacks ALL of the previously requested information. Capital Ones XX/XX/XXXXXXXX letter requested the following documentation : A copy of the sales invoice or purchase agreement, including evidence of how the service differed from what was received. A statement including the number of times the merchant tried to correct the problem and how the cardholder tried to resolve the dispute. Proof of canceled services or returned merchandise. A refund voucher or other documentation supporting a claim that a credit is due. In response, I submitted a signed, dated formal rebuttal letter with the following seven labeled exhibits directly addressing each requested item : Exhibit A : XXXX invoice showing all charged line items and multi-year terms directly responsive to the invoice/purchase agreement request. Exhibit B : XXXX support chat transcript ( XX/XX/XXXXXXXX ) with timestamped agent statements confirming XXXX, refund initiated, and services removed directly responsive to the merchant correction attempts request. Exhibit C : XXXX account screenshot ( XX/XX/XXXXXXXX ) showing disputed services still active despite confirmed removal directly responsive to the canceled services request. Exhibit D : XXXX own chargeback response submitted to Capital One, including the XXXX questionnaire admission that they agreed to a refund and never issued it. Exhibit E : Official written email from XXXX Refund Request Services department ( XXXX ) dated XX/XX/XXXX at XXXXXXXX XXXX formally confirming partial approval of XXXX directly responsive to the refund voucher / documentation of credit due request. Exhibit F : Chronological Statement of Events a full documented timeline directly responsive to the merchant correction history request. Exhibit G : XXXX emails dated XX/XX/XXXX showing payment cancellation notice and domain removal confirmation, demonstrating XXXX removed paid services without issuing any refund after the chargeback was filed. XXXX : Exhibit E alone an official written email from XXXX own refund department confirming refund approval is precisely the type of refund voucher or other documentation supporting a claim that a credit is due that Capital One specifically requested. Capital Ones statement that my response lacks ALL of the previously requested information is factually inaccurate and suggests this documentation was either not reviewed or not properly considered. Failure 3 : Capital Ones closure statement is factually inaccurate and suggests the submitted documentation was not meaningfully reviewed. Capital Ones XX/XX/XXXXXXXX closure letter states the response lacks ALL of the previously requested information. The word all indicates a total absence of responsive documentation. This is contradicted by the fact that seven labeled exhibits were submitted, each directly mapped to Capital Ones stated documentation requirements, including a written refund approval from the merchants own refund department. Under the FCBA and Regulation Z, Capital One is required to : Acknowledge billing dispute correspondence within 30 days. Conduct a reasonable investigation of the dispute within two billing cycles ( not to exceed 90 days ). Provide the cardholder with a written explanation of its findings if it determines the bill is correct. Not close a dispute based on a merchants response when that same merchants own submitted documentation contains admissions that contradict their defense. A closure letter stating documentation lacks ALL requested items when seven exhibits were submitted including a written merchant refund approval directly matching the requested refund voucher category does not reflect a reasonable investigation. TIMELINE OF CAPITAL ONES HANDLING OF THIS DISPUTE XX/XX/XXXXXXXX : Dispute filed with Capital One for {$3500.00} with supporting documentation. XX/XX/XXXXXXXX : Capital One issues letter stating XXXX claimed services were as described. Case temporarily closed. Capital One requests additional documentation by XX/XX/XXXXXXXX and specifies four categories of supporting evidence needed. XX/XX/XXXXXXXX : Full rebuttal package submitted to Capital One via secure upload, including seven labeled exhibits directly addressing all four requested documentation categories. Package included XXXX own written refund approval email, timestamped chat transcripts, XXXX own XXXX questionnaire admission, active services screenshots, domain removal emails, and full chronological timeline. Disputed amount updated to full {$3700.00} due to XXXX removal of paid domain services without refund. XX/XX/XXXXXXXX : Capital One issues closure letter stating response lacks ALL of the previously requested information and closes the case. No explanation of what specifically was missing or insufficient. No analysis of XXXX own contradictory admissions in the XXXX questionnaire. NOTE ON TIMING : Capital Ones XX/XX/XXXXXXXX deadline had not yet passed when they issued the XX/XX/XXXX closure letter. The documentation was submitted on XX/XX/XXXX eleven days before the deadline Capital One themselves set. Closing the case on XX/XX/XXXX with a finding that documentation was lacking, without providing any specific explanation of what was insufficient, does not reflect a good-faith investigation. LEGAL BASIS FOR THIS COMPLAINT The Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1666 ) and Regulation Z ( 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ) impose specific obligations on credit card issuers when a cardholder submits a billing dispute. These include the obligation to conduct a reasonable investigation before determining whether a disputed charge is valid. Capital Ones failure to meaningfully review the submitted documentation including a written refund approval from the merchants own refund department and the merchants own XXXX admission that they agreed to a refund and never issued it and their issuance of a factually inaccurate closure statement asserting total absence of documentation, raises serious questions about whether Capital One met its FCBA obligations in this matter.

narrative: I am filing this complaint regarding inaccurate and misleading credit reporting by Capital One. I previously disputed this account with the credit reporting agencies. The account is being reported as a closed, charged-off revolving account with a balance of approximately {$3100.00} against a reported credit limit of approximately {$2300.00}. This creates a condition where the account is being reported as significantly over the credit limit, resulting in negative available credit on a closed account. I requested verification of the accuracy and completeness of this reporting. Capital One has not provided competent documentary evidence to support : the full account-level basis for the balance reported a complete itemization of the amount claimed, including principal, interest, fees, and credits the contractual basis for continuing to report a balance and past-due amount after charge-off the accuracy of the reported credit limit in relation to the current balance the full payment history and date of first delinquency Simply stating that the account has been verified is not sufficient to establish that the reporting is accurate and complete. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, information furnished to consumer reporting agencies must be accurate, complete, and not misleading. The current reporting of this account is misleading, including the representation of an over-limit balance on a closed account and the continued reporting of past-due amounts without adequate explanation or documentation. I am requesting that Capital One : 1. Conduct a reasonable investigation of this account 2. Provide competent documentary evidence supporting the reporting 3. Correct any inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading information 4. If the information can not be fully verified, request deletion of the tradeline from all consumer reporting agencies Please respond in writing.

One person tried calling the bank with me on the line to verify me but the wait time took longer than 10 mins so they had to hang up. Mind you, I have been dealing with CO and their incompetency and the inconvenience they have caused me for 10 months now, and they cant wait more than 10 mins?? THIS COMPLAINT REPORTS A NEW, POST-RESPONSE FCBA VIOLATION. IT IS NOT A DUPLICATE This complaint is based entirely on Wells Fargo 's own XX/XX/XXXX, resolution letter ( attached ), which constitutes new evidence of willful noncompliance with the Fair Credit Billing Act that did not exist when prior complaints were filed. 1. THE NEW VIOLATION : FAILURE TO PROVIDE A WRITTEN EXPLANATION WITH DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE Under 15 U.S.C. 1666 ( a ) ( B ) ( ii ), when a creditor receives a billing error notice, it must be within two billing cycles or 90 days, either correct the error or mail the consumer a written explanation setting forth the reasons why it believes the account is not in error, along with documentary evidence of the consumer 's indebtedness. On XX/XX/XXXX, I filed CFPB complaints XXXX and XXXX, constituting formal billing error notices under the FCBA. These complaints identified a specific billing error : a {$5900.00} " ADJUSTMENT-PAYMENTS '' debit posted XX/XX/XXXX, with no corresponding prior credit on my account. I demanded Wells Fargo explain this entry, produce the internal General Ledger extract, and refund all interest accrued on the resulting phantom balance. On XX/XX/XXXX, Wells Fargo responded. Their resolution letter, signed by XXXX XXXX, XXXX Escalations Representative, is now in my possession and attached to this complaint. It fails every element of the FCBA 's required response : The letter never mentions the XX/XX/XXXX, ADJUSTMENT-PAYMENTS entry. The letter never explains what payment the adjustment reversed. The letter never addresses the {$5900.00} phantom debit. The letter produces zero documentary evidence supporting the current balance. The letter never addresses the demand for interest refunds. The letter contains no General Ledger data, no ACH Trace IDs, and no suspense account audit. Instead, Wells Fargo 's letter dedicates its entire substantive content to ( a ) an unrelated Bilt-to-Autograph card conversion, ( b ) a minor closure-status correction on my credit report, and ( c ) confirmation that the missing {$6000.00} was not applied to my auto loan a claim I never made. 2. PROOF OF SYSTEMIC NONCOMPLIANCE : IDENTICAL BOILERPLATE ACROSS 8+ COMPLAINTS Wells Fargo submitted the same response, verbatim, to all eight of my CFPB complaints and my XXXX complaint ( Case # XXXX ), regardless of what each complaint specifically demanded. Complaints requesting interest refunds, General Ledger traces, FCRA corrections, and ACH audit trails all received identical text about a card conversion. This is not a reasonable investigation. This is a template macro. Further evidence of non-investigation : In their response to complaint XXXX, Wells Fargo references a missing payment of " {$60000.00} '', which is a dollar amount that does not appear in any document I filed. This typographical error proves that no competent review of my account ledger was conducted. 3. ARBITRATION DOES NOT SUSPEND FCBA OBLIGATIONS Wells Fargo 's letter states : " We received your arbitration demand. These matters will be addressed through arbitration, and we will not respond to the issues outside of that process. '' The FCBA 's investigation requirements under 15 U.S.C. 1666 are statutory obligations triggered by receipt of a billing error notice. They are not discretionary customer service functions that a creditor can defer by citing a private dispute resolution proceeding. No provision of the Federal Arbitration Act, the Truth in Lending Act, or Regulation Z permits a creditor to suspend its FCBA duties because an arbitration demand has been filed. 4. CONTINUED ADVERSE REPORTING DURING ACTIVE DISPUTE While refusing to investigate my billing error, Wells Fargo verified a {$12000.00} balance to XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. Under 15 U.S.C. 1666a ( a ), a creditor may not report a disputed amount as delinquent during the pendency of a billing error investigation. Wells Fargo has not completed or even commenced the required investigation, yet continues to furnish the disputed balance to consumer reporting agencies. ATTACHMENTS Wells Fargo resolution letter dated XX/XX/XXXX ( XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX Auto loan transaction history enclosed with the letter XXXX-to-Autograph conversion notice dated XX/XX/XXXX REQUESTED RELIEF I request that the CFPB compel Wells Fargo to : 1 . Produce the written explanation with documentary evidence required by 15 U.S.C. 1666 ( a ) ( B ) ( ii ), specifically addressing the XX/XX/XXXX, ADJUSTMENT-PAYMENTS entry. 2. Cease reporting the disputed balance to consumer reporting agencies until the FCBA investigation is complete. 3. Refer this matter to the CFPB Enforcement Division as evidence of systemic FCBA noncompliance through template-based responses that do not address individual billing error notices.

Details : Wells Fargo mistakenly processed a final payment twice on my closed credit card account. This resulted in an overpayment of approximately {$4300.00}. Wells Fargo has confirmed they received the returned check. Despite this, they have repeatedly refused to reissue the refund unless I sign a lost or destroyed check affidavit. The affidavit requires me to falsely state that I lost or destroyed the check, agree to pay stoppayment fees, and accept liability for any claims on the original check. None of these statements are true, and I should not be required to sign a false legal document to receive a refund for the banks own error. I have contacted Wells Fargo multiple times ( at least five separate calls ) and have been told each time that a new check was being issued. Instead, I repeatedly receive the same affidavit form. I have been escalated to the Wells Fargo Executive Office, but the issue remains unresolved. Wells Fargo has held my money for over two months, causing financial stress and hardship. As of today, they claim a check has been reissued, but based on prior experience, I have little confidence this is true. What I am requesting : I am requesting that Wells Fargo immediately reissue my refund check without requiring me to sign a false affidavit, and that they return the funds they have been improperly holding for over two months. I am also requesting that the CFPB review Wells Fargos handling of this matter, including : Sending a refund check to the wrong address Requiring a false affidavit despite having the original check in their possession Repeated delays and misinformation Failure of the Executive Office to resolve the issue Withholding of funds that are rightfully mine
