narrative: In XX/XX/XXXX, I went to my local jeweler to purchase a watch for my husband. At the point of sale, the jeweler told me they could finance the purchase through a Wells Fargo credit card. He did not disclose that the transaction would be placed into a deferredinterest promotion, that there was a special terms expiration date, or that failing to pay the balance in full by a specific date would result in retroactive interest. If these terms had been explained, I would not have agreed to the financing. I relied on the information provided at the time of purchase, and the required disclosures were not made. When I later contacted Wells Fargo about the unexpected interest charge, they showed me a copy of the disclosure. The disclosure was located on page two, in very small print, and was not something I was shown or made aware of at the time of purchase. I also do not recall ever signing up for paperless statements, and I believe my account may have been switched to paperless without my consent. As a result, I did not receive any mailed disclosures or reminders about the promotional terms or expiration date. About 12 months after the purchase, I enrolled the account in autopay to ensure payments were always made on time. Throughout XXXX and XXXX, I consistently paid above the minimum payment, believing I was paying down a normal balance. I had almost paid the account off in full. Then XX/XX/XXXX, over {$3500.00} in deferred interest was added to my account without warning. This was the first time I became aware that the purchase had been placed in a deferredinterest promotion. The charge was extremely unexpected and financially damaging. My family is currently experiencing significant financial hardship, including selling our home to manage debts. Despite this, I have never missed a payment and have always paid responsibly. I contacted Wells Fargo multiple times to request information and clarification. First I called in around XX/XX/XXXX and sent a written denial on XX/XX/XXXX stating only that the promotional period had expired, but they did not address the core issue : the promotional financing terms were never disclosed to me by the merchant, the written disclosure was not reasonably presented, and I may have been switched to paperless without consent, preventing me from receiving required notices. After receiving the denial, I contacted Wells Fargo again on XX/XX/XXXX to clarify the core issues and was told I would receive a response within 10 business days from XX/XX/XXXX. I did not receive any followup or resolution within that timeframe. This further shows that I attempted to resolve the issue directly, but the bank did not address my concerns. I am requesting that the deferred interest be reversed due to the lack of disclosure at the point of sale, the inadequate written disclosure, the possibility that I was switched to paperless without consent, my consistent payment history, my autopay enrollment, and the substantial financial hardship this unexpected charge has caused.

Additionally, Capital One has issued credits for disputed transactions and then later reversed those credits, removing funds from my account again without proper explanation or documentation. This pattern has continued for approximately two years. Capital One has : Failed to properly process and investigate my identity theft claim Improperly treated fraud as isolated disputes rather than a single case Issued credits and then reversed them without justification Refused to provide documentation supporting their decisions Prolonged this matter unreasonably, causing ongoing financial harm These actions appear to violate federal consumer protection requirements for handling fraud and dispute investigations. I am requesting : 1. That this matter be treated as a formal identity theft case, not individual disputes 2. A full investigation of all fraudulent transactions as a single event 3. A complete accounting of all credits issued and later reversed 4. Copies of all documentation used in their determinations 5. Immediate reimbursement of all improperly removed funds 6. narrative: This complaint supersedes CFPB Complaint XXXX XXXXXXXX, which was withdrawn to allow filing of a consolidated complaint reflecting significant new evidence and additional harms discovered after the original filing. BACKGROUND : In XXXX XXXX, my wife and I obtained a second mortgage to consolidate credit card debt. XXXX XXXX XXXX served as the escrow company for the loan. Payoff checks were issued through escrow to all creditors, including separate checks for my Citibank XXXX XXXX and my wife 's Citibank XXXX XXXX. Both cards share the same household address and last name. XXXX XXXX XXXX confirmed in writing that the {$2200.00} payoff check for my account was deposited by Citibank on XX/XX/XXXX. DISPUTE HISTORY : On approximately XX/XX/XXXX, after noticing the balance had not cleared, I called Citibank and opened a dispute. I provided the check number, amount, and deposit date. I specifically asked whether the check could have been misapplied to my wife 's account given the shared address and last name. I was told no. Citibank applied a temporary credit and stated they would email me if additional information was needed. I monitored my Citibank account and email throughout XXXX. No communication was received. I assumed the matter was resolved. On approximately XX/XX/XXXX, I received an email stating a minimum payment was due. Upon logging in, I found the full {$2200.00} balance showing as owed. When I called, Citibank informed me they had mailed ( not emailed, as committed ) a letter requesting a copy of the check, and because I did not respond to a letter I never received in a timeframe I was never informed of, they closed the case. I had the case reopened on XX/XX/XXXX and submitted a copy of the canceled check provided by XXXX. NEW EVIDENCE : I have since obtained my wife 's XX/XX/XXXX Citibank XXXX XXXX statement ( billing period XXXX ). The statement definitively shows the {$2200.00} payoff check intended for my account was posted to her account on XX/XX/XXXX, reflected as " XX/XX/XXXX PAYMENT THANK YOU - {$2200.00}. '' This is the same check Citibank representatives told me, across multiple calls in XXXX, XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX, was not on her account. Citibank held the funds on a related account at the same bank, same household, same address, same last name, for nearly XXXX months. The online dashboard for my wife 's account, when filtered to " Since XX/XX/XXXX, '' displays a transaction labeled " XX/XX/XXXX - REVERSE PYMT POSTED IN ERROR XXXX '' in the amount of + {$2200.00}. This reversal was posted only after I filed my original CFPB complaint. The {$2200.00} has since been correctly applied to my account. HARMS CAUSED : ( 1 ) Credit reporting damage : My FICO score dropped 20 points due to Citibank reporting my account as maxed out during the misapplication period, during active vehicle financing. ( 2 ) Interest charges on a balance Citibank was holding the funds for : Throughout the three-month period Citibank held the {$2200.00} on my wife 's account, I was charged interest on that same {$2200.00} balance on my account. Had Citibank applied the funds correctly, my account would have had a XXXX balance. Under the Fair Credit Billing Act, interest should not be assessed on disputed amounts during an active billing error investigation, and my dispute was open from late XXXX forward. ( 3 ) Reliance damage on my wife 's account : Because the XXXX statement reflected a credit balance of - {$1100.00} on my wife 's account ( a balance that only existed because of the misapplied {$2200.00} ), we reasonably relied on that credit balance in managing household finances. My wife used her card for purchases against what the statement showed as available credit. Citibank 's reversal has now converted those good-faith purchases into {$2200.00} of new debt on her account. ( 4 ) Time cost : I have spent well over 10 hours across phone calls, emails, document gathering, and dispute filings resolving an error Citibank 's own systems could have caught in minutes. ( 5 ) Process failure : Citibank committed to emailing me if additional information was needed, then mailed a letter instead, closed my case without notification, and only acted on the misapplication after I filed with the CFPB. The search required to locate the payment - a query by amount, date, and household identifiers- could have been completed in minutes. I provided the check number, amount, and deposit date as early as XX/XX/XXXX and specifically asked Citibank to check my wife 's account. The misapplication was only identified and reversed after regulatory pressure was applied, suggesting no meaningful investigation occurred until the CFPB was involved.

narrative: I am filing this complaint regarding a fraud loss of approximately {$16000.00} from my account due to a coordinated impersonation scam involving individuals posing as Wells Fargos fraud department. On XX/XX/year>, I received a text message that appeared to be from Wells Fargo fraud services stating that a transaction had been declined and asking me to confirm whether it was authorized. After responding NO, I received a follow-up message stating that a representative would contact me. I was then called by individuals who convincingly impersonated Wells Fargo representatives and informed me that my account had been compromised and that I needed to move my funds to protect them. Relying on what I believed were legitimate instructions from Wells Fargo, I transferred funds over the course of four consecutive days. These transfers included an initial amount of approximately {$2000.00}, followed by multiple transactions of approximately {$4900.00} {$5000.00} per day using XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX to newly added external accounts and cards. These transactions exhibited clear high-risk characteristics, including rapid movement of large sums, addition of new external accounts, and repeated transfers over consecutive days. Despite this pattern, no effective fraud intervention occurred. No meaningful warnings, holds, or verification measures were implemented to stop or question this activity. Notably, one of the third-party platforms involved flagged the activity as suspicious, indicating that the transactions met known fraud criteria. However, Wells Fargo did not take action to prevent the continued loss of funds during this multi-day sequence. Wells Fargo has denied my claim on the basis that the transactions were authorized. This conclusion fails to account for the fact that these transactions were conducted under deception as part of an impersonation fraud and social engineering attack. I did not knowingly authorize transfers to a scammer. I acted under the false belief that I was communicating with Wells Fargo and securing my funds. Additionally, when I initially contacted Wells Fargo to report the fraud, a representative made dismissive remarks suggesting that I should have been aware of this type of scam because it is all over the news. This indicates that Wells Fargo is aware of the prevalence of these scams, yet I received no prior warning, targeted alert, or enhanced protection, and no intervention occurred during a prolonged pattern of high-risk activity. Wells Fargo has acknowledged my escalation and indicated that the matter is currently under review by their XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. I am submitting this complaint to ensure regulatory oversight and a fair, thorough review of the banks handling of this situation. Given the documented impersonation, the multi-day high-risk transaction pattern, and the failure of fraud detection and intervention systems, I am requesting that Wells Fargo : Reopen and fully investigate this claim under the context of impersonation fraud and social engineering. Provide a detailed written explanation of why these transactions were not flagged or prevented. Reimburse the full amount of funds lost as a result of this incident. I am writing to submit a formal complaint regarding the payment functionality associated with my Bank of America credit card account using Bank of America 's online portal, specifically paying a bill. My objective is straightforward, I want to make a consistent fixed monthly payment that is greater than the minimum payment in order to reduce my balance efficiently and minimize interest over time. I have attempted the following methods : XXXX ) Recurring Autopay ( Credit Card Settings ) The system only permits XXXX options : minimum payment, statement balance, or minimum payment plus an additional amount. Because the minimum payment is recalculated each month, selecting minimum plus additional amount results in a consistently declining total payment as the balance decreases. This structure prevents me from maintaining a consistent fixed payment and instead extends the repayment period unless I manually intervene each month. XXXX XXXX Bank of America Bill Pay ( Internal Transfer ) I attempted to set up a recurring fixed payment through Bill Pay. However, the system does not allow me to add my Bank of America credit card as a payee. As a result, I am unable to establish a fixed recurring payment through this channel. XXXX ) Future-Dated Payments I attempted to schedule payments in advance to replicate a recurring payment structure. The system only permits payments tied to the current statement cycle and does not allow scheduling sufficiently far into the future to create a stable, ongoing payment pattern. Taken together, these limitations mean that I can not establish a consistent fixed monthly payment using Bank of Americas internal systems. The only way to achieve this outcome is to manually adjust payments each billing cycle or use an external financial institution, i.e. I can send the money out of Bank of America I want to use to pay my credit card bill, then send it back in again via another Banks bill pay system. I am currently within a promotional 0 % interest period, however this issue will become significantly more impactful once the promotional period ends and interest begins to accrue. More broadly, this limitation is especially relevant for consumers who are attempting to proactively and efficiently manage and reduce revolving debt in a disciplined manner. This concern is heightened by the fact that I have previously been able to set fixed recurring payments on this very same account the prior time I used it for a balance transferXX/XX/XXXX years ago. The removal or restriction of this functionality represents a regression that now creates unnecessary barriers to responsible debt repayment. From a consumer standpoint, the combined effect of these limitations across multiple payment channels, including autopay, bill pay, and payment scheduling, appears to systematically prevent the establishment of a fixed recurring payment amount. The practical outcome of this design is that payments tend to decrease over time unless actively managed, which can prolong repayment periods and increase total interest paid. While I am not alleging that I am unable to make payments, I am concerned that the current system design does not adequately support consumers who are attempting to consistently accelerate their debt repayment using standard automated tools. I respectfully request that this matter be reviewed to determine whether : The removal of fixed recurring payment functionality is appropriate Consumers are being provided with reasonable tools to manage and reduce debt efficiently The current design may have unintended consequences that disadvantage consumers attempting to proactively repay debt while maximizing chargeable interest on outstanding balances Thank you for your time and consideration. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

narrative: Two unauthorized XXXX XXXX ACH debit transactions, each in the amount of {$1200.00}, were processed on my Chase account in XX/XX/year>. I did not authorize either transaction and received no benefit from them. The transactions are as follows : XXXX XXXX {$1200.00} Transaction date : XX/XX/year> WEB ID XXXX XXXX XXXX {$1200.00} Transaction date : XX/XX/year> WEB ID XXXX I timely reported both transactions to Chase as unauthorized. Chase opened claims for both transactions and initially issued provisional credit for both, confirming that Chase recognized both transactions as disputed and under investigation. Chase later reversed the provisional credit for one transaction, leaving one unauthorized ACH debit unreimbursed on my account. Chase asserted that it relied on a letter from the merchant claiming a refund was issued ; however, only one refund actually posted to my Chase account. No refund corresponding to the second transaction ever posted. Despite the fact that one unauthorized transaction remained debited, Chase closed both claims and treated the matter as resolved. Chase has not provided a proper written determination explaining why the remaining transaction was deemed authorized or why the provisional credit was reversed, nor has it provided evidence that the funds were returned to my account. Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) and Regulation E ( 12 C.F.R. Part 1005 ), Chase is required to conduct a goodfaith investigation and correct each unauthorized electronic fund transfer. Provisional credit may not be reversed unless the bank determines, based on evidence, that no error occurred. Closing both claims while one unauthorized transaction remains unreimbursed, and shifting responsibility to the merchant, violates Chases obligations under Regulation E. After I reported both unauthorized transactions, Chase repeatedly required me to complete and resubmit the same Disputed Transaction ( s ) Questionnaire dated XX/XX/year> ( Claim No. XXXX ). Chase instructed me to upload, fax, or mail the form and warned that failure to do so could result in denial or delay of provisional credit. I complied and submitted the completed questionnaire identifying the unauthorized ACH debit dated XX/XX/year>. Despite my compliance and submission of documentary proof, Chase continued to require repeated submissions of the same information, failed to resolve the dispute, and ultimately reversed provisional credit and closed both claims. This occurred even after Chase customer service representatives acknowledged that an error had occurred and confirmed that provisional credit had initially been applied to both unauthorized transactions. Chase also directed me to contact the merchant directly and relied on a merchant letter claiming a refund, even though one unauthorized transaction was never credited back to my Chase account. Requiring repeated documentation, shifting responsibility to the merchant, and closing claims while an unauthorized electronic fund transfer remains unresolved is inconsistent with Chases duties under the EFTA and Regulation E. Chases failure to properly resolve this matter caused significant financial hardship. The unreimbursed unauthorized ACH debit removed my last paycheck, leaving me without funds for basic living expenses. I explicitly informed Chase of this hardship and the urgent financial impact while the dispute was pending. Despite being notified that the unresolved unauthorized transaction had exhausted my available funds, Chase failed to take corrective action, reversed provisional credit, and closed the claims, ignoring the financial harm caused by its failure to comply with its legal obligations.

b'Issue: Verification Deadlock
Context: XXXX XXXX, I was reached out to by an individual (self claimed to be named "XXXX" XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. ) that offered to assist with repayment of my credit card debt. XXXX XXXX Capital One placed my account under restriction and requested a phone call to verify account ownership of the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX account used. I reached out to "XXXX" and he agreed to hop on a call the following day at noon. 

Tuesday XXXX XXXX XXXX, :"XXXX" was unable to hop on call, and refused to provide proof of account ownership. Realizing that this was a scam. 

Since then, I have made multiple calls to Capital One, reaching out to customer service, getting this escalated to a fraud and dispute manager, and then escalating to a specialist team. All came back with one answer: we cannot lift your restriction without proof of account ownership. I was provided with the explanation that for account safety, they need to verify account ownership of the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX account despite understanding that I was a victim of the scam and I am unable to verify the bank account. E.g. "I understand you are not the owner of the account, but to lift the restriction you need to provide proof that you are the owner." This continues to go in the same endless circle. XXXX XXXX XXXX, I paid off my full balance and waited for the payment to post, prior to trying again to call. XXXX XXXX XXXX- I removed the XXXX XXXX XXXX card off my portal and called again, receiving the same response that my restriction cannot be lifted due to account ownership verification. This time, the customer service agent described my exact situation, stating that there was a scam going around where the scammer offers to pay off a credit card with a payment that does not go through and then utilizing other methods to take money out of the credit card. The agent explained that Capital One Fraud protection and the restriction was to "protect" the consumer in the event of this scam. However, my question is- if this scam is KNOWN, why wasn't verification of the bank account requested BEFORE the payment? or AT payment? 
Regardless, I would like to understand how Capital One expects its consumers to be able to resolve this issue, when the only resolution is to prove ownership of an account that both I, and Capital One agents, acknowledge is not mine, and impossible. The resolution of scenarios similar to mine is, quite literally, impossible. 

Under this restriction, I am unable to use the card, which I am completely fine with. However, my XXXX miles, worth over $XXXX are unable to be used due to this restriction. I am unable to use these points, transfer these points, or apply to my credit card balance. I then asked about a scenario: If by accident, I "overpaid" my balance, resulting in a negative balance, would I be able to get my overpayment back given that my account is restricted? The manager on the other side of the call then proceeded to read that a refund would not be possible due to the restriction. Luckily, I did not overpay. But if I had overpaid, Capital one would be sitting with my money, and wouldn't refund me because of this restriction. The manager then proceeded to explain that they would transfer the case to multiple different departments to get the money back to me, if I had overpaid. My question regarding this is then : How is account activity allowed in this scenario? Why can't the same methods to allow activity be applied to rewards points usage? 

I have also reached out to the following emails, with no response: XXXX

If the scam and the consequences of the scam are KNOWN to Capital One, why is the victim of the scam being punished and required to provide impossible proof of ownership of an account that both the victim and Capital One is aware don't belong to the victim, and therefore making the request impossible? the following risks have been resolved as well: Connected Bank accounts are verified, the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX bank account used in this fraud situation has been REMOVED, and the remaining balance on the card paid off in full, balance is now $XXXX. Does Capital One just not want to allow the consumer to use their rewards points?'

narrative: Complaint Against : U.S. Bank Mortgage Assistance / Loss Mitigation Department I am filing this complaint regarding serious servicing failures, unreasonable delays, and potential violations of federal mortgage servicing regulations by U.S. Bank, which are placing my home at immediate risk of foreclosure despite submission of a complete loss mitigation application. Background I initially applied for mortgage assistance after experiencing a temporary financial hardship due to a business setback. At that time, I was denied. However, my financial condition has since materially improved, and I am now able to resume ongoing mortgage payments. The only remaining issue is approximately {$30000.00} in arrears, which I can not pay in a lump sum but am seeking to resolve through an assistance program. Following the initial denial, I was incorrectly instructed by multiple U.S. Bank representatives to file an appeal, which does not consider updated financial information. This guidance was misleading and caused unnecessary delay. I subsequently submitted a new application with updated financials reflecting my improved income and ability to sustain payments. Complete Application Submission More than 14 days ago, I submitted a complete loss mitigation application, including : Updated financial documentation Business income verification Bank statements Profit and loss statements Hardship explanation Accountant documentation Proof of IRS-filed extension for 2025 business tax returns I also submitted additional supporting documentation beyond what was required to ensure completeness. Servicing Failures and Regulatory Concerns Despite having a complete application on file, U.S. Bank has : Failed to properly review the application in a timely manner Failed to provide consistent and accurate information Repeatedly requested non-existent 2025 tax returns, despite : Submission of accountant certification of extension Submission of IRS extension documentation Multiple confirmations from U.S. Bank employees that these documents were received and sufficient Underwriting has falsely claimed these documents were not received, despite my submitting them at least four separate times and receiving confirmation of receipt. I have made over 15 follow-up contacts within a 14-day period to ensure my application is processed and to prevent foreclosure. Potential Violations of Federal Law ( RESPA / Regulation X ) U.S. Banks actions raise serious concerns under 12 CFR 1024.41 ( Regulation X Loss Mitigation Procedures ), including but not limited to : Failure to exercise reasonable diligence in obtaining documents and reviewing a complete loss mitigation application ( 1024.41 ( b ) ( 1 ) ) Failure to promptly evaluate a complete application ( 1024.41 ( c ) ( 1 ) ) Failure to provide accurate and consistent information regarding required documents Improper delay tactics that may be effectively steering the account toward foreclosure Additionally, if my application is in fact complete, U.S. Bank may be failing to comply with dual tracking protections under 1024.41 ( f ) and ( g ), which prohibit moving forward with foreclosure while a complete loss mitigation application is under review. U.S. Bank has explicitly stated that I am not protected from foreclosure during this review, which is deeply concerning and potentially inconsistent with federal servicing requirements if my file is complete. Impact These failures are causing : Severe financial harm Risk of imminent foreclosure Unnecessary stress and instability despite my good-faith efforts to resolve the situation At this point, U.S. Banks conduct appears to reflect systemic breakdown in loss mitigation handling and possible non-compliance with federal servicing regulations. Requested Resolution I am requesting that U.S. Bank : Immediately confirm that my application is complete under 12 CFR 1024.41 Cease requests for non-existent 2025 tax returns Promptly evaluate and issue a decision on my application without further delay Immediately halt any foreclosure activity while a complete application is under review Provide a written explanation of delays and contradictory communications This matter is urgent. I am requesting immediate regulatory review and intervention to prevent wrongful foreclosure and ensure compliance with federal law.

On XX/XX/2026, I initiated a wire transfer in the amount of {$16000.00} at my bank branch. At the time of the transaction, I provided complete and accurate wire instructions. These instructions clearly identified XXXX XXXX as the final beneficiary, with XXXX XXXX intended solely as an intermediary bank for routing purposes. The wire was being sent to my own account at XXXX XXXX for the purpose of paying off an existing loan. Despite providing full and correct instructions, the wire was processed incorrectly by the banks teller. Specifically, the required beneficiary information for XXXX XXXX was not properly included in the transmitted wire. As a direct result of this error, the funds were not credited to the intended XXXX account and are currently unaccounted for, with indications that they are held at or within XXXX XXXX. I did not request or rely on the bank to determine or locate wiring instructions. I personally supplied all necessary and correct details. During the transaction, I was instructed only to verify specific numbers presented to me on the screen. I confirmed that only those numbers matched my written instructions exactly. I was not asked to verify the completeness of the wire, nor was I shown the full set of transmitted details. The process did not provide visibility into whether certain information was manually entered, automatically populated, or omitted, and it is not the customers responsibility to identify missing internal fields that were never presented for review. The bank has provided no documentation or proof demonstrating that the wire was processed in accordance with the instructions I provided. They have failed to show that the full beneficiary details for XXXX XXXX were included in the outgoing wire. Any omission or deviation occurred during the banks internal processing and is solely attributable to the bank. As a result of this error : The {$16000.00} has not reached my account at XXXX XXXX The funds have been missing for over 18 days I have incurred ongoing interest charges on the loan the wire was intended to pay off I have experienced significant financial disruption and hardship While the bank has stated that it is attempting to recover the funds, it has failed to provide a clear timeline for resolution and has not clarified what will occur if the funds can not be recovered. I remain in a position of financial uncertainty due entirely to the banks error. This situation reflects a clear failure in the banks handling and execution of a consumer financial transaction and raises serious concerns under UDAAP standards. I am disputing these entries for the following reasons : 1. * * Unverifiable Payment History * * The reported payment history contains inconsistencies, missing months ( including N/R entries ), and irregular reporting patterns. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ), you are required to conduct a reasonable investigation. Reporting incomplete data renders the entire tradeline unverifiable and legally noncompliant. 2. * * Inaccurate and Misleading Account Status * * These accounts are being reported as paid yet continue to reflect severe delinquency and/or charge-off history. This creates a misleading impression of current creditworthiness and violates 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), which requires maximum possible accuracy. 3. * * Failure to Maintain Complete and Accurate Records * * Under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), furnishers are prohibited from reporting information that is incomplete or inaccurate. Full reinvestigation documentation, including : * Method of verification * Complete payment history records used * Identification of the party who verified the information If you are unable to produce complete, verifiable, and compliant documentation, you are required by law to delete these items immediately. -- - Failure to comply with this request will result in escalation, including formal complaints to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) and potential legal action for willful noncompliance under 15 U.S.C. 1681n and 1681o. No fraud alerts or suspicious activity notifications were sent by Chase despite the unusual nature, amount, and foreign location of these transactions. Additionally, there have been multiple inconsistencies in the explanations provided by Chase regarding how the transactions were conducted : * I was initially told all transactions were made using a digital wallet * I was later informed that only one transaction involved a digital wallet, while the others were debit card transactions * I was told by one representative that the transactions were PIN-based * A different representative stated the transactions were completed using tap-to-pay and chip insert methods, without PIN entry These conflicting explanations raise serious concerns about the accuracy and reliability of Chases investigation and denial. Despite this, Chase denied my claim without issuing a provisional credit and has maintained that the transactions were authorized. Based on the lack of possession of my card and phone, the absence of fraud alerts, and the inconsistent and contradictory information provided by Chase, I believe this claim was not properly investigated. GROUND 1 CAPITAL ONE CONFESSED IN WRITING TO REPORTING A BALANCE IT NO LONGER OWNS TWICE
This is not an allegation. This is a confession in Capital One's own words, under Capital One's own case numbers.
Capital One's XXXX XXXX XXXX Response (Case No. XXXX Exhibit A):

These certifications came ten and eleven months after the account was transferred. Capital One did not make an error. Under Metro 2 Credit Reporting Standards, upon transfer of a charged-off account, the original creditor must report a $0.00 balance and update the account status to "DA Transferred/Sold." Under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2(a)(1)(A), a furnisher is prohibited from reporting information it knows or has reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate. narrative: On XX/XX/year>, I initiated a wire transfer in the amount of {$29000.00} from my Wells Fargo account to a company I believed to be a legitimate business selling a vehicle online. I am filing this complaint because I believe Wells Fargo failed to adequately protect me as a consumer in the following ways : XXXX. Failure to Provide Adequate Warning : At the time I initiated the wire transfer, I was not clearly or meaningfully informed that wire transfers are equivalent to cash and are irreversible once sent. Given the size and unusual nature of this transaction, I believe the bank had a responsibility to ensure I understood the risks. 1. Failure to Identify or Act on Red Flags : This was a large, one-time wire transfer to a new recipient, which is not typical activity for my account. Wells Fargo did not question or flag this transaction, nor did they implement any additional verification or fraud prevention measures. 1. Lack of Consumer Protection and Recourse : I reasonably believed that my bank would provide some level of protection against fraud, especially for a transaction of this magnitude. I was not informed that I would bear the full loss in the event of fraud. 1. Inadequate Response After Fraud Was Reported : While a recall attempt was made, Wells Fargo has not provided sufficient detail regarding their efforts, nor have they demonstrated that all possible steps were taken to recover the funds or investigate the receiving institution. Desired Resolution : I am requesting that Wells Fargo : * Conduct a full reinvestigation of this transaction and their handling of the situation * Provide documentation of all fraud prevention measures in place at the time of the transaction * Provide records of the wire transfer, recall attempt, and communications with the receiving bank * Reimburse me for the loss, or provide a detailed explanation of why reimbursement is not warranted under applicable consumer protection standards

The setoff was applied toward a consent judgment that was entered against my spouse alone ( Wells Fargo Bank , N.A . v. [ debtor ], XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX ). I am not a party to that judgment. I was not served, did not consent, and have no liability under it. On XX/XX/XXXX, my {$8300.00} annual performance bonus from my employer was deposited into my checking account, and {$8300.00} of that bonus was transferred from my checking account into the joint savings account on the same day. This is a documented yearly bonus paid to all employees of my company based on individual and company performance. Between the bonus deposit on XX/XX/XXXX and the Wells Fargo setoff on XX/XX/XXXX, the closing balance of the joint savings account never dropped below {$8500.00}. At no point during that period did the balance fall below the {$7000.00} amount Wells Fargo seized. Under the lowest intermediate balance rule, the entirety of the funds Wells Fargo seized is traceable to my bonus deposit. XXXX law strictly limits a bank 's right of setoff against a joint account to the debtor 's beneficial interest as determined by net contribution. Under XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. XXXX, a joint account " belongs to the parties in proportion to the net contributions by each to the account. '' Under XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. XXXX, a financial institution 's right of setoff against a multiple-party account is limited to the debtor 's beneficial interest. The XXXX Supreme Court held in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX ( XXXX ), that " a bank has no right of setoff against the beneficial interest contributed by a nondebtor depositor. '' The funds Wells Fargo seized were my net contribution as a non-debtor depositor. Wells Fargo had no right under XXXX law to set off against those funds. The setoff violated XXXX statutory law and binding precedent. A research case has been opened with Wells Fargo customer service. A formal written demand for return of the {$7000.00} was sent on XX/XX/XXXX to the law firm representing Wells Fargo as counsel of record on the underlying judgment, requesting return within XXXX days. As of this filing, Wells Fargo has not responded substantively or returned any of the seized funds. The savings account is also used to pay our household mortgage, making this an essential household account, not a savings reserve.

Follow-Up Complaint ( Challenge to Post-Hoc Fraud Justification ) I am submitting this follow-up in response to Capital Ones latest correspondence regarding my account closure and the forced redemption of my XXXX rewards miles. Capital Ones most recent response introduces, for the first time, an allegation of first party fraud as justification for denying my rights under New York General Business Law 520-e. This claim is inconsistent with the reasons originally provided to me at the time of account closure and appears to be a post-hoc justification. At the time my account was closed on XX/XX/2026, Capital One explicitly stated that : The closure was based on business concerns It was due to activity inconsistent with typical account usage It did not relate to [ my ] credit worthiness At no point in any contemporaneous communication was fraud alleged. Now, in response to my complaint, Capital One is asserting first party fraud based solely on the claim that documentation I provided validated only 14.66 % of the income stated on my application. This assertion is both incomplete and misleading. 1. Inadequate and Unreasonable Verification Process Capital One requested only personal bank statements, despite the fact that : My income is derived from multiple businesses and sources A substantial portion of verifiable income flows through business accounts between me and my spouse. Limiting verification to personal bank statements alone does not provide a complete or accurate picture of income. More importantly, I was never given the opportunity to provide additional documentation ( such as business financials, K-1s, tax returns, or other supporting records ) that would have fully substantiated my income. A failure to verify income based on incomplete documentation is not fraud. 2. No Evidence of Intentional Misrepresentation Capital One has not identified : Any specific statement that was knowingly false Any evidence of intentional misrepresentation Any conduct tied to misuse of the credit card or rewards program A discrepancy between documentation and reported incomeespecially where only partial documentation was requesteddoes not meet the standard of fraud. 3. Improper Reliance on 520-e ( 4 ) The statutory exception cited by Capital One applies only in cases of fraud or misuse by the holder with respect to the credit card account or rewards program. Capital One has not demonstrated : That any alleged issue was intentional That it related to use of the account or rewards program That it involved any misuse of rewards accumulation or redemption An underwriting or documentation dispute is not equivalent to fraud with respect to the account or rewards program. 4. Post-Hoc Justification to Avoid Statutory Obligations The timing and inconsistency of Capital Ones explanations raise serious concerns. Fraud was never mentioned at the time of closure and is only being raised now, after I asserted my rights under New York law. This suggests that the fraud designation is being used retroactively to avoid compliance with the 90-day redemption requirement. 5. Denial of Redemption Rights and Forced Devaluation Regardless of the above, Capital One : Closed my account on XX/XX/2026 Redeemed my XXXX miles by XX/XX/2026 Forced a conversion to a check at approximately XXXX XXXX per mile Provided no opportunity to redeem, transfer, or use the rewards as permitted under the program This deprived me of the ability to realize the true value of my accumulated rewards.

narrative: I made {$13000.00} across XXXX payments between XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX on my BoA Travel Credit Card when the minimum payment for the month was {$440.00}. I have XXXX sub-balances on this card and their balances as of the statement ending XX/XX/XXXX were $ XXXX 20.49 % APR and {$11000.00} @ 0 % APR until XX/XX/XXXX. I have made no new purchases on the card since this statement was issued. The way the terms of the card work, the minimum payment gets applied to the 0 % balance and anything beyond that should be applied to highest interest balance. After making {$2500.00} in payments on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, I called in on XX/XX/XXXX to check how much of those payments had been applied to which balance and asked what I needed to pay in order to fully clear my interest-bearing balance. That is when I found out that more than {$440.00} of my {$2500.00} payments had been allocated to my 0 % interest balance, hundred of dollars more than should have been, as the interest-bearing balance was not reduced by the correct amount after the payment. I spent almost 2 hours on the phone and was told that a report was being made so a case manager could be assigned and that they would be waiving 3 months of interest on the account as a result of the issues. I also asked them what I needed to pay in order to fully clear the interest-bearing balance and was told {$10000.00}. I then made this payment over the phone with a supervisor who put a note on the account that this was meant to take care of the interest-bearing balance in full. I noted and complained again that in the end I would be making {$13000.00} in payments when I should have only been charged the {$440.00} minimum plus the {$12000.00} and any interest accrued on top. Assuming that we are talking about half a month here, at a 20.49 % APR we are talking about approximately {$100.00} in interest on top. This means that I should have only had to pay {$12000.00} + {$100.00} + {$440.00} = {$12000.00} to clear this balance this month. I have already paid Bank of America {$340.00} beyond what I should have and they incorrectly applied this to the 0 % balance instead of the interest bearing balance. Now, to make matters worse, after paying the {$10000.00}, I called again today to verify that everything went through and have now been told that I still have a {$360.00} interest-bearing balance on my account and they have once again over-applied that {$10000.00} payment towards the 0 % balance. In addition, I received an e-mail back from the Bank saying they would be denying the 3 months of interest credit that was offered yesterday by the previous agent I spoke with. I have now been on the phone with a different supervisor asking them why I am having the same problems twice on the same account with payments being misapplied and reminded them that this left me, the customer, paying more interest on a higher balance as a result. Despite many efforts to get me to think that it all made sense, I ran through the numbers with the supervisor I spoke with and she was eventually coming up with the same figures I was too and agreed it didn't make sense. She tried to get the previously offered credits approved and was denied and then when she went to the Balance Transfer team to talk about this, they claimed everything looked fine, provided no explanation, and refused to come the phone after I asked to speak with them and explain themselves. After saying I was considering closing my account, I was told they would come to the line, was then put on an additional 20+ minute hold, and then got sent back to an entry level agent who knew nothing about the case after 2+ hours on the phone. I went through things with the new agent only to see they misallocated my payment a third time in XXXX as well, only this time less than the minimum payment was applied to the 0 % balance and it was overallocated to the interest-bearing portion. The agent then kept overtalking me instead of explaining himself and after 2.5 hours on the phone, realizing it was going nowhere, I had to disconnect the call and write this complaint. So, essentially, the bank knows it has misallocated XXXX payments, has been passing me around like a football wasting 4+ hours of my time, is making extra interest on the misallocation, has been paid {$340.00} ( likely a little bit more when considering how I calculated the interest ) more than they should have been to clear the full balance already, and is still demanding {$360.00} on top. Even if I were to pay the {$360.00}, based on my experience, they would misallocate this too and I'd end up paying a little bit more. This seems like a trap to confuse and take advantage of the customer and in the end BoA will be attempting to extract an extra ~ $ XXXX beyond what is due from me in order to clear the interest bearing-balance out. The total amount paid if I pay the {$360.00} on top would be {$13000.00} when, again, the amount to clear it all should have been no more than {$12000.00}. This does not account for extra interest that accrues on the larger interest-bearing balance that was left after the first misallocation or any interest that is now accruing on the {$360.00} remaining owed due to the second misallocation ( or any potential third misallocation if the {$360.00} gets paid and doesn't get allocated correctly for a third time ). I am being overcharged on interest as a result of this. The Bank is refusing to correct the misallocation or provide an explanation other than to say " that happened, yes ''. So far I have had my time wasted, my money wasted, been taken advantage of by one of America 's largest banks, and they refuse to take the time to either deal with it or even honor the compensation they said they would provide. This is shameful and wrong.

XXXX position appears to rely heavily on the fact that authentication codes and login information were validated. But if my device, phone, online access, or authentication process was compromised, then the presence of authentication does not resolve whether the transfers were authorized by me. narrative: Subject : Complaint Inconsistent Fraud Determinations, Failure to Properly Process Reports, and Lack of Verifiable Communication I am submitting this complaint regarding the handling of disputed charges by Capital One. The charges at issue occurred between XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX and involve repeated transactions associated with a single digital platform. These transactions formed a pattern of recurring amounts, high-frequency activity, and ultimately appeared across multiple accounts. Due to their similarity to legitimate activity, the pattern was not immediately identifiable as unauthorized. Once the pattern became apparent in approximately XXXX XXXX, I made multiple attempts to report the issue. In XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted Capital One by phone to report the suspected fraudulent activity. During that call, I was informed that each transaction would need to be entered individually. The representative expressed resistance due to the number of transactions and discouraged proceeding. As a result, the report was not completed. Between XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, I attempted to report the issue independently via email. I made multiple efforts to identify and use an appropriate fraud reporting contact but was unable to locate or successfully use a functional email channel. In XX/XX/XXXX, I again contacted Capital One by phone. During this call, the representative again expressed reluctance to process the volume of transactions and suggested that I simply pay the charges rather than proceed with reporting them. I insisted that the report be taken. The representative began entering the disputed transactions and confirmed that one account had been successfully submitted. While processing the second account, the call was disconnected. I did not receive a return call, and the report was not completed. During that XXXX interaction, I was led to believe that at least one set of disputed transactions had been successfully submitted and would be reviewed. Based on that representation, I reasonably expected to receive follow-up communication or written correspondence confirming the status or outcome of the investigation. I allowed a reasonable period of time for such communication to occur. However, I did not receive any phone call, email, or written notice regarding the status or resolution of the reported activity. After receiving no communication or confirmation, I submitted a formal written dispute on XX/XX/XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, I was contacted by phone by a Capital One representative. During that call, I was told that I was being held responsible for the charges because I had failed to report the issue within XXXX days of occurrence. I was also told that prior correspondence had been sent to me regarding the investigation and outcome. I advised the representative that I had not received any such communications. Following that call, I received multiple letters dated XX/XX/XXXX stating that my claims were denied due to insufficient evidence of fraud, with additional references to charges older than XXXX days not being eligible for temporary credit. Subsequently, I received additional documentation dated XX/XX/XXXX, which appears to correspond to the original fraud report initiated during my XX/XX/XXXX phone call. These documents confirm that Capital One opened a fraud investigation at that time and acknowledged the disputed charges. This directly contradicts the later position communicated to me on XX/XX/XXXX, that I failed to report the issue within the required timeframe. The existence of a documented investigation in XXXX demonstrates that the issue was, in fact, reported and processed, and that any failure in follow-through or communication occurred within Capital Ones internal handling of the casenot due to inaction on my part. Additionally, the XX/XX/XXXX documentation reflects multiple and inconsistent positions, including statements that I would not be held responsible for unauthorized charges, while other communications from the same timeframe state that there was insufficient evidence of fraud and that the transactions were valid. These conflicting determinations demonstrate a lack of a clear, consistent, and well-documented investigative conclusion. Although I was informed that prior correspondence had been sent by both mail and email, I did not receive any such communications at the time they were allegedly issued. All documentation in my possession was received only recently, and multiple letters are identically dated XX/XX/XXXX, with no verifiable evidence of earlier delivery. I was also informed that my account was enrolled in paperless delivery. I have reviewed my email records, which contain extensive message history dating back through XXXX. This is a new complaint based on new violations that occurred after my first two complaints. U.S. Banks XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX responses introduce new servicing failures, new contradictions, and new evidence of noncompliance with federal mortgage servicing regulations, including 12 CFR 1024.35, 12 CFR 1024.36, and 12 CFR 1024.41. ( 1 ) Failure to provide required information and failure to correct inaccurate information 12 CFR 1024.35 ( b ) ( 1 ), ( b ) ( 2 ), ( b ) ( 8 ). U.S. Banks XX/XX/XXXX letter admits : We apologize if you did not receive this correspondence. This contradicts their XX/XX/XXXX claim that all servicing timelines were met and that the XX/XX/XXXX packet was mailed.A servicer can not claim compliance while simultaneously admitting nondelivery of required claim information. This is a new violation of the requirement to provide accurate information and correct prior errors. ( 2 ) Failure to respond to prior complaints with a complete and accurate answer 12 CFR 1024.35 ( e ). U.S. Bank reattached prior letters instead of addressing the issues raised.A servicer must conduct a reasonable investigation and provide a substantive written response. Resending old letters is not a response and violates the errorresolution requirements. ( 3 ) Failure to obtain documents from the insurer despite having authority 12 CFR 1024.41 ( c ) ( 2 ) ( i ). The bank continues to blame the insurer for missing documents but refuses to explain why its own internal claim ( opened XX/XX/XXXX for {$40000.00} ) has not progressed.Servicers must exercise reasonable diligence to obtain documents from third parties. U.S. Bank has not done so. This is a new violation. ( 4 ) Contradictory statements regarding call handling and servicing accuracy 12 CFR 1024.38 ( b ) ( 1 ) ( i ). The XX/XX/XXXX letter admits calls on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX were not handled according to our standards and that inaccurate information was provided.The XX/XX/XXXX letter then claims all calls from XX/XX/year> were handled correctly and uses this to imply overall compliance.These contradictions were not addressed and constitute new misrepresentations in the XXXX responses. ( 5 ) Failure to provide a single, consistent point of contact 12 CFR 1024.40 ( a ). The XX/XX/XXXX Relationship Manager letter appears to be a retroactive attempt to cure a compliance failure.A servicer must assign a relationship manager when the borrower first requests assistance, not months later after regulatory complaints. ( 6 ) Failure to advance the loss draft process violation of HUD servicing requirements incorporated into FHA loans. U.S. Bank has not explained why the loss draft process has not advanced despite : an internal claim opened XX/XX/XXXX authority to obtain insurer documents no action taken to move the claim forward FHA servicers must protect the property and advance the claim process. U.S. Banks XXXX letters show new failures to comply. ( 7 ) Failure to provide a complete response to the CFPB 12 CFR 1024.35 ( e ) ( 1 ) ( i ) ( B ). A servicer must provide a response that is complete and accurate.The XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX letters do not address the contradictions, delays, or missing documents. They do not answer the issues raised in the first two complaints.I am requesting a new investigation into these new violations, as U.S. Bank has not provided a complete, accurate, or compliant response to the prior complaints.

narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding unauthorized credit card accounts opened in my name without my knowledge or consent and the lenders failure to meet its obligations under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). While I was married, my XXXX XXXX opened one or more credit card accounts in my name without my authorization. I did not apply for these accounts, did not use them, and was unaware they existed until after she stopped making payments and I began receiving late and delinquency notices. I reported this matter to Chase as fraud and identity theft and formally disputed the accounts. Chase rejected my claim, stating that because prior payments were made from a joint bank account, the accounts are not considered fraudulent. This rationale is incorrect and inconsistent with FCRA standards. Payment from a joint account does not establish that I authorized the opening of credit in my name or had knowledge the accounts existed. Under the FCRA, furnishers are required to conduct a reasonable investigation when a consumer disputes the accuracy or authorization of an account. I specifically requested that Chase review objective application and transaction data, including IP addresses and other identifying information associated with the credit applications and account activity, to determine whether I was involved. Chase has not provided evidence that I applied for or authorized these accounts, nor have they demonstrated that a reasonable investigation was performed. Despite my dispute, negative information related to these unauthorized accounts is being reported and/or threatened to be reported to the credit bureaus. As a result, I am being held responsible for debt I did not knowingly incur, causing ongoing credit and financial harm. I am requesting CFPB intervention to ensure compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act, including : A proper and documented reinvestigation of the disputed accounts Removal of unauthorized accounts from my responsibility Correction and suppression of any inaccurate or adverse credit reporting Confirmation that lack of authorization to open credit can not be overridden solely by payment source The lenders current position improperly conflates access to shared funds with consent to open credit, which does not meet FCRA requirements for accuracy or reasonable investigation.

narrative: I am filing this complaint as a follow-up to a previously closed complaint [ XXXX ] against Wells Fargo Bank. I am refiling because Wells Fargo 's official CFPB response contained a material factual error that invalidates their denial, and because my original filing was brief and unaccompanied by documentation. I am now providing the full picture with supporting attachments. I. WHAT HAPPENED THE FRAUD In XX/XX/XXXX, I was targeted by a sophisticated multi-layered employment fraud scheme. I was referred by a known contact to " XXXX XXXX, '' presented as a legitimate employer ( XXXX XXXX ) seeking an executive assistant immediately. I submitted my resume, completed a job application, and communicated via email and text throughout what appeared to be a standard professional hiring process. XXXX XXXX informed me he would be sending two cashier 's checks digitally to fund my home office setup, representing this as standard onboarding practice. I deposited both checks through Wells Fargo 's mobile deposit application. Wells Fargo accepted both deposits and made the funds available with no hold, no flag, and no warning. I relied on my bank 's acceptance of those deposits as confirmation of their legitimacy a reasonable expectation for any consumer. Based on the available funds and direct instructions from my purported employer, I made three payments to " XXXX XXXX, '' represented as a company-partnered supplier : XX/XX/XXXX {$400.00} via XXXX XX/XX/XXXX {$430.00} via XXXX XXXX ( debit card ) XX/XX/XXXX {$400.00} via XXXX XXXX ( debit card ) Total : {$1200.00} These were not discretionary purchases. They were payments made under explicit fraudulent instruction, funded entirely by deposits Wells Fargo had accepted and cleared. Two days after the deposits, Wells Fargo closed my checking account of nearly 30 years citing " altered checks '' with no prior warning, no hold notice, and no guidance. At that point, {$1200.00} in payments had already been made because Wells Fargo had made those funds available without detection. The supplies I paid for were never delivered. All parties XXXX XXXX, the referring contact, and XXXX XXXX ceased all communication. Every identity involved was fabricated. II. WELLS FARGO 'S ROLE IN THIS LOSS Wells Fargo 's mobile deposit system accepted and cleared two altered cashier 's checks without detection and made those funds available to me. Had Wells Fargo 's system flagged or placed an extended hold on those instruments, I would not have made a single payment. The bank 's failure to detect altered instruments at the point of deposit was a direct and proximate contributing cause of my total financial loss. This is not addressed anywhere in Wells Fargo 's response. III. THE DISPUTE PROCESS FAILED ME I filed a dispute on XX/XX/XXXX. The claim was opened and closed the same calendar day with no outreach to me, no review of my submitted documentation, and no written denial explanation. On XX/XX/XXXX, I spent the majority of the day on calls with at least eight Wells Fargo representatives, each of whom confirmed the claim was still open. It closed immediately following those calls, just after XXXX PST. I also submitted comprehensive documentation email correspondence, text message screenshots, and payment records none of which was reviewed before closure. A same-day closure without investigation, without provisional credit, and without written denial explanation does not satisfy the requirements of a reasonable investigation under Regulation E, 12 CFR Part 1005.11. Wells Fargo subsequently conducted an ECMO review in response to my escalation, which also failed to correct the errors identified below. IV. WELLS FARGO 'S CFPB RESPONSE CONTAINS A MATERIAL FACTUAL ERROR This is the most critical issue in this refiled complaint. Wells Fargo 's official CFPB response references " two XXXX XXXX transfers totaling {$830.00}. '' A Wells Fargo claims representative also stated repeatedly by phone on XX/XX/XXXX around XXXX PST that the transactions could not be reversed because they were made via " XXXX XXXX. '' This is factually incorrect. I have attached transaction screenshots that clearly show both payments were processed directly from my Wells Fargo debit card not from an XXXX XXXX account. XXXX XXXX and debit card transactions are governed by different dispute frameworks, different chargeback rights, and different regulatory standards under Regulation E. If Wells Fargo investigated and denied these transactions under an XXXX XXXX classification, they investigated the wrong transaction type entirely. A denial built on a misclassified transaction is not a valid denial it is evidence that no proper investigation occurred. I am requesting that the CFPB note this factual error as part of Wells Fargo 's official response record and require Wells Fargo to reinvestigate under the correct transaction classification. V. WELLS FARGO 'S " NO FRAUD INDICATORS '' FINDING IS UNSUPPORTED Wells Fargo 's response states their investigation found " no indicators present confirming fraud. '' I submitted email correspondence, text message screenshots, and payment records documenting every stage of the fraudulent scheme fabricated employment, fraudulent cashier 's checks accepted by Wells Fargo 's own system, explicit payment instructions, promised delivery that never occurred, and complete disappearance of all parties. Wells Fargo 's response does not identify what evidence they reviewed, what investigative standard was applied, or why fabricated professional identities, altered financial instruments cleared by their own bank, and a vanishing supplier do not constitute fraud indicators. A conclusion of " no fraud '' that does not engage the submitted evidence is not an investigation it is a predetermined outcome. VI. WELLS FARGO DIRECTED ME TO CONTACT THE MERCHANT MULTIPLE TIMES Wells Fargo 's response and their Executive Office representative advised me to " resolve this with the merchant directly. '' This advice confirms that Wells Fargo either did not review my submitted documentation or chose to ignore it entirely. There is no legitimate merchant to contact. Every party involved the employer, the referral, and the supplier was a fabricated identity operating as part of a coordinated fraud scheme. Directing a documented fraud victim to contact a fictitious scammer is not a resolution. It is a deflection that further demonstrates the inadequacy of Wells Fargo 's investigation. VII. THE AUTHORIZATION DEFENSE DOES NOT APPLY Wells Fargo 's position is that I authorized these transactions and therefore bear full liability. Authorization requires informed and voluntary consent. My consent was obtained entirely through fabricated employment, false professional identities, and fraudulent financial instruments. There was no legitimate transaction every element was manufactured to deceive me. Authorization induced by fraud is not valid authorization. The CFPB 's own guidance recognizes that " authorized '' does not mean " voluntary and informed '' in the context of scam-induced payments. Wells Fargo has not addressed this distinction in any of their responses. VIII. SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION ATTACHED -Wells Fargo 's official CFPB response referencing XXXX XXXX misclassification -Debit card transaction screenshots rebutting the XXXX XXXX classification -Email correspondence documenting the fraudulent hiring process and payment instructions -Text message screenshots documenting payment instructions and delivery promises XXXX and XXXX XXXX payment confirmations showing dates, amounts, and recipient Message documenting promised check reissuance after account closure Active complaint reference numbers : FBI IC3 [ XXXX ], FTC [ XXXX ] , OCC [ filed XX/XX/XXXX , awaiting case # ], California DFPI [ XXXX ]. I have been a Wells Fargo customer for nearly 30 years with no prior fraud history. I am requesting a thorough, lawful reinvestigation and the reimbursement I am entitled to under federal consumer protection standards.

narrative: Formal Complaint Regarding Missing Returned Funds and Failure to Resolve Electronic Funds Transfer Dispute I am submitting this complaint to request assistance regarding a missing {$14000.00} involving my Wells Fargo business account and Wells Fargos failure to properly investigate and resolve the matter. Under NACHA Operating Rules, which govern ACH transactions : Return code RO2 ( Account Closed ) requires the receiving bank to return funds promptly Each ACH transaction must have a valid trace number for tracking through the network Originating and receiving banks must be able to trace, verify, and reconcile returned entries Concern # 1 : Wells Fargo has not successfully traced the return This suggests potential non-compliance with ACH tracking, documentation, and return processing requirements. Concern # 2 : This reflects a failure in interbank communication, reconciliation, and funds recovery procedures, leaving the consumer bearing the loss. This matter has caused financial hardship and significant stress to my business. I respectfully request that the XXXX XXXX Board of Financial Institutions : Review Wells Fargos handling of this dispute Assist in requiring Wells Fargo to conduct a full investigation Determine the location/status of the returned funds Require Wells Fargo to reimburse the missing {$14000.00} if the funds can not be located Thank you for your attention to this matter.

'' This reasoning applies Goods Not Received logic that delivery of the virtual currency satisfied the merchant 's obligations to a dispute that had been reclassified under Quality of Services Received. In addition, the disputed charges far exceeded the amount of money typically maintained in the account, and I do not normally overdraft or engage in spending patterns remotely similar to these transactions. After the denial, during conversations with Bank of America representatives, I learned additional information that was apparently known to the bank but was not disclosed to me during the original investigation. I was informed that there had been multiple failed authorization attempts and failed CVV attempts before the transactions were eventually approved. I was told that someone repeatedly attempted different security codes until one succeeded. I was also informed by a representative on the phone with my local bank agent that additional suspicious activity involving attempted ACH activity or related account activity occurred after the debit card fraud. Due to these fraud concerns, Bank of America restricted my account to credit only status and opened a replacement account for me. This information appears highly relevant to whether my account was compromised and whether the disputed transactions were unauthorized. Despite these indicators of suspicious activity, my original fraud claim was denied. The unauthorized charges effectively drained my bank account and created immediate financial hardship for my family. I am a mother and am currently awaiting my next paycheck while attempting to manage essential expenses after losing access to these funds. I also requested information regarding hardship assistance or a hardship line of credit from Bank of America during this process, but I was never contacted regarding that request. I have since requested reconsideration of the claim and am currently awaiting a new determination. However, I am concerned that the original investigation may not have been reasonable or complete given the apparent evidence of fraudulent activity. I am requesting that Bank of America : conduct a thorough reconsideration of the fraud claim, provide copies or summaries of the evidence relied upon in denying the original claim, explain how the failed CVV attempts and suspicious ACH-related activity were evaluated during the investigation, provide any relevant investigative findings or fraud notes, and reimburse the unauthorized charges if the investigation confirms the transactions were fraudulent. narrative: Here is a stronger complaint that directly addresses both * * Chases conduct * * and * * CFPBs handling of the matter * * : Consumer Financial Protection Bureau RE : Request for Supervisory Review of CFPB Complaint Handling and JPMorgan Chases Continued Withholding of Funds CFPB Case No. : XXXX Financial Institution : JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . I am submitting this complaint because the Consumer Financial Protection Bureaus handling of my prior complaint appears to have accepted JPMorgan Chases response without meaningful review of the actual facts presented. My concern is no longer limited to JPMorgan Chases conduct, but now also includes the failure of the complaint resolution process to address the substance of the issue. JPMorgan Chase has continued to provide the same repetitive response, refusing to release my funds based on documentation demands that are impossible to satisfy under the circumstances. The central issue is straightforward : Chase closed my account while I was overseas and claims that a cashiers check was issued for my remaining funds, approximately {$40000.00}. I never received this check. Because I never received the check, I do not possess the cashiers check number or the issuance date. Yet Chase continues insisting that I must provide the very information that would only be available if I had actually received the check. This is circular, unreasonable, and obstructive. The CFPB appears to have accepted Chases response without questioning this obvious contradiction. I respectfully ask : How is a consumer expected to provide the number and issuance date of a cashiers check that was never delivered? If the bank issued the instrument, Chase itself has full internal access to : * the cashiers check number * the issuance date * the exact amount * mailing records * tracking or delivery information, if any * stop-payment or reissuance procedures These are records maintained by the banknot the consumer. Instead of addressing this reality, Chase continues issuing the same boilerplate denial. Even more concerning, Chases response contains statements that appear inconsistent with the facts. I previously submitted a notarized affidavit executed in XXXX, XXXX, concerning the lost/non-received cashiers check. Chase now claims the document was not signed or notarized, while also simultaneously referencing supposed issues with the notary section. These contradictory assertions raise serious questions about whether my submission was reviewed in good faith. Chase also claims that the notary date is no longer valid, which requires explanation. A notarization confirms the authenticity of a signature on the date executed. It does not simply become invalid because time has passed unless Chase is relying on some internal policy, which has not been properly explained. This complaint therefore raises two issues : First, JPMorgan Chases continued withholding of consumer funds through unreasonable and impossible procedural demands. Second, the CFPB complaint handling process accepting conclusory institutional responses without addressing the actual consumer complaint. I request supervisory review of this matter and answers to the following : 1. Why was Chase not required to explain how a consumer could provide check details for a check never received? 2. Why was Chase not required to provide evidence of the alleged cashiers check issuance, including check number, issuance date, mailing method, and delivery confirmation? 3. Why were contradictory claims about my notarized submission accepted without scrutiny? 4. What substantive review was conducted before closing or accepting Chases response? At this point, this matter concerns not only Chases refusal to release funds, but whether the consumer complaint process is functioning as intended. I request : * immediate supervisory review by the CFPB * reopening of this complaint * formal demand that Chase provide documentary proof of the cashiers check issuance * explanation of Chases legal basis for refusing to reissue funds * escalation to the appropriate federal banking regulator if necessary This matter has caused significant financial harm, operational disruption, and prolonged deprivation of access to my own funds. I expect a substantive review rather than another procedural closure based solely on Chase repeating the same unsupported response. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX
