I asked because the receipt did not clearly disclose any actual fee, commission, spread, vendor markup, or embedded exchange-rate cost. I was told there were no fees. However, the receipt states that Chases foreign exchange rates include spreads paid to Chase and its vendors and that Chase may make a commission for providing foreign exchange services. Had Chase clearly disclosed before the transaction that the exchange rate included an embedded spread, commission, vendor markup, or other cost approaching 9.91 % to 10 %, I would not have completed the transaction with Chase. I relied on the statement that there were no fees, and I was not provided a clear, upfront disclosure showing the actual cost built into the exchange rate. After I discovered the exchange-rate issue, I attempted to have Chase reverse or unwind the transaction. Chase refused. The branch manager stated that there was nothing she could do. Instead of reversing the transaction at the original rate, Chase offered to buy back the same XXXX pesos at a worse exchange rate of XXXX USD per XXXX. Item Calculation Amount Original amount debited from checking {$990.00} Chase buy-back offer XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX {$810.00} Total loss if I accepted buy-back {$990.00} {$810.00} {$180.00} This placed me in a forced-loss position. Chase refused to unwind the transaction after I raised the disclosure issue, and the only alternative Chase offered would have caused me to lose approximately {$180.00} in total. Because I am leaving for my vacation and must use the XXXX pesos, I no longer have a practical option to return the currency. The branch manager also stated, in substance, that as long as she has been working for Chase, no one has ever complained about the foreign currency exchange disclosures. That statement reinforced my concern that this may be a systemic issue, not merely a one-time misunderstanding. It suggests that Chase branch management and staff may not be properly trained on Chases disclosure obligations or may not understand the compliance risks involved when customers are told there are no fees while Chase may still earn compensation through an embedded spread, commission, vendor payment, or exchange-rate adjustment. The absence of prior customer complaints does not mean the disclosure was adequate or legally compliant. It may instead indicate that customers were not aware of the embedded cost or did not understand that the exchange rate included compensation to Chase or its vendors. This is precisely why clear, upfront disclosure is necessary. I believe Chases conduct was unfair and deceptive. Chases representative told me there were no fees, but Chases receipt indicates that Chase may receive compensation through spreads, vendor payments, and/or commissions. Whether Chase labels the cost as a fee, spread, commission, vendor markup, or exchange-rate adjustment, the practical result was the same : Chase used a materially worse exchange rate and did not clearly disclose the embedded cost before debiting my checking account. This conduct appears to implicate federal consumer financial protection laws and regulations, including the following : Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ). The CFPB states that under the Dodd-Frank Act, it is unlawful for providers of consumer financial products or services to engage in unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices. Chases statement that there were no fees, combined with an undisclosed embedded exchange-rate cost approaching 10 %, raises deceptive and unfair-practice concerns. Its deceptive because Chase did not properly disclose the fees, and tow representative stated there are no fees. It is unfair because as a consumer, once they took the money out of my account, I had no recourse for them to correct the mistake of insufficient disclosure and the charged my {$97.00}. Regulation E / Electronic Fund Transfer Act. Because the funds were debited directly from my Chase checking account, this also raises transaction-disclosure and error-resolution concerns. Regulation E applies to electronic fund transfers that authorize a financial institution to debit or credit a consumers account. Chase should explain whether this checking-account debit was treated as an electronic fund transfer and, if so, what disclosures and error-resolution rights applied. Truth in Savings Act / Regulation DD. Regulation DD applies to deposit accounts, including checking accounts, and requires disclosures concerning account terms and fee schedules. Regulation DD also provides that a depository institution must provide account disclosures before an account is opened or before a service is provided, whichever is earlier, when a fee required to be disclosed is assessed. Because this currency exchange was funded from my checking account and may have involved account-based pricing, commission waivers, or foreign exchange service charges, Chase should identify the checking-account terms, fee schedule, foreign currency exchange disclosures, commission schedule, waiver terms, and any preferred-pricing provisions that applied. Because Chase failed to clearly disclose the true cost of the currency exchange, refused to unwind the transaction at the original rate, and instead offered a buy-back rate that would have caused an additional loss, I have lost confidence in Chases handling of my deposit-account services. I am considering closing my Chase accounts when I return from my trip.

Earlier this year, I opened a Wells Fargo account in person with the assistance and approval of branch leadership after providing identification and completing the banks standard verification procedures. Based on conversations and the circumstances surrounding the closure, it appears this decision may be connected to a much older account issue from many years ago in which I was the victim of fraud and unauthorized use involving my banking information. I want to make absolutely clear that I was not the perpetrator of fraud, was never accused or convicted of any criminal wrongdoing, and did not intentionally misuse any account or banking service. What is especially concerning is that despite the significant amount of time that has passed, and despite Wells Fargo personnel reviewing and approving me for a new account relationship earlier this year, I appear to remain subject to a permanent internal restriction without meaningful reconsideration or review. Consumers who experience fraud or identity theft should not be indefinitely treated as though they themselves committed fraud. I fully understand and respect Wells Fargos obligation to protect against financial crime and manage risk. However, I believe there should also be a fair process that distinguishes actual perpetrators of fraud from consumers who were themselves victims of unauthorized activity. Since the original incident occurred many years ago, I have continued maintaining banking relationships elsewhere without issue. I have never engaged in intentional fraud, account abuse, or criminal conduct. I am simply requesting the opportunity to maintain ordinary personal and business banking services with Wells Fargo like any other legitimate customer. I am respectfully requesting : * a formal executive-level review of my profile and any internal fraud or risk coding associated with my name, * confirmation regarding whether negative information was reported to ChexSystems, XXXX XXXX XXXX , or similar consumer reporting agencies, * correction of any inaccurate or misleading fraud-related classifications if present, * and fair reconsideration of my eligibility to maintain personal and business banking relationships with Wells Fargo. Description of Incident : On XX/XX/year>, I deposited a check for {$1300.00} via the Chase mobile app, which was purportedly payment for a remote position I had secured. Verification : After a 24-hour pending period, the Chase mobile app and website updated the status of the check to " Confirmed. '' Communication : According to the Chase website, once a check is " confirmed, '' the funds are " available for use. '' I interpreted this statusprovided by a major financial institutionas a verification that the check had successfully cleared the issuing bank and was legitimate. Reliance on Information : Based solely on this " confirmed '' status, I proceeded to use {$1000.00} of the funds to purchase gift cards as instructed by the employer, believing the bank had verified the security of the deposit. Reversal : Several days later, Chase notified me that the check had been returned. This resulted in a significant financial loss, as the " confirmed '' funds were retracted from my account after I had already spent them. Basis for Complaint : While I understand that federal regulations require banks to make funds available quickly, the use of the term " Confirmed '' is misleading to the average consumer. To a layperson, " confirmed '' implies that the bank has verified the validity of the funds with the originating institution. By explicitly stating the money was " available '' and " confirmed, '' Chase provided a false sense of security that directly led to my financial victimization.

narrative: I submit this complaint as a victim of identity theft and unauthorized electronic fund transfers and as a final effort to resolve this matter before filing suit against Capital One Bank for violations of the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) and Regulation E. Approximately two years ago, my XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX came out of remission and I was diagnosed with a XXXX XXXX XXXX. I underwent XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and periods of medical incapacity while being evaluated for tXXXX XXXX During this time, my cellular telephones, financial accounts, computers, and personal identifying information were compromised and taken over without authorization. An individual identified as XXXX XXXX gained unauthorized access to my devices, financial information, and accounts and initiated unauthorized XXXX debits and electronic transfers involving Capital One accounts ending in XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX. Bank statements and correspondence were redirected away from my residence through unauthorized change-of-address activity, preventing discovery of the fraud while I remained critically ill and repeatedly hospitalized. I never authorized XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, or any other person to debit, transfer, withdraw, or otherwise access funds from my accounts from 2022 through the present date. XXXX XXXX likewise never authorized the disputed ACH debits or payment activity and never provided verbal, written, electronic, or any other authorization permitting my accounts to be debited. She is herself a victim of the same identity theft activity. Despite sworn affidavits, police reports, FTC Identity Theft Reports, medical documentation, and corroborating evidence establishing identity theft and lack of authorization, Capital One continues denying reimbursement and relies upon assumptions and speculation rather than competent evidence of authorization. Capital One does not possess and has never produced : Any signed ACH authorization ; Any authenticated electronic authorization ; Any recorded authorization ; Any authenticated device verification ; or Any competent evidence establishing knowing authorization for the disputed transactions. Under 15 U.S.C. 1693g, the burden rests entirely upon the financial institution to prove authorization for disputed electronic fund transfers. Regulation E further requires a reasonable, good-faith investigation once unauthorized transfers are reported. Other financial institutions, including XXXX and XXXX XXXX, investigated substantially similar fraudulent activity arising from the same identity theft events and reimbursed unauthorized transactions after determining the activity was fraudulent and unauthorized. Capital One instead continues victim blaming despite overwhelming evidence that I was critically ill, medically incapacitated, and the victim of widespread identity theft during the relevant periods. My circumstances fit squarely within the protections and extended look-back provisions applicable to victims of unauthorized electronic fund transfers and identity theft under federal law. The unauthorized activity was not reasonably discoverable while my accounts, devices, and communications remained compromised during prolonged medical incapacity. I request that the CFPB require Capital One to : 1. Reimburse all unauthorized ACH debits and electronic transfers ; 2. Cooperate in returning the unauthorized funds to my bank accounts ; 3. Refund all associated fees and charges ; 4. Correct any adverse credit reporting connected to the fraudulent activity ; 5. Provide all records relied upon in denying my disputes, including device logs, IP logs, authentication records, ACH authorizations, change-of-address records, and internal fraud investigation notes ; and 6. Comply fully with the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E. I attach sworn affidavits, police reports, FTC Identity Theft Reports, medical documentation, and supporting records establishing that the disputed transactions were unauthorized.

I am submitting this follow-up complaint regarding Wells Fargos handling of multiple unauthorized electronic fund transfer ( EFT ) disputes, the resulting overdraft balance, and the closure of my checking account. I previously filed complaints regarding unauthorized transactions that I did not authorize, initiate, participate in, or benefit from. Wells Fargo responded but failed to adequately address several important issues regarding the investigation and denial of these claims. The disputed transactions included : - Claim XXXX : {$900.00} XXXX transaction disputed on XX/XX/XXXX and denied on XX/XX/XXXX - Claim XXXX : {$140.00} XXXX XXXX transaction disputed on XX/XX/XXXX and denied the same day - Claim XXXX : {$200.00} XXXX XXXX XXXX transaction disputed on XX/XX/XXXX and later denied after provisional credit reversal - Claim XXXX : unauthorized recurring payments totaling {$92.00}, initially denied and later reversed after additional review and credited back on XX/XX/XXXX My disputes consistently involved claims of unauthorized transactions and fraud. However, Wells Fargos denial explanations repeatedly referenced concepts such as : - failure to return merchandise, - no indication services differed from the merchant description, - or failure to revoke authorization in a timely manner. These explanations do not address my actual disputes, which were that certain transactions themselves were unauthorized. Most concerning is the {$900.00} XXXX transaction. I did not authorize this transaction, did not conduct business with XXXX, did not receive any benefit from the transaction, and have never shopped there. Wells Fargos response failed to explain what evidence was relied upon to conclude that the transaction was authorized. Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E, financial institutions are required to conduct reasonable investigations into alleged unauthorized EFTs. Under 15 U.S.C. 1693g ( b ), the burden of proof is on the financial institution to establish that the transfers were authorized. Importantly, Wells Fargo later overturned one previously denied claim after additional review and recredited my account for {$92.00} on XX/XX/XXXX. This demonstrates that at least one prior investigation result was inaccurate and raises concerns regarding the reliability and adequacy of the investigations performed on the remaining denied claims. The disputed transactions contributed directly to the accounts negative balance and eventual closure. Wells Fargo closed the account on XX/XX/XXXX while disputed unauthorized transaction balances remained unresolved. I do not believe consumers should be required to pay overdraft balances and fees arising from disputed unauthorized transactions before the institution adequately proves authorization. Wells Fargo also stated that it reported the account to XXXX XXXX XXXX and internal recovery systems. I am concerned that disputed balances tied to unresolved unauthorized transaction claims are continuing to affect my ability to access banking services. I am requesting CFPB review regarding whether Wells Fargo : - Conducted reasonable investigations under Regulation E - Properly satisfied its burden of proving authorization under 15 U.S.C. 1693g ( b ) - Improperly treated unauthorized EFT disputes as merchant or merchandise disputes- Improperly reversed provisional credits without sufficient proof of authorization - Improperly maintained overdraft balances and fees arising from disputed unauthorized transactions - Improperly closed the account while disputed unauthorized transactions remained unresolved - Improperly reported disputed balances to XXXX XXXX XXXX or related systems

narrative: I am filing this complaint against Citibank / Citi Cards for failing to properly investigate and resolve a billing dispute filed under the Fair Credit Billing Act. Summary of the dispute : On XX/XX/year>, I was charged {$940.00} by XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( XXXX, PA ) for a plumbing service call at my rental property ( XXXX, PA XXXX ). The work performed was described as clearing a blocked sewer main line using a cable snaking machine. I am disputing {$800.00} of this charge on the grounds that the service was not completed as expected. Key evidence of failed service : Only seven ( 7 ) days after the first visit, on XX/XX/year>, the same plumbing company ( XXXX XXXX ) was called back to the same property for the identical sewer blockage problem and charged me an additional {$420.00} ( Invoice # XXXX ). The second technicians own invoice notes confirm that the fresh air inlet the exact access point used on the first visit was still covered, and that the house trap was narrow filled with dirt and mulch. The technician recommended a hydrojet and camera inspection, which should have been performed during the first visit given the severity of the blockage. In other words, XXXX XXXX own documentation proves the first visit failed to resolve the problem. Citis handling of the dispute : I filed a dispute with Citi on XX/XX/year> ( Citi Case ID : XXXX ) on the grounds of goods/services not as expected. Citi issued a conditional credit of {$800.00} at that time. I subsequently sent Citi a detailed written dispute letter via certified mail, including both invoices and photographic evidence showing the severity of the initial blockage and the condition of the drain at the second visit. Despite this documentation including the merchants own second invoice as evidence of an incomplete first repair Citi sided with the merchant and reversed the conditional credit, holding me responsible for the full disputed amount. Why I believe Citis decision was incorrect : Under the Fair Credit Billing Act, a billing dispute based on services not rendered as expected requires the card issuer to conduct a reasonable investigation. I provided Citi with two invoices from the same merchant one for the disputed charge and a second one, dated just seven days later, for the same work at the same location. The second invoice is not a separate, unrelated service : it is direct, contemporaneous evidence from the merchant itself that the first repair was incomplete. narrative: To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this complaint regarding the handling of my dispute involving a transaction with XXXX XXXX My dispute was improperly evaluated as a simple merchandise not returned matter, despite extensive written documentation demonstrating that the actual issue involves merchant misrepresentation, contradictory guidance, and undisclosed conditions introduced after my reliance on the merchants written communications. The merchant, XXXX XXXX, provided written clarification extending its 45-day money-back guarantee through approximately XX/XX/XXXX. This clarification was provided directly by the company via email in response to ambiguity regarding its published terms and conditions and its advertised 45-day risk-free trial. I relied on that written clarification in good faith. Afterward, the merchant reversed its position and introduced an additional condition that the product ( or empty product bags ) allegedly needed to be physically received by their facility within the same guarantee window, after having told me the empty bags could be disposed of seeing as how they were consumable goods. This condition was never disclosed in the written clarification provided to me, nor was it communicated as a requirement when I was instructed I could continue trying the product until approximately XX/XX/XXXX. On the contrary, the company continued encouraging me to try additional product shipments after my cancellation request had been ignored and after I had already informed them the product was not working for me and that I intended to rely on the advertised 45-day money-back guarantee. It was only after additional questioning on my part that the company disclosed the additional shipment allegedly would not qualify under the guarantee, at which point I declined the shipment again. Prior to that clarification, the company was also attempting to hold me financially responsible for that shipment despite my cancellation request having been submitted before processing and shipment. They did, however, after much time and effort and multiple emails, eventually refund me for that second shipment, calling it a " courtesy '' instead of taking accountability for shipping it out and causing a bigger issue to begin with. The dispute and complaint therefore are not simply about returned merchandise. The bank reversed provisional credits without addressing the core evidence : the merchant denies the account exists, the transactions were initiated using stolen account information, and at least one of the transfers was indisputably reported within the required timeframe. Chases position improperly shifts liability onto me despite clear regulatory protections for identitytheft victims and accountnumber fraud cases. narrative: I am a current XXXX credit card holder. On XXXX XXXX XXXX, I received a promotional email from Chase Bank that was addressed to me by name. The offer was up to {$900.00} for opening a new Chase Total Checking account and a new Chase Savings account and completing the qualifying activities. It included a specific offer code ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) and was presented as a thank you to me as an existing Chase customer. Around that same time, I logged into the Chase Mobile app, applied for both accounts, and was approved. Chase opened a Chase Total Checking account ending in XXXX and a Chase Savings account ending in XXXX. On XXXX XXXX XXXX roughly a week after the accounts were opened, I received an email from Chase titled " Account update. '' It said both accounts had been restricted to protect against potential fraud and may close soon. Both account numbers were referenced. The email stated, " Due to recent activity, or because we need more information from you, we have restricted your account ( s ) and may close it soon, '' and directed me to call XXXX. I called Chase. The representative told me that Chase 's terms and conditions allow the bank to terminate banking relationships at its discretion and that I would not be able to open new Chase deposit accounts. I was not given a specific reason for the closure. I was not told which database or flag triggered it. I was not given any opportunity to provide information or resolve whatever the underlying concern was. The part I find difficult to make sense of is the timing. The closure happened so quickly that I never had a chance to do anything with the accounts. I did not deposit any money. I did not set up direct deposit. I did not initiate a single transaction. I had no opportunity to complete any of the qualifying activities that would have earned the bonus. The accounts were effectively opened and closed before they were ever used. That tells me the closure could not have been based on actual account activity, because there was none. It strongly suggests a pre-existing internal flag or external consumer reporting check that Chase already had on me at the time it sent the solicitation. What has happened since the closure is also worth flagging. I am still receiving the same {$900.00} promotional email from Chase, asking me to open the exact accounts I have just been told I am not allowed to open. Today, XXXX XXXX XXXX after the restriction notice and after my call with Chase confirming I can not have these accounts, I also received an email from Chase congratulating me on my new Chase accounts. The same accounts that have been closed. This is not the first time something like this has happened either. Chase has opened and then closed deposit accounts I applied for on more than one prior occasion. That repeating pattern points to a persistent internal flag rather than anything tied to specific account behavior. I want to be clear about my goal in filing this complaint. It is not punitive. I value Chase as an institution and, given Chase 's national footprint, I am actively looking to transition my primary banking from the credit union I currently use to Chase. The promotional offer was meaningful to me because I was prepared to make Chase my primary bank, not because of the bonus itself. What I am asking for is a path forward to actually establish that deposit relationship and enough transparency about what happened so I can address the underlying issue. CFPB Desired Resolution : 1. A documented path for me to actually establish a Chase Total Checking and Chase Savings relationship. I am actively trying to move my primary banking from my current credit union to Chase, and I am asking for a workable resolution that allows me to become a Chase deposit customer, not a refund or one-time payout. 2. A written explanation of the specific reason Chase closed accounts ending in XXXX and XXXX, so I can understand and, if possible, address whatever the underlying concern is. 3. Disclosure of whether the closure was based on XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX, another consumer reporting agency, or Chase 's internal risk database. If an external consumer reporting agency was involved, I need to know which one so I can exercise my dispute rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. 4. Confirmation of whether Chase has reported the closure to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. If so, I want to know what was reported so I can address it with those agencies directly.

On XX/XX/XXXX, a prior written request for validation and verification of the alleged debt was sent to your office via Certified Mail. As of XX/XX/XXXX, no response, documentation, verification, or lawful validation has been provided. Accordingly, this letter constitutes a second formal demand for compliance with federal consumer protection laws, including but not limited to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ). Specifically, the following documentation is demanded immediately : 1. A complete copy of the original signed retail installment sales contract and financing agreement ; 2. Verification and validation of the alleged debt pursuant to federal law ; 3. A complete chain of assignment and transfer demonstrating lawful ownership and authority of Capital One Auto Finance to collect on the alleged account ; 4. Forward flow agreements and any purchase/sale agreements evidencing transfer from the dealership to Capital One Auto Finance ; 5. Complete account-level documentation reflecting : * Itemized accounting, * Payment history, * Interest calculations, * Fees, * Credits, * Accurate balance owed ; 6. Written verification bearing competent evidence that the alleged debt is legally enforceable against the undersigned consumers. The following federal statutes are applicable to this dispute and request : 15 U.S.C. 1692g Validation of Debts This statute requires that a consumer be provided validation of the debt upon dispute. Specifically, under 1692g ( b ) : > If the consumer notifies the debt collector in writing within the thirty-day period that the debt, or any portion thereof, is disputed, the debt collector shall cease collection of the debt until the debt collector obtains verification of the debt and a copy of such verification is mailed to the consumer. Accordingly, all collection activity must cease until proper written verification is produced. 15 U.S.C. 1692e False or Misleading Representations This statute prohibits : > Any false, deceptive, or misleading representation or means in connection with the collection of any debt. Attempting to collect without competent proof of ownership, assignment, validation, or legal standing may constitute deceptive collection activity under this section. 15 U.S.C. 1666 Billing Error Resolution This statute provides protections regarding disputed accounts and obligates creditors to conduct reasonable investigations into disputed matters. The statute requires acknowledgment and investigation of disputes submitted in writing concerning account accuracy and obligations. Failure to provide adequate documentation, investigate disputed balances, or respond to written disputes may constitute noncompliance with federal law. PLEASE TAKE NOTICE : Because Capital One Auto Finance has failed to provide lawful verification and documentation after receipt of the certified correspondence dated XX/XX/XXXX, continued collection activity without compliance may constitute violations of federal consumer protection statutes. Until the requested documentation is produced, you are hereby instructed to : * Cease all collection activity ; * Cease reporting or furnishing disputed information to any consumer reporting agency ; * Refrain from making any representations regarding ownership or enforceability of the alleged debt without competent documentary proof. This letter is not a refusal to pay, but rather a lawful notice of dispute and demand for strict proof and verification pursuant to federal law. Please provide all requested documentation within thirty ( 30 ) days of receipt of this correspondence. Sincerely, -- - XXXX XXXX -- - XXXX XXXX, Co-Signer CC : Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) Federal Trade Commission ( FTC )

Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ), 15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq., and Regulation E, financial institutions are required to properly investigate and handle electronic fund transfer issues involving consumer accounts. Additionally, ACH transactions are governed by XXXX Operating Rules, which generally require that transactions sent to closed accounts be returned by the receiving financial institution within the required return timeframe rather than retained or delayed without explanation. The Wells Fargo bank representative informed me that from the banks side the funds/account were essentially in limbo and stated there was nothing they could do other than tell me to wait. I was not provided any meaningful explanation, escalation, investigation details, ACH return information, or estimated timeline regarding the handling of the funds. Being told that over {$10000.00} in educational refund funds are in limbo without a clear answer as to whether the funds were rejected, internally held, or returned is unreasonable and has caused significant uncertainty, financial hardship, and distress. Because Wells Fargo had prior knowledge that the account was closed and incapable of receiving deposits, the bank had a duty to promptly reject and return the ACH payment to the originating institution. Any unreasonable delay, internal hold, or failure to timely process the return may constitute improper handling of consumer funds and may interfere with my ability to access educational refund money intended for tuition, housing, transportation, and living expenses. As a direct result of the banks actions and/or delay : I have been deprived access to over {$10000.00} in educational funds ; I have suffered financial hardship and uncertainty regarding the status of my money ; The originating institution has been unable to promptly reissue payment ; and I have spent significant time attempting to trace and resolve the transaction. I am requesting : An immediate investigation into the status and location of the ACH funds ; Immediate return of the funds to XXXX XXXX if the account can not legally accept deposits ; Written confirmation regarding whether the ACH was rejected, returned, or internally held ; ACH trace and return information, including any applicable return codes ; Compensation or corrective action to the extent Wells Fargo failed to timely process the return in accordance with applicable banking and ACH rules ; and Assurance that Wells Fargo is complying with consumer protection laws governing electronic fund transfers and closed accounts. Attached documentation includes : Screenshots from XXXX XXXX showing the refund issuance details and transaction information ; Screenshots from Wells Fargo confirming the receiving account ending in XXXX is closed. The continued delay and lack of transparency regarding the handling of these funds has interfered with timely access to money intended for educational purposes and has caused avoidable financial distress.

These representations were material to my purchasing decision and formed the basis of the contractual relationship between myself and the merchant. Following purchase, delivery, installation, and attempted implementation of the software, I experienced substantial deficiencies affecting functionality, performance, reliability, and usability. The software failed to perform in a manner reasonably consistent with the representations made before purchase and did not provide the benefits or operational capabilities advertised during the sales process. Despite good-faith efforts to work directly with the merchant and obtain support and resolution, the issues remained unresolved. As a result, I was deprived of the benefit of the bargain and did not receive conforming goods and services consistent with the transaction for which payment was made. FACTUAL BASIS FOR DISPUTE 1. Goods and Services Not as Described The software and related services delivered materially differed from the functionality, capabilities, reliability, and operational expectations represented by the merchant before purchase. The representations made concerning the software 's capabilities created reasonable expectations regarding performance and usability. The product delivered failed to satisfy those expectations and did not perform as represented. Because the software delivered materially differed from the representations relied upon during the transaction, these charges qualify for review as goods and services not received as described. 2. Defective and Non-Conforming Product The software exhibited substantial deficiencies affecting its intended use and operation. The product failed to perform in a commercially reasonable manner and did not provide the functionality that formed the basis of the purchase transaction. A product that can not reasonably perform its intended purpose may constitute a non-conforming product for purposes of consumer billing-dispute rights and chargeback review. 3. Breach of Contract The merchant entered into a contractual relationship by offering software and services under specific representations concerning functionality, performance, support, and expected results. The failure to deliver goods and services substantially consistent with those representations constitutes a material breach of the agreement under which payment was made. Had the true nature and limitations of the product been accurately disclosed, I would not have entered into the transaction. 4. Material Misrepresentation The merchant 's advertising, promotional statements, sales presentations, and product descriptions materially influenced my purchasing decision. The actual functionality and performance experienced after delivery appear inconsistent with those representations. To the extent that material information concerning software capabilities, operational limitations, performance expectations, support availability, or system functionality was omitted, inaccurately described, or otherwise misrepresented, the transaction may involve deceptive or misleading business practices warranting consumer protection review. FEDERAL CONSUMER PROTECTION AUTHORITIES I respectfully request that U.S. Bank evaluate this dispute pursuant to all applicable federal laws and consumer-protection regulations, including the following : Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) The Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1666 et seq. ) provides consumers with the right to dispute billing errors involving : Goods not delivered as agreed ; Goods or services materially different from what was represented ; Defective or non-conforming products ; Charges resulting from misrepresentation or contractual nonperformance. The FCBA requires creditors to conduct reasonable investigations of disputed transactions and protects consumers against liability for qualifying billing disputes. Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) The Truth in Lending Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. ) was enacted to promote fairness and transparency in consumer credit transactions. TILA provides consumers with important dispute rights concerning credit card purchases involving defective products, non-conforming services, and transactions affected by material misrepresentations. The protections afforded by TILA should be liberally applied to ensure consumers receive the benefit of fair dispute-resolution procedures. Regulation Z Regulation Z ( 12 C.F.R. Part 1026 ) implements the Truth in Lending Act and establishes procedural protections governing disputed credit card transactions. These protections include the right to dispute charges arising from transactions involving products or services that fail to conform to contractual representations and expectations. Federal Trade Commission Act The Federal Trade Commission Act ( 15 U.S.C. 45 ) prohibits unfair or deceptive acts or practices affecting commerce. Examples may include : Material misrepresentations concerning products or services ; Misleading advertising ; False or unsupported performance claims ; Omissions of material facts affecting purchasing decisions ; Failure to provide promised products, services, or support. To the extent the merchant 's representations materially influenced the transaction and are inconsistent with the product delivered, these issues warrant careful review. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau enforces federal consumer-financial laws and safeguards consumers against unfair, deceptive, or abusive practices. The CFPB 's consumer-protection framework emphasizes : Fair treatment of consumers ; Meaningful dispute investigations ; Accurate review of documentary evidence ; Protection from deceptive commercial conduct ; Accountability when consumers do not receive products or services as represented. I respectfully request that these consumer-protection principles be considered during review of this dispute. I am filing this complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. regarding material misrepresentations, deceptive business practices, failure to legally provide mandatory consumer disclosures, and systemic electronic fund access failures that resulted in actual financial damages totaling {$7500.00}. I am a XXXX veteran with documented memory-related cognitive limitations. To safely manage my finances and avoid the severe personal safety risks associated with handling large amounts of physical currency, I rely strictly on secure digital banking infrastructurespecifically mobile wallet functionality and electronic transfersas a necessary disability accommodation. On XX/XX/year>, approximately one and a half hours before the branch closed, I opened a checking account at the Chase XXXX XXXX XXXX. I explicitly informed the representative that I required immediate, reliable electronic access to my funds for scheduled international travel the following day ( XX/XX/XXXX ) because I could not safely carry physical currency. I was explicitly assured by Chase personnel that I would have immediate access to my deposited funds via mobile wallet functionality, electronic transfers, and ATM usage. These material representations directly induced me to open the account and deposit my funds. At the time of account opening, Chase personnel failed to provide me with any physical account disclosures, fee schedules, or account terms. In an explicit admission to me, a Chase Escalations Manager stated that the only electronic signature on file from my branch session was solely to verify that my personal information was correct. This constitutes a direct compliance failure by JPMorgan Chase. Under the Federal E-SIGN Act and Regulation DD, a financial institution can not legally substitute paper disclosures with electronic delivery without obtaining a separate, explicit, affirmative E-SIGN Consumer Consent Disclosure. Verifying identity or confirming that personal details are spelled correctly does not meet the legal threshold for electronic delivery consent. Because Chase failed to obtain valid electronic consent and failed to provide physical copies, they are in non-compliant violation of Regulation DD 's mandatory account-opening disclosure rules, leaving me completely unaware of hidden account holds or restrictions. Immediately after leaving the branch, I experienced a catastrophic, total access failure. Every digital channel failed : transfers to my external XXXX account were blocked, mobile wallet transactions were declined, and ATM withdrawals failed. Again I explicitly disclosed my status as a disabled veteran and detailed my memory-related cognitive limitations, reiterating that I could not safely handle or carry physical cash. Representatives stated that a flag existed on the account, but assured me they would contact XXXX to remove it and that the issue would resolve within approximately XXXX minutes in a brief phone call with the fraud department. I relied on this representation to my severe detriment ; the issue was not resolved, and the total electronic block remained. On XX/XX/year> ( the morning of my flight ), I returned to the XXXX XXXX XXXX. Chase personnel identified an alleged address mismatch with XXXX XXXX and stated it was completely corrected. A single {$20.00} test transaction processed successfully inside the branch. However, immediately upon leaving the branch, the systemic failures resumed. The mobile wallet failed, ATM access was declined, and transfers remained blocked. This proves the access barrier extended far beyond a simple mobile wallet sync issue. On XX/XX/year>, I received my physical debit card. No disclosures were included. I spent over three hours on multiple calls with Chase escalation teams. A representative on a 50-minute call explicitly stated that my card was " functioning properly '' and that they " saw no declined transactions. '' Yet, at approximately XXXX XXXX that same night, the physical card was systematically declined at an ATM. escalated this internally to the Chase Executive Office ( Case Reference : XXXX ). The final determination issued by reviewer " XXXX '' is a bad-faith, liability-shielding mischaracterization of events. Chases written response attempts to reduce this multi-day, multi-channel crisis to a routine " address mismatch. '' Their defense completely ignores the fact that the address was corrected on XX/XX/XXXX and that physical ATM and debit card declines continued days afterward. Furthermore, their response claims I " raised no concerns '' at account opening, disingenuously portraying me as dishonest ; I had no concerns to raise on XX/XX/XXXX because I had not yet attempted to use the non-functional product Chase marketed to me until only after banks closing hours. Neither was I aware that Chase does NOT HAVE A 24/hour customer service line. The fraud department is the only department 24 hours. As a direct result of Chases deceptive practices, electronic fund blockages, and total failure to accommodate my disability needs during a critical travel window, I suffered severe, measurable financial harm : 1. Travel Loss ( {$1700.00} ) : Because Chase completely froze access to my travel capital, I was forced to miss my scheduled international flight on XX/XX/year>. 2. Cash Loss ( {$5800.00} ) : Because Chase paralyzed all electronic channels and provided no alternative digital access bridge, I was forced into a highly vulnerable physical security position. To access my own money, I had to physically enter a branch and withdraw massive physical cash reserves, forcing me to handle large amounts of physical currency despite my cognitive limitations, which directly resulted in a subsequent physical cash loss of {$5800.00}. I possess corroborating audio recordings of Chase personnel and fraud supervisors admitting that I should have received physical disclosures, that this situation was highly unusual, and that they had " never seen anything like it. '' I advise the CFPB when looking into the matter to request phone recordings between myself and Chase staff to corroborate my affidavit. From XX/XX/year> - XX/XX/year>. These phone calls will also include conversations with Chases executive office.

narrative: FORMAL DATA INTEGRITY DISPUTE : ACCOUNT LEDGER CORRUPTION & SYSTEMIC REPORTING INACCURACIES CHRONOLOGY OF EVENTS : XX/XX/XXXX : Executed a Retail Installment Contract ( Contract # XXXX ) with Capital One Auto Finance for an Amount Financed of {$21000.00} over a strict contractual 72-month term at an Annual Percentage Rate ( APR ) of 14.51 %. XX/XX/XXXXXXXX : Following a repossession, Capital Ones internal digital ledger recorded a transaction line item for liquidation asset recovery designated as " Auction Proceeds Received '' in the amount of - {$3200.00}. XX/XX/XXXXXXXX : Capital One issued a formal, physical written " Explanation of Deficiency Calculation '' statement. This mailer explicitly states that the " Proceeds from sale of Collateral '' were {$3900.00}. This creates an unreconciled, immediate {$650.00} accounting conflict between the bank 's written consumer disclosures and its internal transactional system. The letter demanded a final deficiency balance of {$25000.00}. XX/XX/XXXXXXXX : Capital One 's internal ledger shows three consecutive " Waiver Adjustments '' applied to the account in the amounts of - {$7900.00}, - {$470.00}, and - {$130.00}, totaling an uncommunicated ledger reduction of - {$8500.00}. The consumer was never sent an updated, corrected physical statement accounting for these massive adjustments. XXXX XXXX : Capital Ones live online mobile banking platform shows the active balance ( " Today 's Payoff Amount '' ) is {$16000.00}. Simultaneously, Capital One is actively furnishing a severely inflated balance of {$25000.00} to national credit reporting agencies ( XXXX and XXXX ), resulting in an active {$8300.00} reporting variance between the banks internal database and public credit repositories. SUMMARY OF LEGAL AND SYSTEMIC COMPLIANCE VIOLATIONS : 1. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Violation 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) The creditor is actively publishing a debt balance of {$25000.00} to public credit repositories while their own internal consumer application shows an active payoff balance of {$16000.00}. Under the FCRA, data furnishers are strictly mandated to maintain " maximum possible accuracy. '' Furnishing an outdated, unreconciled balance that overstates a consumer 's debt by more than {$8300.00} is a severe, actionable violation of credit reporting integrity. 2. Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) Article 9 Non-Compliance Under UCC Article 9 ( governing post-repossession liquidations and deficiencies ), a secured creditor is legally required to provide a mathematically accurate, commercially reasonable calculation of asset liquidation proceeds. Capital One can not establish a legally valid deficiency balance because its own records are fundamentally flawed : it claims a {$3900.00} asset sale in writing while only crediting the transaction ledger {$3200.00}. This {$650.00} discrepancy invalidates the baseline calculation of the alleged deficiency. 3. Unilateral Contract Alteration While the original signed contract mandates a strict 72-month amortization term, Capital One 's live digital infrastructure tracks and calculates this loan under a 73-month term. A financial institution can not unilaterally extend the term structure of a signed consumer contract without explicit consent. This structural deviation invalidates the integrity of all subsequent interest calculations, payoff schedules, and demanded balances. 4. Severe Systemic Profile Corruption The severe data corruption and mismatched balances on this account have completely broken online automated identity verification channels through national clearinghouses ( such as XXXX ), locking out the consumer and forcing slow, archaic mail-in paper verification processes. REMEDY REQUESTED : Because Capital One Auto Finance has demonstrably failed to maintain a single, historically accurate, or mathematically reconciled ledger and has unilaterally altered the contractual term structure, the integrity of this debt is completely compromised. The creditor is incapable of proving a legally sound " Sum Certain. '' I demand that Capital One Auto Finance be ordered to immediately cease all collection activities, cease furnishing conflicting data, and permanently delete and block this entire trade line from all consumer reporting agencies ( XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX ) to prevent ongoing consumer injury.

The caller ID displayed as a Wells Fargo phone number, and the caller possessed knowledge of my account activity, causing me to reasonably believe I was speaking with legitimate Wells Fargo personnel. I was informed that my account had been compromised and that I needed to immediately move funds as part of a fraud reversal and account security process intended to protect my account. Believing I was following legitimate fraud prevention instructions from Wells Fargo, I sent fourteen separate {$1000.00} XXXX XXXX transfers to a third party. During the same timeframe, an additional XXXX transaction for {$8900.00} ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ) was processed. I did not authorize this transaction, I do not recognize the merchant, and I did not receive any goods or services. I reported the fraud immediately upon realizing I had been deceived. Wells Fargos Response Wells Fargo repeatedly denied reimbursement and concluded there were allegedly no fraud indicators present. However, Wells Fargo simultaneously acknowledged in writing that I was the apparent victim of a Wells Fargo impersonator scheme. Additionally, Wells Fargo issued written notice dated XX/XX/year> stating that my account information may have been lost or stolen during the same timeframe as the disputed transactions. Wells Fargo later confirmed : the XXXX XXXX and XXXX claims were reviewed as related matters, the XX/XX/XXXX account compromise/lost-stolen notice related to these claims, and the account involved was closed and replaced after the incident. Despite these facts, Wells Fargo maintained that the transactions were authorized and directed me to pursue recovery directly through XXXX XXXX and XXXX. Why I Dispute Wells Fargos Determination This matter is not a simple merchant dispute. The transactions occurred only because I was deceived by an individual impersonating Wells Fargo while I believed I was protecting my account from fraud. Authorization obtained through impersonation, deception, urgency, and social engineering is not meaningful authorization. The following are clear fraud indicators that Wells Fargo acknowledged or should have considered : Spoofed Wells Fargo caller ID Impersonation of Wells Fargo fraud personnel Fourteen rapid consecutive {$1000.00} transfers Additional high-dollar XXXX transaction to an unfamiliar merchant Immediate reporting of the incident Wells Fargos written acknowledgment of an impersonation scheme Wells Fargos XX/XX/year> account compromise/lost-stolen notice Closure and replacement of the affected account I respectfully dispute Wells Fargos conclusion that there were no fraud indicators present. Requested Resolution I respectfully request that CFPB require Wells Fargo to : conduct a full independent review of these claims under Regulation E and the Electronic Fund Transfer Act, reconsider the classification of these transactions as authorized, explain specifically how Wells Fargo determined there were allegedly no fraud indicators, provide all documentation and evidence relied upon in denying the claims, and reimburse the disputed amount of {$22000.00}. I acted in good faith under the belief that I was communicating with Wells Fargo and taking steps to protect my account. Thank you for your time and consideration regarding this matter. XXXX XXXX

The attached exhibits also show small attempted transactions being declined while the account was near the {$300.00} limit, along with payment confirmations and posted-payment confirmations. Capital One declined transactions as low as approximately {$1.00}, {$1.00}, {$6.00}, {$7.00}, {$9.00}, {$12.00}, {$18.00}, {$24.00}, {$29.00}, {$30.00}, {$30.00}, and {$38.00}, repeatedly claiming that these transactions either would have put me over the {$300.00} credit limit or that the account was already over the {$300.00} credit limit. Formal Complaint and Request for Review Mishandling of Capital One Fraud Claim and Account Closure Chronological Timeline of Events Early XX/XX/year> : A debit card was reported missing after being inadvertently left behind at a bar in XXXX, MD. The cardholder immediately canceled the card with Capital One as missing or stolen. XX/XX/year> : Upon reviewing the account, an unauthorized {$20.00} ATM withdrawal and an attempted suspicious {$850.00} check deposit at a Capital One ATM near the bar were discovered. XX/XX/year> : After the check cleared, it was confirmed to be a stolen, altered check with the cardholders name fraudulently added. A fraud claim was promptly opened with Capital One, and all relevant details were provided. The cardholder also spoke directly with Capital Ones fraud prevention team. XX/XX/XXXX & XXXX, XXXX : The cardholder received brief email notifications : first, that the claim was closed, and then that it was denied due to authorization and/or participation in the transaction activity, implying complicity without evidence. XX/XX/year> : Capital One removed the {$850.00} provisional credit and closed the joint checking and savings accounts. XX/XX/year> : An in-person meeting was held with a Capital One Multi-Branch Manager, providing further documentation and a detailed timeline. The manager assured escalation of the matter. XXXX XXXX : Despite repeated follow-ups by phone and email ( most recently on XX/XX/XXXX ), no further response was received from the Branch Manager, the branch, or Capital One Corporate . Documentation of Bank Failures Lack of Communication : No substantive follow-up or explanation was provided after the claim denial, despite efforts to supply additional evidence and seek clarification. Unreasonable Investigation : The denial cited authorization and/or participation without considering clear evidence that the card was lost and used without the cardholders knowledge, and that the PIN could have been easily guessed due to its simplicity. Failure to Meet Legal Obligations : Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) and Regulation E, banks must conduct a reasonable investigation, provide written explanations for denials, and can not use consumer negligence ( such as an easily guessed PIN ) to increase liability or infer authorization. The burden of proof is on the bank to show the transaction was authorized, not on the consumer to prove otherwise.

narrative: I am submitting a new complaint regarding the banks handling of my unauthorized transaction claim because the banks prior response did not comply with RegulationE. This is not a duplicate complaint. This complaint concerns the banks procedural noncompliance, unsupported factual assertions, and failure to provide the documentation required under XXXX XXXX XXXX. In its denial letter, the bank stated that I confirmed the transactions via XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX and confirmed again by phone on XX/XX/XXXX, and that the transactions were authorized based on transaction and account history, location, and pattern of use. These are factual assertions that require supporting evidence. However, the bank did not provide the documentation required under RegulationE to support these claims. Specifically, the bank did not provide : SMS logs showing the alleged confirmation The actual call recording for the alleged XX/XX/XXXX call ( only a transcript was provided ) Authentication logs ( IP address, device, location, login data ) Internal investigation notes Merchant documentation Any evidence demonstrating that I actually authorized the transactions The bank did provide screenshots that appear to contain internal notes from a call in which they claim I confirmed the transactions, as well as a transcript of a call they assert reflects my confirmation. However, internal notes and a transcript are not the underlying evidence required to substantiate such a claim. Without the original call recording or authentication data, I can not verify the accuracy of the banks interpretation or meaningfully challenge its conclusion. Without access to the actual evidence, I can not meaningfully understand, evaluate, or appeal the banks determination. This is similar to being asked to respond to a decision in a legal proceeding without being given the evidence used to reach that decision. RegulationE requires the bank to provide copies of the documents it relied upon, and I am simply requesting the information necessary to review and respond to their findings. The only other documentation the bank provided was : ( 1 ) a list of transactions, which is not evidence of authorization, and ( 2 ) an outsourced Visa investigation packet for a single {$330.00} transaction. The XXXX packet does not satisfy the banks independent obligations under RegulationE and does not address the remaining disputed transactions. I also attempted to file a police report regarding the unauthorized transactions, but was informed that I could not do so because the merchant is based in XXXX XXXX and therefore outside the jurisdiction of local law enforcement. Although a police report is not required under RegulationE, I still made a goodfaith effort to obtain one. I am including this detail so the CFPB is aware that I attempted to provide every form of documentation reasonably available to me. In addition, I made a goodfaith effort to stabilize the account by moving my savings to cover approximately half of the overdraft created by the unauthorized transactions. I did this to prevent further fees and demonstrate that I was not attempting to avoid responsibility for the account while the dispute was pending. This situation has caused significant and ongoing stress, largely because I have been unable to obtain the evidence necessary to understand or respond to the banks determination. I have made every goodfaith effort to resolve the matter, but the lack of transparency has made it difficult to move forward. Finally, I am concerned that the bank issued provisional credit before completing its investigation. Under RegulationE, provisional credit is intended to protect consumers during an investigationnot to serve as a basis for later denying a claim without providing the required evidence. The sequence of events raises questions about whether the investigation was completed in a reasonable and compliant manner.

I am submitting this complaint regarding the handling of a fraudulent online transaction by both XXXX and Citibank and their subsequent failure to conduct a reasonable investigation despite being presented with evidence of fraud. I purchased XXXX watches from an online seller that had been recommended through XXXX 's platform. The seller represented that the items being sold were wristwatches. However, the watches were never delivered. Instead, I received small packages containing inexpensive tin toy rings that bore no resemblance to the merchandise purchased. Upon discovering the fraud, I promptly notified both XXXX and Citibank and disputed the charges. I explained that this type of scheme is a well-documented fraud commonly employed by overseas scammers. The seller ships a low-value item with a valid tracking number in order to create the appearance of delivery, while never shipping the product actually purchased. Despite my explanation and despite the obvious discrepancy between the goods ordered and the goods received, both XXXX and Citibank declined my disputes. Their decisions appeared to rely solely on the existence of tracking numbers rather than any meaningful investigation into whether the merchandise delivered matched the merchandise purchased. Neither institution requested photographs of the items received, sought evidence regarding the nature of the shipment, nor appeared to undertake any substantive review of the facts presented. Instead, they simply concluded that because a package had been delivered, the transaction was valid. In my view, this falls far short of the reasonable investigative standards that consumers should expect from financial institutions entrusted with handling fraud claims. As a result of their refusal to adequately investigate the matter, I closed my Citibank account and blocked further use of my XXXX account. I have since been subjected to collection threats for charges arising from what I believe to be a clear case of merchandise fraud. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate whether XXXX and Citibank fulfilled their obligations under applicable consumer protection laws and regulations, including their duties to conduct reasonable investigations of disputed transactions and claims of fraud. I further request that the disputed charges be reviewed and that any collection efforts associated with these transactions be suspended pending a proper investigation. I am prepared to provide supporting documentation, including transaction records, dispute correspondence, photographs of the items received, and any other evidence necessary to substantiate this complaint. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

narrative: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Complaint Company : Wells Fargo Bank Related Claim ID : XXXX Related Executive Escalation Reference : XXXX Related CFPB Complaint Reference : XXXX Complaint Category : Investigation Process / Complaint Handling / Inconsistent Findings Complaint Narrative : This complaint concerns Wells Fargo 's handling of the investigation process itself and the changing factual basis used to support denial of my fraud claim. My original complaint involved unauthorized debit-card transactions totaling approximately {$15000.00} including resulting fees. However, the focus of this complaint is not simply the denial of reimbursement. Rather, it concerns the consistency, accuracy, and reliability of the investigative process utilized to reach that determination. Throughout the handling of the matter, Wells Fargo systems and representatives reflected materially different transaction counts and records. During the course of the investigation, I was presented with approximately 27 transactions, 30 transactions, 35 transactions, and ultimately 39 disputed transactions identified through reconciliation efforts. Because the underlying disputed transaction records changed depending on the representative, department, or system being reviewed, I became concerned regarding the reliability of the data used to support the investigative conclusions. Additionally, Wells Fargo 's written denial specifically stated : " The shipping address provided to the merchant for the disputed transaction ( s ) matches your address on file. '' When I challenged that statement, I explained that the address maintained on file with Wells Fargo was my mother 's residence and that I do not routinely receive packages or merchandise shipments at that address and have not done so for years. Following that challenge, the explanation provided by Wells Fargo changed from shipping address matching to billing address matching. These are materially different facts. A shipping address concerns where merchandise is delivered. A billing address concerns payment verification. As a result, I am unable to determine which factual basis was actually relied upon during the investigation. I also received an executive-level review following my original CFPB complaint. During those discussions, I was advised that the claim had been denied. However, after being informed of the denial, I was then asked multiple additional investigative questions regarding possession of the card, possession of the PIN, access to the account, and related issues. This created additional confusion because it is unclear why substantive investigative questions were still being asked if the determination had already been finalized. Conversely, if the investigation remained ongoing, it is unclear how the matter could already be considered closed. Another concern involves the investigative factors relied upon to support denial. Wells Fargo repeatedly referenced factors including : Continued possession of the physical card ; Continued possession of the PIN ; Geographic similarity ; Merchant similarity ; Digital-card activity ; and Android-device activity. However, the matter also involved a documented impersonation event in which an individual posing as a Wells Fargo representative possessed substantial account-specific information, including personal identifying information and card-related information. During that impersonation event, I was advised that an alleged unauthorized user had been added to the account and was associated with a telephone number utilizing the same XXXX area code as my own number. This raises concerns regarding the degree of weight placed upon geographic-pattern analysis and other account-association indicators when evaluating sophisticated account-compromise scenarios. Additionally, Wells Fargo has repeatedly referenced digital-card and Android-device activity as a basis supporting denial. However, I have not been provided documentation explaining how Wells Fargo determined that the device involved belonged to me rather than an unauthorized actor possessing compromised account information. My concern is that several factors cited in support of denial appear to demonstrate association with an account rather than authorization by the account holder. I am requesting review of Wells Fargo 's investigative and complaint-handling process, including : inconsistent transaction records; changing factual explanations ; conflicting shipping-address and billing-address rationales ; post-denial investigative activity ; the factual basis supporting device attribution conclusions ; and whether the investigative methodology utilized was sufficiently reliable and internally consistent under the circumstances presented. Requested Resolution : I request an independent review of Wells Fargo 's investigative process, the factual basis relied upon in support of denial, and the consistency of the records and explanations provided throughout the handling of this matter. I also request that Wells Fargo be required to clearly identify the specific evidence relied upon to support its conclusions and address the inconsistencies outlined above.

I am filing this complaint because Citibanks billing dispute department mishandled a credit card dispute by failing to distinguish between an initial outbound delivery and a subsequent customer return. Furthermore, the bank closed the case without requesting documentation from me and has failed to respond to subsequent appeals containing definitive proof of return. The chronological facts of the transaction history are as follows : XX/XX/2026 : I incurred a charge of {$850.00} from XXXX XXXX XXXX for an order containing XXXX large items valued at {$420.00} each. XX/XX/2026 : I made a separate, unrelated purchase from the same merchant for a third item totaling {$420.00}. Subsequent Returns : All three items were initially delivered to my residence, but all three items were subsequently returned to the merchant. Due to the large physical size of the merchandise, each item required an individual return shipping label. I initiated a billing dispute for the XX/XX/XXXX charge of {$850.00} because the merchant failed to issue the appropriate refunds. Citibank subsequently closed the investigation in favor of the merchant. The bank stated that the merchant provided outbound tracking data confirming delivery to my residence, concluding that the merchandise remains in my possession. This conclusion represents a fundamental administrative error by Citibank. Outbound delivery confirmation merely establishes how the merchandise was originally received. It does not invalidate a legitimate " XXXX XXXX '' claim. The core of this dispute rests on the subsequent return shipments tracking back to the merchant 's possession. The comprehensive financial breakdown illustrates the unresolved discrepancy : XXXX XXXX XXXX : XXXX items at {$420.00} each, totaling {$1200.00}. Merchant Documentation : The merchant issued official email confirmations acknowledging the receipt and processing of returns for XXXX out of the XXXX items. They failed to issue a confirmation for the final item, despite tracking verifying its delivery to their warehouse. Credits Posted : My Citibank account statement reflects only XXXX single credit of {$420.00}, which posted on XX/XX/2026. XXXX XXXX XXXX : I am missing a total of {$850.00} in valid return credits. On XX/XX/2026, I submitted a formal appeal via email ( attached ) detailing this timeline and offering the official merchant return labels, distinct return tracking delivery receipts, and the merchants own return confirmations. To date, Citibank has not acknowledged or acted upon this correspondence, leaving the case closed without reviewing the evidentiary data. By allowing a merchant 's initial outbound shipping proof to override explicit evidence of a completed return, Citibank has failed to conduct a proper and reasonable investigation as outlined under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ). The merchant has retained both the returned merchandise and my funds.

I am filing this complaint against Wells Fargo for a violation of Regulation E ( 12 CFR 1005.6 ) and a failure to investigate unauthorized electronic fund transfers. THE FRAUD : A merchant identifying as " XXXX XXXX '' has been charging my debit card without my valid authorization. This merchant utilizes deceptive " dark patterns '' and " negative option billing '' to initiate recurring charges. According to CFPB Circular XXXX and Circular XXXX, transactions are classified as " unauthorized '' under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act when a consumer is misled into providing card information through deceptive marketing or fraudulent misrepresentation. THE BANK 'S REFUSAL : I contacted Wells Fargo on XX/XX/year> to report these unauthorized charges. I spoke with Manager XXXX ( XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX ). I requested a full investigation and refund of all fraudulent charges. Manager XXXX refused to open a claim or investigate any transactions older than 120 days. He stated that bank policy and " card network rules '' ( Visa/XXXX ) prevent the bank from assisting with any charges beyond that 120-day window. THE VIOLATION : Internal bank policies and card network chargeback rules do NOT override my federal protections under Regulation E. Under 12 CFR 1005.6, my liability for unauthorized transfers is capped, and the bank has a legal duty to investigate. While there is a 60-day reporting window following a statement, the bank remains liable for unauthorized transfers that occurred prior to the 60th day after the statement was sent. By applying a blanket 120-day " system limit '' to a claim for unauthorized fraud, Wells Fargo is willfully ignoring its obligations under federal law and is denying me the protections guaranteed by the Electronic Fund Transfer Act. RESOLUTION REQUESTED : I am requesting that Wells Fargo immediately perform a full investigation into all charges from " XXXX XXXX '' and provide a full reimbursement for all unauthorized funds stolen from my account, regardless of the 120-day network rule.

I am reporting misconduct by Chase, the national bank and credit card issuer that is part of JPMorgan Chase. What started as a dispute over a {$5.00} Chase merchant offer for a pet-food order I made for my mother 's cats has turned into months of stonewalling, misrepresentation of terms and conditions, digging in of heels with blatant dishonesty, and even hostility on the part of Chase customer service. This is no longer about {$5.00}. This is about a bank that refuses to do the right thing despite numerous reasonable attempts by the customer, even when the bank 's deception has been laid bare. Several months ago, I was perusing merchant offers available for my Chase credit card. I saw there were two offers available that applied to the same merchant. One offered {$10.00} cash back for spending {$50.00} or more at XXXX, and the other offered {$5.00} cash back for doing the same. Because I had not seen Chase simultaneously provide multiple offers for the same merchant before, I did the responsible thing and carefully read the terms and conditions to determine if combining offers was disallowed. The fine print said nothing about that, so I saved both offers and proceeded with a XXXX order that met the criteria. But I received only the {$10.00} credit. The {$5.00} credit remained missing. I contacted Chase customer service about this error, and what followed has been a months-long stream of lies and nonsensical claims with some hostility sprinkled in -- and the stunning willingness to burn decades of customer goodwill -- all over {$5.00} when Chase is XXXX in the wrong. The crux of their argument is that an excerpt from the merchant-offer terms and conditions that states " Offer valid XXXX time only '' means multiple offers can not be combined. That is an obvious lie, as no reasonable person would read it that way. " Offer valid XXXX time only '' is standard merchant-offer language that means an offer can't be used repeatedly on multiple purchases. It means nothing about multiple offers applying to a single purchase. I have explained this to customer service many times now. Further, Chase has repeatedly stated that they can not issue me the missing {$5.00} credit, even as a " goodwill gesture, '' because they have to treat all customers equitably. I have replied that I am not asking for special treatment, because any cardholder who had both offers saved should have received both credits. I have repeatedly explained the simple remedy : revise future merchant-offer language to explicitly state that offers can not be combined. I will honor and respect what is clearly written in the terms and conditions. But because that language was not included in these offers at the time I used them, Chase owes me the missing {$5.00} credit. But as I said at the beginning, this isn't about {$5.00} ; it's about accountability, transparency, and decency. This is about a bank claiming their terms and conditions state something they clearly don't, and when that lie is called out, repeatedly doubling down on it rather than admitting the obvious truth, making amends, and revising future offer language to reflect their intent. Worse, one of my early attempts to resolve this was via a phone conversation with an agent on the Chase " escalation team '' who literally hung up on me mid-sentence while I calmly pushed back on his attempts to gaslight me with the claim that " Offer valid one time only '' means " Offers can not be combined. '' I know it was not a dropped call because I heard him talking over me and saying he was going to hang up. That's shockingly unacceptable unprofessional behavior from any organization towards a customer who is firmly but calmly making their case and refusing to accept a lie. I have mentioned this incident multiple times in my subsequent messages to Chase customer service, and it has not even been clearly acknowledged, let alone apologized for. That alone is incredible. If all of this reflects how Chase does business and trains their customer-facing employees, it reflects a systemic problem at the XXXX of the company. The fact that they are willing to exhibit such ugly behavior over a mere {$5.00} only highlights the sheer absurdity. I certainly wouldn't trust them to handle anything of greater value.
