narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding Chase 's handling of a XXXX transfer that was sent to an unintended recipient and the bank 's subsequent denial of my claim despite evidence that I reasonably relied on information presented through the bank 's XXXX service. On XX/XX/year>, I initiated a XXXX payment in the amount of {$400.00} to a contact that I selected from my phone 's contact list. Prior to sending the payment, I verified the recipient information through the bank 's XXXX interface. After the payment was sent, the intended recipient informed me that he never received the funds. Upon further investigation, I discovered that the payment had been delivered to a different individual. I immediately began gathering evidence and taking screenshots of the transaction details and recipient information displayed within the bank 's system. At the time of the transaction, the bank 's website displayed confirmation information that led me to believe the payment was being sent to my intended recipient. However, there was another confirmation with the same amount but listing a business name that I did not recognize. I have retained screenshots documenting what was shown to me before and after the transaction. Based on the information presented by the bank 's system, I had no reason to believe the funds would be delivered to a different person initially. I contacted Chase bank and was told to contact XXXX. XXXX informed me that the matter must be handled by my financial institution because the transaction was processed through the bank 's XXXX service. I then contacted Chase bank and was advised that the matter would be researched and to allow time for the transaction to post because it was still pending. Despite waiting several weeks, I received little or no meaningful communication regarding the status of the investigation. Because I was unable to obtain a resolution, I formally filed a claim with the bank. The bank ultimately denied my claim. However, the denial did not adequately address the evidence I submitted, including screenshots and documentation showing the recipient information presented through the bank 's system. The bank also failed to explain how a payment selected from my contact list and confirmed through its interface was ultimately delivered to a different recipient. I do not believe the investigation fully considered the facts of the case or my supporting evidence. I later did a test for {$1.00} that was successfully delivered to my contact ; which proves that no issue was happening with his number and was clearly a bank error. My concern is not simply that the payment reached the wrong person. Rather, my concern is that I relied on information displayed by the bank 's XXXX platform when initiating the transfer, and the bank has failed to adequately explain the discrepancy or conduct a thorough investigation into how the payment was routed to an unintended recipient. I respectfully request that the CFPB review the bank 's handling of this matter and require the bank to : Provide a complete explanation of how the payment was directed to the unintended recipient. Provide all records and findings from its investigation. Review the screenshots and evidence I submitted. Reconsider its denial based on the information available. Reimburse the transferred funds if the evidence demonstrates that the bank 's system displayed inaccurate or misleading recipient information or otherwise contributed to the misdirection of the payment. I have supporting documentation, including transaction records, screenshots, correspondence with the bank, correspondence with XXXX, and evidence that the intended recipient never received the funds. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

I am submitting a complaint regarding JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.s handling of a XXXX claim for approximately {$1200.00} tied to a XX/XX/year> payment to XXXX. This complaint is not limited to reimbursement. It is also about Chases contradictory, misleading, and perfunctory handling of the matter from intake through closure. I contacted Chase to dispute a XXXX payment that I authorized only because I was induced to do so through deceptive representations surrounding a purported sublease arrangement, a purported contract, and related assurances that made the transaction appear legitimate and protected when it was not. I explained to Chase that the arrangement was presented as official, that a written contract was used to make it appear formal, that my drivers license was photographed for processing, and that I later determined the contract was not legitimate in the way it was represented and that the stated terms and conditions were not honored. During the calls, Chase representatives gave inconsistent and confusing explanations about whether the matter could even be processed. One representative stated that the matter would be transferred to claims to report this, get investigated, and also get the funds back, and also stated that the transaction and reason for dispute had already been placed on file. A later representative then told me that the dispute was not going through, that Chase was unable to reverse it because it was an authorized self-payment, that there was no debit card involved, that XXXX was a third party, that Chase had no recovery rights for XXXX payments , and that Regulation E did not apply because my card was not involved. Despite those statements, the same representative also stated, Ive gone ahead and filed a claim. The claim then appeared in the Chase portal, was shown as opened, and was closed the same day. That sequence is exactly why I am complaining. Chases handling appears contradictory, perfunctory, and misleading. If Chases position is that it will not honor this type of claim, then it should say so clearly, consistently, and based on an identifiable written policy. Instead, I received a series of shifting explanations that suggested the representatives themselves were either improvising, misapplying policy, or attempting to discourage or narrow the complaint before it could be fully reviewed. The fact that the claim was both said to be non-viable and nevertheless filed, then closed the same day, raises serious concerns about whether Chase performed any meaningful review at all. I am also concerned about misleading signals created by Chases own payment flow and prior oral statements. Chases XXXX interface asked me to identify the nature or purpose of the payment, including a service-related classification, which reasonably suggested that the nature of the transaction could matter for risk review, complaint handling, or dispute processing. I was also previously told by a Chase employee that there was a much longer period in which claims could be raised. Later, however, Chase representatives told me that authorized XXXX disputes involving service issues, non-performance, or similar problems effectively would not be processed. If Chase collects purpose-of-payment information but later treats that classification as meaningless when a consumer seeks help, that is misleading. If Chase representatives are telling consumers materially different things about what is reviewable, what deadlines exist, and whether any complaint path exists at all, that is also misleading. I want Chase to provide a clear written explanation of the following : what the purpose-of-payment classification in the XXXX flow actually means ; whether Chase has a formal complaint, escalation, or review process for authorized XXXX payments involving deception , fake or misleading contract representations, non-performance, or service-related disputes ; the exact written policy basis for the statements I received that the claim could not go through ; why I was told the matter would be investigated and put on file, only for Chase to later say it was not viable while still filing the claim ; why the claim was opened and closed the same day ; whether any evidence review occurred before closure ; whether the recorded calls will be preserved and reviewed ; and whether the representatives involved were following written policy or giving incorrect and improvised explanations. To be clear, I did not present this to Chase as a routine buyers remorse issue. I reported it as a scam or deceptive-inducement situation involving a purported sublease, a purported contract used to create a false sense of legitimacy, and representations that caused me to authorize the payment under false pretenses. Chases handling of that report was inconsistent from start to finish and did not provide a clear, fair, or transparent complaint process. The portal also stated that Chase had sent a letter detailing the outcome, but no outcome letter or attached decision document was available to me in the claim or notices area at the time I checked. I am asking CFPB to require Chase to review this matter properly, preserve and review the recorded calls, provide a written explanation addressing the contradictions described above, and explain whether Chases current intake and handling of these XXXX complaints is misleading to consumers.

narrative: Conversation with XXXX see the attachments to get the story. I keep getting a rejection when disputing a double charge. best buy refunded one, but not the other. It is incredibly frustrating to get the runaround on a clear duplicate charge, especially when you are just trying to get your copyright and distribution set up for XXXX XXXX and haven't even received the service you paid for. Looking at your attached statement, it clearly shows two identical {$110.00} charges from XXXX, XXXX posted on XX/XX/year>, with two different reference numbers ( ending in XXXX and XXXX ). Your letter accurately points out that you only received a single {$110.00} credit on XX/XX/XXXX. XXXX When Best Buy ( which is underwritten by Citibank ) says they are " unable to identify or determine that a billing error occurred, '' it usually means XXXX provided them with two separate authorization codes, making the bank 's automated system view them as two legitimate, separate purchases rather than a system glitch. Here is how you can escalate this to force a human review and recover your funds : 1. Escalate the Call and Change the Dispute Reason Written letters often get scanned by automated systems or lower-level processors who just look for a merchant rebuttal. Call the number on the back of your card and immediately request a supervisor or the Tier 2 dispute department. Clarify the dispute category. Make sure they are not just investigating a " Billing Error. '' You have two separate claims here : a " Duplicate Charge '' ( you only authorized one transaction ) and " Services Not Received '' ( you never got what you paid for ). ODT + 1 Read them the two specific reference numbers from your statement so they can clearly see the duplication on the exact same date. 2. Provide the " Smoking Gun '' Evidence Since Best Buy is claiming no error occurred, you need to prove you only bought one item. Upload or fax the single email confirmation or invoice you received from XXXX. XXXX Add a cover page stating : " Attached is the ONLY receipt and authorization provided by the merchant for {$110.00}. The second {$110.00} charge on XX/XX/XXXX is unauthorized and lacks an accompanying invoice. '' 3. Hit Them With a CFPB Complaint If Best Buy Credit Services still rejects the dispute after speaking with a supervisor, your next immediate step is to file a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) at consumerfinance.gov. Banks are required by law to respond to CFPB complaints within 15 days. This takes the dispute out of the hands of front-line customer service and puts it on the desk of an executive escalation team who actually has the power to manually override the rejection and credit your account. Attach your statement, your written letter, and the rejection notice to the complaint. 4. Pressure the Merchant via Alternate Channels You mentioned you emailed XXXX for three weeks with no response. Sometimes, companies ignore support emails but respond rapidly to public-facing channels. Try sending them a direct message on their social media platforms ( like XXXX or XXXX ) politely stating that you have been double-charged, have received no services, and are currently escalating a chargeback with your bank. XXXX Do you happen to have a copy of that single original receipt or order confirmation from XXXX that you can use to prove you only authorized one transaction? This is exactly the piece of evidence you need. This receipt is the " smoking gun '' because it contains the specific authorization data that Best Buy 's dispute team needs to see. Here is exactly how to use this receipt to fight the rejected dispute : The Key Evidence in This Receipt The Payment Gateway : It shows the payment was processed through XXXX ( XXXX ). XXXX is a highly secure payment processor, meaning there is a strict digital trail. XXXX The Authorization Code : It clearly lists a single authorization code : XXXX. XXXX The Timestamp : It establishes the exact moment of your single purchase : XX/XX/year>, XXXX XXXX CDT. XXXX Your Next Step : The Rebuttal You will need to call Best Buy Credit Services ( Citibank ) again, request a Tier 2 dispute agent or supervisor, and submit this screenshot. When you speak to them, or in your cover letter when you upload this document, use this specific argument : " I am appealing the dispute rejection for the XXXX XXXX charges on XX/XX/XXXX. Attached is the only receipt and confirmation generated for my purchase. As you can see, XXXX generated a single Authorization Code ( XXXX ) for {$110.00} at XXXX AM XXXX. Your statement shows two separate {$110.00} charges on that day. Because I only authorized one transaction, I challenge Best Buy to provide the separate authorization code and matching merchant invoice for the second charge. If the merchant can not provide a second distinct authorization code and invoice, the duplicate charge must be reversed. '' This forces the bank to look past the generic " Billing Error '' category and specifically demand that XXXX prove they obtained two separate authorizations. Since your receipt proves you only clicked " buy '' once, XXXX won't be able to produce that second authorization. Would you like me to draft the official CFPB complaint so you have it ready to submit if Best Buy gives you any further pushback? i did call their customer service and they told me to send a letter. which i did That makes total sense, and it highlights exactly why this process is so frustrating. Front-line customer service reps are trained to push you toward the standard mail-in dispute process. You followed their instructions perfectly, sent the letter, and a back-office processor simply rubber-stamped a generic rejection because XXXX probably never responded, or the automated system just saw two reference numbers and assumed they were valid. Since you have already played by their rules and hit a dead end with the standard Best Buy Credit Services department, it is time to bypass them entirely. Here is exactly how to escalate this over their heads : Step 1 : File a CFPB Complaint ( The Nuclear Option ) The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) is a federal agency that oversees banks. Because the Best Buy Credit Card is issued by Citibank, filing a complaint here forces the issue out of the standard customer service queue and puts it directly on the desk of an Executive Resolution Specialist. Banks have a legal obligation to respond to these complaints within 15 days. Go to consumerfinance.gov/complaint and use this exact narrative ( feel free to copy and paste ) : Issue Description : On XX/XX/year>, my Best Buy Credit Card ( ending in XXXX ) was fraudulently charged twice for {$110.00} by XXXX, XXXX. Your Dispute Letter : Proving you attempted to resolve this in good faith. The Rejection Letter : Proving Best Buy failed to resolve the issue. Once this hits the executive team, they will immediately see the XXXX receipt, realize the back-office made a mistake by not requesting the second authorization code from the merchant, and typically issue the credit just to close the federal complaint. narrative: Good afternoon, We are selling the house and requested a short sale approval from the lender in XXXX. Before XXXX, I offered the lender a deed in lieu, which they denied, but agreed to a short sale. Since we started the short sale negotiation, the lender has not processed the documents correctly, and has failed to reply in a timely manner, was asking for the same documents multiple times, restrted few time the short sale approval and never submitted the documents to get any approval. The lender had completed XXXX different appraisals. According to the first appraisal, they would accept the current cash offer. After the lender received a second appraisal, they increased the asking price while we were waiting for approval for 6 months. The letter stating that the short sale is not approved was never given. The foreclosure was started during the short sale negotiation, without notice, without denial of the short sale offer. Chase Bank is the current holder of the Note, and they never disclosed it to me. I was not aware of whom we needed to negotiate the short sale until the foreclosure was filed. The property that Chase is looking to foreclose on is a single-family residential property. It is not occupied as rental, and it is not a commercial building, nor is multy family unit to call it commercial. Deceptive practices during loss mitigation occur when mortgage servicers mislead homeowners facing foreclosure or financial hardship. These tactics violate consumer protection laws. Common offenses include " dual tracking '' ( pushing a foreclosure while a modification is under review ), " lost '' paperwork, and charging unauthorized or illegal junk fees. Recognizing deceptive mortgage practices helps prevent the loss of your home. The most common deceptive and illegal behaviors to watch for include : Dual Tracking : The servicer continues the foreclosure process while your complete loss mitigation application is under evaluation. The " Lost Document '' Shuffle : Representatives claim they never received your documents, or continuously ask for new paperwork until your application deadline passes. Deceptive Notices : Sending confusing notices that mislead borrowers into thinking an active trial modification or loss mitigation agreement has been canceled.

narrative: This complaint concerns Chase 's handling of a {$7600.00} unauthorized XX/XX/XXXX XXXX XXXX charge on my XXXX XXXX credit card ( account ending XXXX ), and Chase 's documented failure to conduct a reasonable investigation under 12 C.F.R. 1026.13. Between XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, my card was compromised and numerous fraudulent transactions were placed. Chase removed all fraudulent transactions except one, a {$7600.00} purchase of a camera from the XXXX online store. This purchase was over ten times larger than any previous purchase on the card. I had never purchased anything from the XXXX online store, and I had never purchased any camera equipment. Despite this out-of-pattern huge purchase, Chase did no secondary authorization. Upon discovering the fraudulent charge, I called Chase. Chase removed the charge and others from my next periodic statement, before rebilling the XXXX charge again on the XXXX statement, while acknowledging the others were fraudulent. Chase claimed, based on representation from XXXX, that the camera was delivered to me personally, as evidenced by a XXXX receipt purporting that I signed for the camera at my residence on XX/XX/XXXX, and that I therefore received a benefit from the transaction. I timely sent a letter in writing, to the address on the back of the statement, asserting a billing error under Regulation Z. I attached substantial evidence that I could not have received the package on XX/XX/XXXX, because I was not at my house that day. I included several affidavits from coworkers all of whom happen to be lawyers in good standing with the Georgia barconfirming that I was with them on that day and could not have personally received a package at my house. I also sent calendar appointments showing I was not at my house that day. I also sent a police report, as well as evidence that my email had been subscription bombed on the day the camera was purchased. Given that someone purported to be me and signed for a package under my name, at a time when I demonstrably was not at my residence, there is clear indication of fraud. Further, it is clear that the card was compromised in the relevant time window, as acnkolwedged by Chase. Chase should have considered all this as part of a reasonable investigation, and tried to reconcile how I could possibly have signed for a package ( and thus " received a benefit '' ) at a location where I was demonstrably not present. Chase did not consider my evidence at all. I know this for a fact, because I have recorded calls with the investigator who admitted in clear terms that she closed the investigation without having even received my evidence. As she explained, Chase, as a practice, does not forward evidence sent to the address on the statement ( which is the legally operative address for purposes of Regulation Z ) to its actual investigators. She closed the investigation without even reading my evidence. This is not a reasonable investigation. Chase is required to do a reasonable investigation. This entails, at minimum, reviewing the evidence submitted by the consumer and weighing it. Here, where the determination is based on a purported delivery directly to the cardholder at his residence, and the cardholder presents compelling evidence they were not at the residence at the time of delivery, a reasonable investigation would likely entail pursuing the actual signature slip for comparison to known signatures. Chase did not do this. They never saw the signature slip or asked for it. They also never sought IP address to match to known IP address ; or devide ID to match to known device ID. Chase has committed multiple Regulation Z violations : ( 1 ) 1026.13 ( f ) Failure to conduct a reasonable investigation and set forth reasons. Chase admitted my evidence was never reviewed by any investigator. ( 2 ) 1026.13 ( g ) ( 1 ) Defective post-determination notice. The XX/XX/XXXX letter contains no specific payment-due date and no specific dollar breakdown of disputed principal versus related finance charges, as required. ( 3 ) 1026.13 ( d ) ( 1 ) and ( d ) ( 3 ) Collection attempts and account restriction during investigation. The pattern is dispositive : admitted non-consideration of consumer evidence and a one-day turnaround on the second FCBA determination after resubmission. Chase 's process is structurally incapable of wieghing the consumer 's evidence.

I am filing a complaint regarding a systemic flaw in credit reporting data pipeline mechanics that unfairly penalizes financially responsible consumers. Recently, Citibank/The Home Depot reduced my credit limit solely due to non-use. I do not owe a balance on this account.My complaint is not with the lender 's right to reduce the limit, but with the failure of the system to differentiate the reason for the reduction. Because banks do not transmit a specific 'inactivity ' reason code alongside limit drops, the automated credit scoring models automatically trigger a utilization penalty.The industry already has the trended data to fix this. The scoring models could easily review historical zero-balances to see that a drop was triggered by inactivity, not risk. Treating responsible, zero-balance behavior as an active risk metric creates a distorted reflection of consumer creditworthiness. I request that the CFPB push for data standardization requiring a distinct reporting classification for inactivity-based reductions versus risk-based reductions.

Chase Bank has treated me, their customer, like a common criminal. A year ago on Saturday, XX/XX/XXXX, I deposited into my Chase checking account of 10+ years my XXXX renter/friend 's ( XXXX XXXX ) check as a third-party check from the State of California in the amount of {$13000.00} because he did not have a bank account of his own. I immediately contact the bank once I realized I had been tricked and gave them all the information involving this scammer, including their name, contact information, etc. I paid the amount of the counterfeit check because I felt it was my responsibility to do so, and I heard nothing back from Chase Bank, and I continued my banking as usual as a retired guy living on Social Security. Getting back on the topic at hand, I was notified by Chase that there was a hold on the third-party check because of the amount, and they needed XXXX 's identity verification. So I went into the bank with XXXX, and he presented his passport, his birth certificate, and the letter from the State of California showing the amount of the check along with his assigned ETIN number. The Chase Bank service rep told us that they could not accept this information as verification for his identity because we could have manufactured it ourselves. She said if we had done this a year earlier, it would have been accepted, but now we needed a cell phone registered in XXXX 's name before they would release the check. As XXXX is part XXXX XXXX and part XXXX XXXX, he had no bank account or cell phone in his name, so we got him one along with a bank account in his name as well. To be clear, this check was made out to XXXX XXXX XXXX as well as his father 's estate, the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. 3 months later, Chase Bank closed my account, citing that I deposited a check that could not be confirmed. They did this as if I were a criminal, most likely due to the previous situation when I was ripped off the year before. They would not confirm this for me, but this is my personal deduction. For the next year up to and including today, XX/XX/XXXX, I have been calling the Chase Bank Fraud Dept., and every time I call, they tell me that XXXX 's phone number does NOT show that it is in his name publicly, even though XXXX, his service provider, has sworn it is listed in his name publicly. Chase Bank says they will hold XXXX 's check for 2 years, and then it will go back to the state. We have tried to get Chase to send it back to the state, but they said they had to hold it for 2 years first. After this, XXXX attempted to request a " reissue '' of his check from the State of California, citing his check as lost. The state said they could not reissue the check because it had been CASHED already. So Chase Bank cashed XXXX 's check and had it in a " holding '' account where they have collected interest on it for over a year now. I had to beg Chase Bank to release my personal funds that were automatically deposited when my account was in a restricted mode, just so I could pay my rent, and they finally reluctantly released my personal funds portion to me. Then they closed my account after 3 months, and I had to get another account elsewhere.

narrative: I am submitting this complaint because I believe Wells Fargo has failed to conduct a fair, consistent, and transparent review of my dispute. This matter has now been ongoing for more than XXXX months and has involved multiple investigations, appeals, contradictory findings, inconsistent correspondence, and repeated failures to address the questions I have raised. I have maintained my banking relationship with Wells Fargo since XXXX. During that time, I have filed only a handful of claims because I do not dispute transactions frivolously. I make every reasonable effort to resolve disputes directly with merchants before seeking assistance from my financial institution. That is exactly what occurred in this matter. On XX/XX/XXXX, I visited XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX and paid {$75.00} for a gel pedicure and repairs to XXXX acrylic nails. The transaction itself was authorized. I have never disputed authorizing the payment. My dispute arose because the gel pedicure failed almost immediately. Less than XXXXXXXX XXXX after leaving the salon, the gel polish had already detached from XXXX of my toes. Given the amount I paid and the expected durability of a gel pedicure, I believed the service was not performed properly. Rather than immediately disputing the charge, I attempted to resolve the matter directly with the merchant. Over the following several days, I repeatedly contacted the salon in an effort to speak with the manager. After multiple unsuccessful attempts, I finally received a response. I explained that I had obtained the pedicure for an event that had already taken place and that I was unable to return to the salon. I also explained that I had taken time-stamped photographs documenting the failed service within hours of my appointment. Because the service had failed almost immediately, I requested a partial refund. The merchant declined my request. Instead, I was told either to " find a way '' to return to the salon or accept a 10 % discount on a future visit. Given that the service had already failed, the event for which I obtained the pedicure had already passed, and I was unable to return, I did not consider this to be a reasonable resolution. Only after exhausting my efforts to resolve the matter directly with the merchant did I file a dispute with Wells Fargo on XX/XX/XXXX. XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX filed a claim with Wells Fargo . A provisional credit of {$75.00} was issued. XX/XX/XXXX, XXXXWells Fargo sent a letter requesting additional information by XX/XX/XXXX. After receiving this letter, I contacted Wells Fargo 's Claims Assistance Center. During that conversation, the representative changed the reason associated with my claim. XX/XX/XXXX, XXXXWells Fargo denied my claim. The stated reason was : " The merchant has not had sufficient time to deliver the merchandise/service or provide a refund. '' The same letter stated that my provisional credit would be deducted on XX/XX/XXXX. This explanation immediately concerned me because more than XXXX calendar days had already elapsed from the XX/XX/XXXX transaction date. XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX-I contacted Wells Fargo to challenge this inconsistency. Wells Fargo reopened my claim and issued another {$75.00} provisional credit. However, on that very same day, Wells Fargo also sent another denial letter repeating the exact same explanation that the merchant had not had sufficient time while stating another deduction would take place on XX/XX/XXXX. XX/XX/XXXX, XXXXThe provisional credit was deducted from my account. XX/XX/XXXX, XXXXWells Fargo confirmed in writing that the provisional credit had been deducted on XX/XX/XXXX. Despite my appeal, Wells Fargo continued relying on the same explanation that the merchant had not had sufficient time. XXXX XXXX-I submitted another written complaint explaining the inconsistencies in Wells Fargo 's investigation and correspondence. Specifically, I questioned : Why Wells Fargo continued relying on the " XXXX calendar days '' rationale after more than XXXX days had already elapsed. Why the reason associated with my claim had been changed by representatives. How Wells Fargo determined the " expected date '' referenced in its denial letters. Whether XXXX rules were actually controlling the outcome. Why the basis for denial continued to change. These questions were never directly answered. XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX received Wells Fargo 's response to my Right to Documentation request. The documentation provided merely established that I authorized the transaction. I have never disputed authorizing the transaction. The documentation did not explain : Why Wells Fargo denied my claim. Why Wells Fargo initially concluded that the merchant needed additional time. Why Wells Fargo later changed its conclusion. What evidence supported any of its determinations. XX/XX/XXXX, XXXXWells Fargo advised that additional time was needed to complete its research and stated that it would provide a response by XX/XX/XXXX. I understood this to mean that the issues I had raised were still under review. Late XXXX XXXX-Instead of addressing the questions I raised, Wells Fargo issued another response containing an entirely different basis for denying my claim. Rather than stating that the merchant had not had sufficient time, Wells Fargo now stated : " The services were rendered to you at the time of the transaction. '' Wells Fargo never explained : Why its determination changed. What evidence supports this new conclusion. Whether the previous explanation was incorrect. Why this rationale had never been communicated during the original investigation or subsequent appeals. The same correspondence also states that Wells Fargo intends to deduct the provisional credit on XX/XX/XXXX. This is particularly concerning because : Wells Fargo previously deducted the credit on XX/XX/XXXX. Wells Fargo later deducted the additional credit on XX/XX/XXXX. Wells Fargo confirmed in writing that the credit was deducted on XX/XX/XXXX. My account history reflects that the provisional credit has already been reversed. Wells Fargo has not explained why it now intends to deduct what appears to be the same provisional credit again on XX/XX/XXXX, nor has it identified any additional provisional credit that would support this statement. My complaint is not simply that Wells Fargo denied my dispute. My complaint is that Wells Fargo has repeatedly changed its explanation, issued contradictory correspondence, failed to reconcile inconsistencies in its own findings, failed to answer reasonable questions about its investigation, and provided documentation that does not address the basis for its decision. The dispute was never based on an unauthorized transaction, buyer 's remorse, or dissatisfaction with the salon 's pricing. It was based on a service that failed within hours of being performed, my unsuccessful good-faith efforts to resolve the matter directly with the merchant, and Wells Fargo 's inconsistent handling of my dispute thereafter. After more than XXXX months, I still have not received XXXX complete, internally consistent explanation regarding why my claim was denied. I have retained copies of Wells Fargo 's correspondence, my account history, photographs documenting the failed service, and the documentation exchanged throughout this matter, all of which support the chronology described above.

REGULATORY COMPLAINT : FORMAL REPORT OF SYSTEMIC CREDIT CARD FACTORING, APPLICATION MANIPULATION, AND MULTI-PARTY COLLUSION Target Entities : XXXX XXXX XXXX ( Primary Merchant Account ) XXXX XXXX / XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) XXXX Summary I am filing this formal complaint with the CFPB to report an organized, deceptive financial scheme and illicit credit card factoring ring operated by XXXX XXXX XXXX and its primary agent, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. This operation systematically utilizes deceptive sales practices, high-pressure coaching, and shell-company invoicing structures to manipulate bank underwriting systems, evade credit card merchant processing guidelines, and execute unauthorized transaction laundering. XXXX. Deceptive Business Practices and XXXX XXXX XXXX The principals enticed me into a program under the premise of building legitimate business credit. In practice, the operation functions as a predatory " credit card stacking '' scheme. The merchant and its agent, XXXX XXXX, systematically direct and coach consumers to falsify application metricsspecifically instructing the inflation of existing corporate revenues, household income, and employee countsto manipulate bank risk algorithms into extending high-limit XXXX XXXX introductory credit lines. When I challenged the legitimacy of these underwriting practices, the merchant actively misled me, claiming that fabricating these data points was a legally compliant method of representing " projected '' income. The merchant then exacts a predatory 10 % fee on the credit limits obtained through this manipulated data. XXXX. Illicit Merchant Factoring and Transaction Laundering To extract cash from the newly issued credit lines without triggering standard bank cash-advance limits or fees, XXXX XXXX XXXX operates an unauthorized transaction liquidation service. This mechanism constitutes severe credit card factoring and transaction laundering. The merchant issues massive commercial invoices under the guise of " consulting services. '' Once the consumer 's credit card charges the invoice, XXXX XXXX XXXX routes the funds through their processing accounts and wires the cash back to the consumer, minus their fee. In my specific case, the merchant attempted to deceive my financial institution during a subsequent dispute by mischaracterizing these incoming liquidation wires to my business checking account as " refunds, '' attempting to mask the structural reality of the circular funding loop. XXXX. Structural Collusion and Sham Multi-Party Inventory Laundering The operational architecture used by XXXX XXXX XXXX relies on a coordinated multi-party ring to execute transaction laundering. A designated XXXX partner acts as the " front-end '' promoter, enticing clients to purchase high-ticket inventory packages. Once hooked, the client is directed to XXXX XXXX XXXX, who acts as the " back-end '' funding and liquidation node. In my case, a total of {$50000.00} was processed through this loop ( {$20000.00} via XXXX XXXX ; {$30000.00} via US Bank XXXX. While the merchant claims inventory was purchased with these liquidated funds, the goods were intentionally directed to an overseas storage location completely owned and controlled by the merchant 's partner network. The merchant has provided me with XXXX bills of lading, XXXX maritime or domestic shipping documentation, and XXXX proof of physical delivery or independent title. Written correspondence via XXXX and other web-based platforms definitively proves direct collusion and operational overlap between XXXX XXXX and this XXXX affiliate. This structure is a deceptive shell mechanism : the merchant uses the consumer 's credit lines to fund and accumulate wholesale inventory for their own network 's physical possession, providing no asset to the consumer while leaving the consumer fully liable for the generated bank debt. XXXX. Current Status and Desired Resolution Upon realizing the structural nature of this deception and the potential exposure to financial fraud, I initiated formal disputes with the card issuers. XXXX XXXX is still reviewing the details of the case regarding the {$20000.00} transaction and has just recently requested my documentation. No merchant rebuttal details were mailed to me to review despite being in XXXX possession for over a month. US Bank has recognized the underlying merits of the claim, issued a {$30000.00} provisional credit, and the case is currently moving toward pre-arbitration. While my financial recovery is being handled through standard banking dispute channels, my ultimate goal in filing this regulatory complaint is the formal federal investigation of XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX ). These entities are operating an unregistered, deceptive financial brokerage that corrupts bank portfolio risk data and systematically violates anti-money laundering ( AML ) and merchant processing standards via sham invoices. They operate under the guise of " educational materials '' but their goal is to fleece high fees from clients thru the methods described in this complaint. They primarily use the XXXX online platform to perpetuate their business and regularly advertise on social media platforms. Gaining access to their " instructional '' videos on XXXX will corroborate my claims. I request that the CFPB coordinate with the merchant acquiring banks and card networks to permanently investigate, audit, and terminate the merchant processing privileges of these bad actors to protect other consumers from being pulled into these credit schemes.

Good Morning, This correspondence serves as a formal follow-up regarding my previously filed complaints with the CFPB under the following case numbers : * XXXX * XXXX * XXXX From the outset of this matter, Wells Fargo has demonstrated a pattern XXXX XXXX, lack of transparency, and procedural failure that has significantly impacted me as a consumer. Despite this, I have since received repeated and persistent daily collection calls demanding payment. Each time, I have been forced to re-explain the situation, only to be told that there are no records of any active investigation or payment hold. This reflects a serious breakdown in internal communication and record-keeping. This conduct has now escalated to the level of harassment. I have been subjected to repeated, unnecessary contact due to Wells Fargos failure to properly document and manage my case internally. Additionally, during one interaction, a representative inappropriately suggested that if I were receiving SNAP or food stamp benefits, I could use those funds to make payments. This statement was not only irrelevant, but also unprofessional and indicative of a lack of proper training and sensitivity. Ive formally requested that Wells Fargo provide all documentation and evidence demonstrating that the disputed transactions were authorized. I was assured that this request would be fulfilled. As of today, XX/XX/year>, no such documentation has been provided. The disputed transactions occurred on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/year>, and were reported on XX/XX/year>. Wells Fargo denied my claim based on the following assertions : * My card was in my possession * No device linked to a digital wallet was reported lost * The transactions were conducted using a device associated with my account However, these statements are conclusory and unsupported. At no point has Wells Fargo provided any actual evidence demonstrating that I authorized these transactions. Furthermore, Wells Fargos determination appears to be in direct violation of Regulation E ( 12 C.F.R. Part 1005 ), including but not limited to : Under 12 C.F.R. 1005.6, a financial institution bears the burden of proving that a transaction was authorized in order to impose liability on the consumer. Wells Fargo has failed to meet this burden. The mere claim that a transaction originated from a device associated with my account does not establish authorization, intent, or participation. Under 12 C.F.R. 1005.11, Wells Fargo is required to : * Conduct a reasonable investigation * Review all relevant information * Provide the results of the investigation * Supply documentation upon request To date, Wells Fargo has failed to provide : I formally requested that XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX provide complete transfer trace information and investigative records associated with the disputed transactions, including but not limited to : IMAD ( Input Message Accountability Data ) numbers ; OMAD ( Output Message Accountability Data ) numbers ; Full Fedwire and ACH trace reports ; Transaction routing and settlement records ; Receiving bank information ; Beneficiary account details ; SWIFT or Federal Reserve reference numbers if applicable ; Device information and authentication logs ; IP access logs ; Internal fraud investigation notes ; Transaction authorization records ; Fraud analysis reports ; Any records relied upon to conclude that the transactions were authorized. This lack of transparency and failure to produce documentation constitutes noncompliance with federal error resolution requirements. Further compounding these issues, Wells Fargo has acknowledged that the activity is consistent with a known fraud scheme and implemented lost/stolen account safeguards, yet simultaneously concluded that there were no indicators of fraud. These positions are contradictory and can not be reconciled, further evidencing an incomplete or unreasonable investigation. At this stage, XXXX XXXX actions reflect systemic failures, unsupported conclusions, and disregard for regulatory obligations. This is my final request : Provide, within a reasonable timeframe, all documentation, evidence, and investigative materials relied upon in denying my claim, including but not limited to authentication records, device data, and internal investigation notes. Failure to comply will leave me no option but to escalate this matter further, including pursuing legal counsel and all available remedies. I expect a complete and documented response without further delay.

Over the course of several days, they quietly monitored the computer, observing how our finance operator logged into our bank and bill-pay systems, how she processed payments, and when she stepped away from her desk. They noticed she frequently remained logged into these systems. To keep the session active while she was away, the attacker displayed a full-screen XXXX overlay with a message reading, in substance, " We are updating the computer, please don't turn off. '' Believing this was a legitimate system update, she left the computer running and authenticated, which gave the attacker uninterrupted access to our financial accounts. The unauthorized transactions : On XX/XX/year>, using that remote access, the attacker executed a sequence of transfers designed to move money out of our accounts to an outside recipient we have never done business with. First, they moved {$5300.00} out of a separate, affiliated business account into our checking account to stage the funds a transfer between XXXX distinct business entities that we would never make in the normal course of business, and which by itself was fraudulent. They then used our bill-pay platform ( XXXX ) to send a {$5000.00} wire to a payee identified as an individual, under an invoice we never created. That {$5000.00} wire completed. The attacker attempted a second {$5000.00} wire to the same payee, but it failed due to insufficient funds. The payee 's records show clear signs of fraud : the contact email was a personal XXXX address rather than a business domain ; the payee listed inconsistent addresses in XXXX different states ; and the wire was directed to a bank account different from the one shown in the payee 's own stated bank details. Continued attack attempts : The attacker also accessed our payroll system and attempted to add a XXXX XXXX in order to route additional money out. XXXX of our owners received a text-message alert about the change, caught it in progress, stopped it, and changed the password before any funds could move. Our immediate response : As soon as we discovered funds leaving the account, we acted. We reported the fraud to the bank in person at a branch, fully reset the compromised computer to remove the remote-access software, changed all passwords across our systems, opened entirely new bank accounts, and froze our credit because the attacker had access to identifying information. We also filed a police report and a fraud report with the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC Report # XXXX ). The bank 's reversal the core of this complaint : When we first reported the fraud, the bank did the right thing. It recognized the {$5000.00} wire as fraudulent, reversed it, and returned the funds to our account. Shortly afterward, however, the perpetrator called the bank by phone, falsely claimed the transaction was a legitimate payment, and the bank reversed its own decision pulling the {$5000.00} back out of our account and sending it to the fraudster. The bank relied entirely on this unverified phone call. The caller was the very person who committed the fraud. There was no documentation of a legitimate business relationship, no verification that the caller was an authorized or genuine payee, and no consideration of the extensive evidence of fraud surrounding the transaction. A perpetrator 's self-serving phone call is not a valid basis to reverse a correctly identified fraudulent wire. The payment records that appear to show a " valid '' transaction exist only because the attacker generated them while remotely controlling our computer through our own authenticated session which is exactly why the payment superficially appears to have originated from us. That is a direct consequence of the account takeover, not evidence that we authorized anything. We have provided supporting documentation, including transaction records, the fraudulent payee 's details, bank statement entries, and our FTC report confirmation, as attachments to this complaint.

On XX/XX/2026, I was robbed at gunpoint while abroad in XXXX. My phone, debit card, and credit cards were stolen. I have a police report documenting the robbery. On XX/XX/2026, the day after the robbery, I called Chase to report what happened and to regain access to my funds. I explained that my phone and cards had been stolen and that I was abroad without normal access to money. Chase told me to wait 24 hours and call back. After waiting, I called back. Instead of providing a workable emergency access method, Chase told me they still could not restore access or authenticate me in a useful way. I was told they would send me a replacement card, but the card was shipped to my home address in New York, not to me in XXXX, so it did not help me access funds while stranded abroad. On XX/XX/2026, I spent hours on the phone with Chase again. I explained repeatedly that I was abroad after an armed robbery, had no working phone, had no cards, and needed access to my own funds to buy a phone, repay a friend, travel safely, and/or reach the XXXX Embassy XXXX I had identity documents available and a police report. I asked for alternative verification that did not depend on my stolen phone. Chase transferred me through multiple departments, including fraud/consumer protection/global assistance. Chases system kept requiring mobile-app, phone, or SMS verification, but that was impossible because the phone was stolen. Chase representatives tried multiple phone numbers for verification codes, but the system would not allow them. I was told email would not help. I was not given a secure document-upload option for my passport, ID, or police report. I was told a representative could not perform a transfer for me because my account required me to do transfers online, even though Chase was blocking me from getting online. During the call, I made clear that I was researching my rights and reading consumer-protection information while speaking with Chase. I was not asking Chase to ignore security. I was asking for a senior manual review or alternative identity-verification process because the ordinary phone-based process was impossible after the robbery. Chase repeatedly told me to wait, call back, use phone verification, go to a branch, or wait for a card. None of those options solved the emergency. I was outside the United States, had no stolen-phone access, no card in my possession, and no realistic way to go to a XXXX Chase XXXX XXXX I had already borrowed approximately {$500.00} from a friend and was being forced to keep borrowing or remain stranded. I also spent hours on international calls trying to resolve the issue. By the end of the XX/XX/XXXX call, the Chase representative said he had run out of tools, could not authenticate me at the required level, could not transfer me to anyone else, and would have to release the line. The practical result was that Chases fraud-prevention system locked out the lawful customer after a documented violent robbery and provided no workable emergency alternative. I believe Chases conduct may violate or implicate federal consumer financial protection law, including the prohibition on unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices under the Consumer Financial Protection Act, 12 U.S.C. 5531 and 5536. The conduct was unfair because it caused substantial injury : I was abroad without access to my funds after a violent crime. I could not reasonably avoid the injury because Chases required authentication method depended on the stolen phone, and Chase did not provide a workable alternative. The injury was not outweighed by the benefit of fraud prevention once Chase refused any practical manual review despite my police report and identity documents. I also believe Chases handling raises issues under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E because I promptly reported the theft of access devices, including my phone/cards, yet Chases process left me unable to protect and access my account through any workable alternative channel. At minimum, CFPB should investigate whether Chases procedures for stolen access devices, emergency authentication, blocked online access, and customer access to funds are reasonable and compliant.

narrative: * * Complaint Against Capital One Business Credit Card Account * * I am submitting this complaint regarding the servicing of my Capital One Business Credit Card account and the significant financial harm that resulted from a series of inconsistent and inaccurate communications I received from Capital One representatives. My name is XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. I am a business owner and have always taken my financial obligations seriously. Prior to the events described below, my company maintained an excellent payment history with Capital One. We routinely paid statement balances in full, including a statement balance of approximately {$110000.00} shortly before the issues described below began. I specifically selected this Capital One business card because it was marketed as a card with no preset spending limit. My understanding was that responsible payment history and account performance would determine spending capacity. Without warning, Capital One suddenly restricted my ability to use the card for new purchases. When I immediately contacted Capital One to understand why this had occurred, the representative I spoke with stated they did not know why the account had been restricted and indicated that it should not have happened. Despite this acknowledgment, the restriction remained in place. Because my business relied on this account for operating expenses, I was forced to move my company 's spending to other financial institutions in order to continue operating. Recognizing that Capital One had effectively removed the card as a financing tool for my business, I asked whether any payment plan or hardship program was available so that I could responsibly manage the remaining balance. I was specifically told that Capital One did not offer payment plans. Months later, after my account became delinquent, Capital One placed me on a payment plan. I believe this raises a significant concern. If payment plans existed when I initially requested one, I was provided inaccurate information that directly affected my financial decisions. If they did not exist at that time, I have requested an explanation from Capital One as to when those programs became available and why I was told otherwise. Another issue involves the authority granted to my account manager, XXXX. Throughout the life of this account, XXXX was not permitted to perform certain account functions, including redeeming rewards points, because she was reportedly not authorized to do so. However, during Capital One 's investigation of this matter, I was informed that they relied on conversations with XXXX regarding repayment and delinquency because she was considered an authorized account manager. I have requested documentation explaining what authority she possessed, what authority she did not possess, and why Capital One considered her authorized to negotiate repayment matters while restricting her authority for other account functions. Capital One also reported multiple late payments to the credit bureaus, causing my personal credit score to fall from approximately XXXX to approximately XXXX in a very short period of time. As a direct result, another financial institution reduced one of my personal credit card limits from approximately {$35000.00} to approximately {$4400.00}. This damage extends well beyond the Capital One account itself and has materially affected my overall financial profile and ongoing business financing opportunities. I initially believed I had been told by Capital One that I had 180 days before the account would be reported to the credit bureaus. Capital One has since advised me that, after reviewing recorded calls, it believes its representatives stated 120 days rather than 180 days. I have requested the transcripts of those recordings so I may independently review what was communicated. Regardless of the outcome of that issue, the broader concerns remain unresolved : * My account was unexpectedly restricted despite a strong payment history and recent six-figure payment. * A Capital One representative reportedly stated the restriction should not have occurred. * I was told no payment plans were available, yet was later placed on one. * I received inconsistent information from multiple representatives throughout the servicing of this account. * These events collectively resulted in substantial financial harm. I have attempted to resolve these issues directly with Capital One 's Executive Office before submitting this complaint. While they reviewed one aspect of my complaint, they have not provided satisfactory explanations regarding the account restriction, the contradictory information about payment plans, or the authority issues involving my account manager. I respectfully request that the CFPB review this matter and require Capital One to fully address these concerns, including providing complete explanations of the servicing decisions made on my account, the information communicated by its representatives, and whether its handling of this account complied with its obligations to treat customers fairly and accurately. I appreciate your time and consideration.

narrative: I am filing this complaint against Chase Home Lending regarding my refinance, loan number XXXX. I refinanced with Chase after contacting them to compare against my existing XXXX XXXX, which was at approximately 6.9 %. My purpose was clear from the beginning : I wanted a refinance that would help me consolidate high credit-card debt and improve my monthly financial position. Chase represented that it could meet or improve on my existing situation, and I proceeded based on that understanding. Instead, Chase structured and closed a loan that did not accomplish the stated purpose. The loan resulted in approximately {$27000.00} in fees and points, provided {$0.00} in cash-out proceeds for debt consolidation, ( despite being told mupltiple times there would be cash for me ) and required me to wire approximately {$1700.00} at closing. I was not clearly warned before closing that the cash-out/debt-consolidation purpose had effectively failed or that I would end up paying money into the closing rather than receiving funds to pay down debt. There was also a serious communication and handoff failure. I was shifted between Chase personnel without a clear introduction or explanation of who was responsible for what. XXXX XXXX, XXXX ID XXXX, locked the rate on XX/XX/2026 and was identified as the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX, was identified as the manager. XXXX XXXX later handled processing items such as homeowners insurance documentation and was professional in that administrative role, but the overall loan structure and management response were deeply flawed. A major issue was the property valuation and its impact on the cash-out purpose of the loan. When the valuation came in lower than expected, Chase did not clearly explain to me that the debt-consolidation payout was in jeopardy or that the loan no longer served the purpose I had repeatedly discussed. I was worn down by the process and told Chase to move forward, but that should not be treated as informed consent to a loan that no longer achieved the purpose Chase had used to sell me on refinancing. In addition, I was told that I would have XXXX deferred mortgage payments. Instead, only XXXX payment appears to have been deferred, and I was left with an unexpected payment burden. My current Chase mortgage information shows a {$3800.00} mortgage payment made on XX/XX/2026 and another {$3800.00} payment due XX/XX/2026. This payment schedule, combined with the failure to provide cash-out proceeds, has caused immediate financial hardship. After the loan closed, I escalated the matter to Chase. XXXX XXXX called me and attempted to de-escalate the situation by stating that Chase had a free refinance program and that I could refinance again later in the summer. I relied on that verbal commitment as the proposed resolution. When I later requested the commitment in writing, XXXX XXXX began recharacterizing it as a non-guaranteed marketing offer rather than the resolution that had been represented to me. The escalation process has also been mishandled. I had multiple interactions with Chase escalation representatives. XXXX XXXX was helpful and transparent, but other representatives were not. XXXX representative claimed my case had been closed because a determination was left on my voicemail. I saved my voicemails, and no such determination message exists. A promised return call from the first escalation representative also never occurred. This complaint is not about buyers remorse. It is about Chase selling and structuring a refinance around debt consolidation and payment relief, then closing a loan that produced the opposite result : no cash-out proceeds, significant fees and points, an unexpected amount due at closing, and less payment deferral than represented. Chase then attempted to resolve the matter verbally with a promised free refinance, only to walk that promise back when I requested written confirmation. I am requesting that Chase be required to : XXXX. Conduct a formal audit of all call recordings, internal notes, emails, loan estimates, closing disclosures, valuation records, and payment-schedule records related to this refinance. XXXX. Explain why a refinance intended for debt consolidation closed with approximately {$27000.00} in costs and {$0.00} cash-out proceeds. XXXX. Explain why I was required to wire approximately {$1700.00} at closing. XXXX. Explain why I was told there would be XXXX deferred payments but only XXXX appears to have been deferred. XXXX Review the conversation in which XXXX XXXX XXXX that Chase had a free refinance program and that I could refinance again later in the summer. XXXX. Honor the promised corrective resolution or provide equivalent financial relief. XXXX. Refund or credit fees, points, payment impacts, or other costs caused by Chases loan-structuring failure and misrepresentations. XXXX. Confirm that no negative credit reporting, late-payment reporting, or adverse servicing action will occur while this dispute is pending. XXXX. Provide a complete written response identifying what Chase reviewed, what it found, and what corrective action it will take. I have already attempted to resolve this through Chases escalation process. Chase has not provided an adequate resolution, and the situation has created immediate financial hardship.

narrative: On XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, I submitted a formal data request to Capital Ones executive compliance office seeking a manual extraction of my transaction history, correspondence records and security logs for accounts that I closed in XXXX. Capital Ones automated portal forces consumers to log in with active online banking credentials to access account data. This makes it impossible for former customers, whose online credentials have been deactivated, to exercise their right to access their historical records. On XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, an executive escalation specialist ( 'Bri ' ) placed a verified incoming phone call to me, acknowledging receipt of my request and stating they were assigned to handle the escalation. However, on XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, that same specialist issued a written refusal stating that Capital One is " unable to assist '' with locating or manually extracting data affiliated with these closed accounts. Crucially, Capital One 's team chose to transmit this sensitive data denial to an archived, legacy email address tied exclusively to my historical XXXX profile. This legacy address was completely omitted from my current active request and correspondence. This creates a severe regulatory contradiction and a data security failure in the following areas : 1. False Claim of Technical Limitation : The only way the escalation team could target that specific legacy email address was by successfully indexing, searching and retrieving my deactivated XXXX consumer records from Capital One 's backend infrastructure. Capital One actively located and extracted my historical data to route a denial, proving their claim of being " unable to locate or extract '' the remaining transaction file is completely false. 2. Data Security and Routing Failure : Transmitting sensitive compliance and financial communications to an unverified, archived inbox rather than the verified, active email explicitly provided in my active communications violates basic financial data safeguarding protocols. Capital One is violating its obligation to provide basic consumer account records under federal standards by trapping former customers behind an impassable digital login wall while actively using backend archives to route sensitive correspondence to unverified legacy channels.

narrative: CFPB Complaint Against Wells Fargo Bank , N.A . Product : Checking Account / Debit Card Dispute Investigation Issue : Inconsistent Claim Handling, Premature Claim Denials, Partial Provisional Credits Without Explanation, and Erroneous Claim Closure ________________________________________ I am filing this complaint regarding Wells Fargo 's handling of multiple disputed transactions involving the merchant Topstep. The claims at issue arise from the same merchant, the same course of dealings, and the same underlying dispute. Despite this, the claims have received different outcomes, and I have not been provided with an explanation for the different treatment. The relevant claims are : Claim No. XXXX ( XXXX transactions ) Closed/Denied Claim No. XXXX ( XXXX transactions ) Closed/Denied Claim No. XXXX ( XXXX transactions ) Closed/Denied Claim No. XXXX ( XXXX transactions ) In Progress Claim No. XXXX ( XXXX transactions ) Closed with the notation, " We closed this claim at your request. '' My concern is not simply that Wells Fargo reached an unfavorable decision. My concern is that the information currently available to me raises questions regarding whether these claims are being evaluated under a fair and consistent process. Different Outcomes for the Same Underlying Dispute The claims involve the same merchant and the same underlying dispute. However, the outcomes have been materially different. XXXX XXXX. XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX were denied. Claim No. XXXX remains in progress. Claim No. XXXX was marked as closed at my request. I have not been provided with an explanation regarding the criteria used to reach these different outcomes. Partial Provisional Credits Without Explanation With respect to Claim No. XXXX, Wells Fargo stated that additional information was needed and represented that a letter had been sent requesting supporting documentation. Wells Fargo also issued provisional credits for only a portion of the transactions included within that claim. Based upon the claim information available to me, Claim No. XXXX contains twelve disputed transactions. However, provisional credits were issued for only six of those transactions. I have not been provided with an explanation regarding the criteria used to distinguish between the six transactions that received provisional credits and the six transactions that did not. Because all XXXX transactions arise from the same merchant and the same underlying dispute, I am requesting an explanation of the determining factors Wells Fargo relied upon in deciding to issue provisional credits for certain transactions while withholding provisional credits for the remaining transactions within the same claim. Claims Closed Before I Was Able to Present My Evidence For Claim No. XXXX, Wells Fargo indicated that additional information was needed and stated that a letter had been sent requesting supporting documentation. As of the date of this complaint, I have not yet received that letter. I was waiting for the letter because I understood it would explain what information Wells Fargo wanted reviewed. On XX/XX/year>, I contacted Wells Fargo and was advised that Wells Fargo was seeking copies of the merchant 's terms and conditions as well as communications between myself and the merchant. During that same call, I advised Wells Fargo that I was compiling a comprehensive evidentiary package and intended to provide the requested documentation. At the time XXXX XXXX. XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX were denied, Wells Fargo had not yet received any of the evidence I was preparing to submit. I had not yet been given an opportunity to present my supporting documentation, provide the merchant communications Wells Fargo later requested, submit the terms and conditions Wells Fargo later requested, or provide the evidentiary package I was assembling regarding the dispute. This raises concerns because certain claims were denied before Wells Fargo reviewed my evidence, while another claim involving the same merchant and same underlying dispute remained open pending additional information. Similar Claims Investigated Through Another Financial Institution I also have claims involving the same merchant that were submitted through another financial institution using a different debit card. Those claims involve the same merchant, the same course of dealings, and the same underlying dispute. That institution continued its investigation, obtained information relating to the dispute, and ultimately received transaction reversals from the merchant. I am not suggesting that Wells Fargo is required to reach the same conclusion as another financial institution. However, it is difficult for me to understand how Wells Fargo could deny claims involving the same merchant and same underlying dispute before receiving the evidence that I was preparing to submit, particularly when another institution investigating the same dispute was able to obtain information from the merchant and secure reversals. Claim Incorrectly Marked as Closed at My Request Claim No. XXXX was closed with the notation : " We closed this claim at your request. '' I never requested that Claim No. XXXX be closed, withdrawn, or canceled. No such request was ever made. After discovering that notation, I contacted Wells Fargo on XX/XX/year>. During that call, I informed the Wells Fargo representative that I had never requested closure of the claim. The representative advised me that Wells Fargo 's records appeared to indicate that an investigator believed I had requested that the claim be withdrawn or canceled. I informed the representative that this information was incorrect. I requested that the claim be reopened and investigated. The representative acknowledged my concern and advised that a request would be submitted to reopen the claim. This raises additional concerns regarding the accuracy of Wells Fargo 's claim records and the basis upon which Claim No. XXXX was closed. If Wells Fargo believes that I requested closure of the claim, I request that Wells Fargo identify the communication upon which it relied and explain how it concluded that I requested closure. No such request was ever made. Requested Resolution I respectfully request that Wells Fargo : 1. Explain the investigative steps taken before denying XXXX XXXX. XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX. 2. Explain what evidence was reviewed for each denied claim. 3. Explain whether information was obtained from the merchant and whether any merchant responses were relied upon. 4. Explain why Claims Nos. XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX were denied while Claim No. XXXX remained open and pending additional information. 5. Explain the determining factors used to issue provisional credits for six transactions within Claim No. XXXX while withholding provisional credits for the remaining six transactions. 6. Explain what evidence, criteria, or investigative findings were relied upon in making that distinction. 7. Explain the basis for the notation that Claim No. XXXX was closed at my request. 8. Correct the claim record if the notation that I requested closure was inaccurate. 9. Provide a meaningful opportunity for my supporting documentation and evidentiary package to be reviewed before final determinations are made on these claims. 10. Reconsider any denied claims after reviewing the evidence relevant to the dispute. I am currently compiling a comprehensive evidentiary package consisting of merchant communications, terms and conditions, account records, transaction records, platform records, screenshots, refund-related communications, investigation materials, and other supporting documentation relevant to these claims. Thank you for your review and assistance in this matter.

narrative: I am submitting this complaint against Wells Fargo regarding its denial of my fraud claim involving my checking account ending in XXXX. I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate Wells Fargo 's handling of my claim and require the bank to conduct a fair and complete review. I am also requesting reimbursement of my financial loss in the amount of * * {$390.00} * *. On XX/XX/XXXX, I sent {$390.00} through XXXX to secure what I believed was a legitimate car rental reservation in XXXX. The individuals advertising the rental represented themselves as a legitimate business and instructed me to send payment through XXXX. I relied on those representations and authorized the transfer because I genuinely believed I was paying a legitimate company for a legitimate service. Shortly after the payment was sent, I discovered that I had been the victim of a scam. The individuals who received my money stopped responding to my messages, and no rental vehicle was ever provided. I immediately attempted to recover my funds by contacting XXXX and Wells Fargo. Unfortunately, by the time the fraud was discovered, the recipient had already collected the funds in cash, preventing recovery through XXXX 's partner bank. I filed a fraud claim with Wells Fargo, explaining that I had been deceived into authorizing the payment through fraudulent misrepresentation. I provided consistent information throughout the investigation that this was not simply a dispute over services rendered, but rather a scam in which criminals falsely represented themselves as a legitimate business in order to obtain my money. Wells Fargo denied my claim. I requested reconsideration, but the bank upheld its decision. In its written response, Wells Fargo acknowledged that I believed I was the victim of a scam and recognized that the recipient became unresponsive after receiving my payment. However, the bank stated that my claim was denied because " a cancellation was not made or attempted prior to the expected date of service. '' I believe this reasoning fails to address the actual nature of my complaint. My claim was never based on cancelling a legitimate service. My claim was that I was induced to authorize a payment through fraud. By the time I realized I had been deceived, the scammers had already disappeared with my money. Expecting a victim of fraud to cancel a transaction before discovering the scam is unreasonable and does not meaningfully address whether the payment was obtained through deception. Despite acknowledging my report of fraud, Wells Fargo never explained why my claim appeared to be evaluated as a merchant or service dispute rather than as a scam. The bank also did not explain what evidence it relied upon, what investigative steps it took, or why my evidence of fraudulent misrepresentation did not warrant a different outcome. I believe Wells Fargo 's investigation was incomplete because it focused on whether I cancelled the transaction rather than whether I was induced to authorize the payment through fraud. Throughout the process, I repeatedly explained that I did not voluntarily choose to lose my money. I was intentionally deceived by individuals impersonating a legitimate business. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate whether Wells Fargo properly evaluated my claim, whether the bank applied the appropriate dispute procedures, and whether it provided a fair and adequate investigation consistent with its obligations to consumers. As a resolution, I respectfully request that Wells Fargo : * Reopen and conduct an independent review of my fraud claim. * Provide all documentation, investigative notes, and policies relied upon in denying my claim. * Explain why my report of fraud was evaluated using cancellation or merchant-dispute criteria. * Reimburse me for my loss of * * {$390.00} * *, as I believe I was the victim of a fraudulent scheme rather than a routine merchant dispute. I have made every reasonable effort to resolve this matter directly with Wells Fargo before filing this complaint. Despite multiple attempts, the bank has maintained its denial without adequately addressing the substance of my concerns. Thank you for your time and consideration. I respectfully request the CFPB 's assistance in reviewing Wells Fargo 's handling of this matter and helping facilitate a fair resolution. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX
