narrative: I am submitting this complaint as a follow-up to CFPB Complaint No. XXXX and Capital One XXXX XXXX. XXXX regarding a disputed transaction involving XXXX XXXX / XXXXXXXX XXXX in the amount of {$87.00}. My concern is not only the merchants conduct, but Capital Ones decision to reverse the provisional credit after receiving the merchants response while appearing to evaluate this matter solely as a cancellation-policy dispute rather than considering the actual circumstances that gave rise to the dispute. The original purchase was made on XX/XX/XXXX for a discounted promotional kayaking excursion voucher. Because of the age of the transaction by the time the scheduled excursion occurred, I was unable to pursue a traditional dispute through normal channels and ultimately sought assistance through my original CFPB complaint. Following that complaint, Capital One opened a dispute investigation and issued a temporary credit for the disputed transaction, as well as related fees and interest charges. Capital One then contacted the merchant for a response. After receiving the merchants response, Capital One rebilled the disputed amount to my account and informed me that the case would be considered closed unless I provided additional information by XX/XX/XXXX. I am disappointed in Capital Ones decision to reverse the provisional credit based upon the merchants response, particularly because the merchants rebuttal focused almost entirely on the existence of a refund policy and the assertion that the tour was not cancelled, while largely ignoring the circumstances that actually caused the dispute. I am equally disappointed that after Capital One invited me to continue the dispute, I was informed that I would either need to mail documentation or call to obtain a secure upload link in order to submit additional information. Rather than providing a direct and accessible method for continuing the dispute online, I was required to take additional steps simply to provide the information Capital One requested. Therefore, I am submitting the requested information through this CFPB complaint and attaching all supporting documentation. This dispute did not arise because I simply changed my mind about attending a tour or later decided I wanted a refund despite a refund policy. I traveled from out of town specifically for this excursion and incurred lodging, fuel, food, travel, and planning expenses in order to participate. Upon arrival for the scheduled excursion, I encountered a completely different situation than the one later portrayed by the merchant. I arrived around XXXX minutes before the scheduled XXXXXXXX XXXX check-in time, as many reasonable and responsible customers would for a guided outdoor excursion on XXXX XXXX that theyve travelled a good distance to attend. When I arrived, the building was locked. No guide was present. No management representative was present. There was no organized check-in process. There was no communication regarding equipment, launch procedures, guest instructions, or whether the excursion was even operating. It was an abandoned rendezvous location. Over the next twenty-plus minutes, additional guests continued arriving while confusion persisted regarding whether the tour was taking place. Eventually, individuals associated with the operation arrived. When asked what was happening, they stated they were only shuttle drivers and that they had to figure out what was going on. At no point during my presence at the rendezvous location was meaningful information provided regarding who was in charge, what was happening, why normal operations were not occurring, or what guests should expect. The merchant has since attempted to dismiss these concerns by emphasizing that I arrived early and left prior to departure. However, there is a significant difference between a scheduled check-in time and a scheduled launch time occurring at a separate location requiring transportation. I remained at the rendezvous location until approximately XXXX XXXX roughly twenty minutes after the scheduled XXXXXXXX XXXX check-in time and only ten minutes before the scheduled XXXXXXXX XXXX launch. During that period, employees repeatedly stated they did not know what was happening and had to figure things out. The shuttle driver specifically dropped off passengers and then parked the shuttle rather than remaining available to transport additional guests or provide information regarding the status of the excursion. Based upon the complete lack of communication, organization, operational leadership, and professionalism displayed by a company responsible for conducting guided excursions on XXXX XXXX, I no longer felt comfortable participating and elected not to proceed. After the incident, I attempted to resolve the matter directly with the merchant. My first communication was submitted through the companys online contact form because that was the only contact method provided to me at the rendezvous location. The individuals present were unable or unwilling to provide direct ownership or management contact information. Regardless of whether those individuals were employees or contractors, I find it unacceptable that a guided outdoor excursion had no management representative available at the check-in location and no meaningful way for customers to contact ownership during active business operations. After receiving no response to my first communication, I sent a second communication directly to the email address provided in an automated email sent later that same evening requesting that I leave a review for an excursion I never attended. Neither communication received a response. In fact, I only learned any details regarding the alleged emergency after the owner publicly responded to my XXXX review. The owner never responded to my direct communications and instead chose to respond publicly while continuing to ignore my attempts to resolve the matter privately. The merchants response to Capital One focused primarily on the argument that the voucher was non-refundable and that I did not cancel pursuant to company policy. However, the merchants own response to the Michigan Attorney General contains several admissions that directly support the concerns I have raised from the beginning. In that response, the merchant admits that the emergency : temporarily impacted normal check-in operations. The merchant further states : communication during the emergency could have been clearer and further admits : We have since reviewed internal procedures to further improve communication protocols during unforeseen events. These admissions are important because they acknowledge operational disruption, communication deficiencies, and the need for procedural review and improvement after the incident. The owner simultaneously argues that I should accept responsibility while acknowledging that communication procedures required improvement and that normal check-in operations were impacted. If communication protocols required review and improvement afterward, then there was clearly a communication breakdown during the event itself. That communication breakdown is the very issue I have consistently raised from the beginning and the primary reason I lost confidence in participating. The merchants abbreviated submission to Capital One largely omitted these admissions and instead framed the matter as a simple refund-policy dispute. My concern is that Capital One appears to have accepted that framing. The dispute is not whether a refund policy existed. The dispute is whether the circumstances presented to paying customers at the scheduled check-in location were consistent with the level of communication, organization, professionalism, and operational management reasonably expected of a guided commercial excursion. The merchants own statements acknowledge that they were not. I am therefore requesting that Capital One conduct a fair review of the complete circumstances surrounding this dispute rather than relying solely upon the merchants assertion that no cancellation occurred under company policy. Documents Attached and Submitted in Support of This Complaint XXXX. Original CFPB Complaint No. XXXX Complaint that resulted in Capital One opening a dispute investigation despite the age of the transaction. XXXX. Capital One Case Documentation Capital One Case No. XXXX. Capital One Dispute XXXX XXXX. XXXX. XXXX. XX/XX/XXXX Capital One Dispute Letter Showing Capital One opened the dispute, issued a provisional credit for the transaction, and credited related fees and interest while awaiting the merchants response. XXXX. XX/XX/XXXX Capital One Dispute Letter Showing Capital One reversed the provisional credit after receiving the merchants response and informed me that I would need to either mail documentation or call to obtain a secure upload link in order to continue the dispute. XXXX. Merchant Chargeback Response Submitted to Capital One Including the merchants statements regarding the refund policy, alleged fulfillment of the excursion, and request that the chargeback be reversed. XXXX. Michigan Attorney General Complaint File Including the complaint and closure correspondence. XXXX. Merchant Response Submitted to the Michigan Attorney General Including the merchants admissions that : normal check-in operations were impacted, communication during the incident could have been clearer, and internal procedures were reviewed afterward to improve communication protocols during unforeseen events. XXXX. Follow-Up Email Sent Directly to the Merchant After Initial Contact Attempt Submitted Through the Merchants Online Contact Form Submitted after the incident in an effort to resolve the matter directly with the company. Sent after receiving an automated review request for an excursion I never attended. These attempts at communication went unanswered. XXXX. Public Review and Merchant Response Demonstrating that the merchant chose to respond publicly while failing to respond to direct communications. XXXX. Reservation Confirmation and Reminder Emails Showing the scheduled XXXX XXXX check-in/meet time and XXXXXXXX XXXX launch time. Included because the merchant repeatedly characterizes the issue as my arrival before check-in, despite the fact that I remained at the rendezvous location until approximately XXXXXXXX XXXX, roughly twenty minutes after the scheduled check-in time and only ten minutes before the scheduled launch. These documents demonstrate that check-in and launch were separate events occurring at different times and that customers were expected to arrive before launch in order to complete check-in and transportation arrangements. Collectively, these documents demonstrate that this dispute arose from operational disruptions, communication failures, and the handling of the excursion itselfnot from a simple disagreement regarding a refund policy. My position remains unchanged. Medical emergencies happen. My concern has never been that an emergency occurred. My concern is that paying customers were left without meaningful communication, leadership, organization, or confidence in the operation at the very time they were expected to participate in a guided XXXX XXXX excursion, and that the merchant continues to characterize those concerns as irrelevant while simultaneously admitting that communication and operational procedures required review and improvement afterward. Under these circumstances, I do not believe this matter can be fairly reduced to a simple no refund policy dispute.

He explained that criminals were attempting to use my accounts as part of a large money laundering operation and that Wells Fargo needed to immediately secure my accounts. As part of the " security process, '' he instructed me that Wells Fargo needed to verify my identity by sending authentication codes to my phone. Believing I was speaking with an actual Wells Fargo fraud investigator, I provided the requested authentication codes. What I did not realize until much later was that while I believed I was verifying my identity to Wells Fargo, I was actually giving the criminals the one-time security codes they needed to access my online banking, change my passwords, lock me out of my own accounts, and ultimately obtain unauthorized cash advances using my credit card accounts. The individual remained on the phone with me for more than two and a half hours. During that time, he never pressured me with threats or obvious scare tactics. Instead, he patiently answered every question I asked and consistently provided information that appeared to verify his identity and his access to confidential Wells Fargo systems. He told me my accounts had been identified in a federal money laundering investigation involving approximately one hundred Wells Fargo customers. According to him, criminals were using legitimate customer accounts to launder funds before withdrawing the money in person. He claimed I was one of ten customers currently being targeted. To reinforce the story, he sent me emails containing Wells Fargo logos and what appeared to be official documentation referencing cooperation between Wells Fargo, the FBI, and FinCEN in an ongoing money laundering investigation. Looking back, I now know these documents were fraudulent, but at the time they appeared authentic. Because I have spent my career in mortgage banking and have taken annual anti-money laundering training, I questioned nearly everything he told me. Every concern I raised was met with an immediate, detailed, and believable explanation. When I commented that I did not hear the normal Wells Fargo hold music whenever he placed me on hold, he explained that he was working from a secure investigation room with the FBI 's FinCEN division. That explanation seemed plausible given the nature of the investigation he described. He then instructed me to go to my local Wells Fargo branch because, according to him, an individual impersonating me was expected to return later that afternoon to withdraw approximately {$5600.00} in laundered funds from my account. He insisted that Wells Fargo needed me to withdraw the money first so federal investigators could use it as evidence in the criminal investigation. I initially refused and told him I would rather contact the police directly. Rather than becoming defensive, he calmly reassured me and continued providing details that, at the time, appeared impossible for anyone outside Wells Fargo to know. He instructed me to check my account balance at the Wells Fargo ATM before entering the branch. Before I even looked at the screen, he accurately stated the amount that was available in my account. When the ATM displayed the exact balance he had quoted, it significantly strengthened my belief that I was speaking with someone who had legitimate access to Wells Fargo 's internal systems. Once inside the bank, the deception became even more convincing. While I stood in line, the caller accurately identified the names of the tellers on duty and the branch manager. He told me I was third in line waiting to be served. He correctly described my clothing, including my blue shirt, white shorts, and the fact that I was wearing an earbud in my right ear. He even stated that he could see me through the bank 's surveillance cameras. At that point, I looked throughout the branch to determine whether anyone nearby could have been watching me. The branch was essentially empty, and there was no obvious way someone outside the bank could have observed me with such precision. Combined with his knowledge of my account information, this convinced me that he truly had access to Wells Fargo 's internal security systems. He then walked me through exactly what the teller would do before it happened. He predicted that she would ask whether I wanted large or small bills, that she would count the money twice using the counting machine, place the cash into an envelope, and provide me with a receipt bearing her name. Every one of those events occurred exactly as he described. Each correct prediction reinforced my belief that I was cooperating with a legitimate Wells Fargo fraud investigation rather than being manipulated by criminals. Looking back, I recognize these were carefully orchestrated psychological tactics designed to gain my trust. At the time, however, every piece of information the caller provided appeared to independently verify his legitimacy. That trust ultimately resulted in my being manipulated into surrendering {$5600.00} under the false belief that I was assisting Wells Fargo and federal investigators in stopping an active money laundering operation. The emotional impact of this crime has been devastating. Beyond the financial loss, I have experienced tremendous anxiety, humiliation, sleeplessness, and a profound loss of confidence in the very security systems I believed existed to protect customers. As someone who has spent nearly four decades in financial services helping others safeguard their finances, realizing that I had been manipulated so completely has been deeply traumatic. I respectfully request that Wells Fargo and the Arizona Attorney General fully investigate not only the fraud itself, but also how criminals were able to convincingly impersonate Wells Fargo personnel, possess information that appeared to come from internal banking systems, and manipulate a customer into believing he was acting under the direction of Wells Fargo and federal law enforcement. Wells Fargo 's Response and My Concerns Following the fraud, I immediately reported the incident to the XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX. and Wells Fargo and fully cooperated with every request made by the Bank. I was assured that two separate fraud investigations would be opened and that the matter would be thoroughly investigated. Based on those assurances, I believed Wells Fargo would carefully review the circumstances surrounding this highly sophisticated fraud and objectively evaluate the evidence. Unfortunately, that was not my experience. Throughout this process, the bank never requested information from me regarding the case. They never asked for the police report, the text messages or the emails that caused me to fall victim to this fraud scheme. XXXX XXXX XXXX Department approached my claim as though I was responsible for what happened, rather than recognizing that I was the victim of an elaborate and well-orchestrated criminal scheme. At no point did I feel that my concerns were taken seriously or that the investigators demonstrated any empathy for the significant financial and emotional impact this crime has had on me. One of my greatest concerns is that there were numerous indicators of suspicious account activity that, in my opinion, should have triggered additional fraud prevention measures or, at a minimum, prompted immediate contact from the Bank. Within a very short period of time : My online banking password was changed multiple times. I was locked out of my own online banking account. Passwords associated with my credit card accounts were changed. Cash advances totaling approximately {$5600.00} were processed against my credit card accounts. These events were completely inconsistent with my normal banking behavior. I have been a loyal Wells Fargo customer for many years. During that time, I had never taken a cash advance against my credit cards, nor had I ever repeatedly changed my online banking passwords within minutes of one another. These activities represented a dramatic departure from my established account history. I repeatedly asked Wells Fargo representatives why these multiple password changes, account lockouts, and unusual cash advances did not generate heightened fraud alerts or additional verification procedures before the transactions were completed. To date, I have never received a meaningful explanation. Instead, Wells Fargo concluded that because I ultimately withdrew the money and handed it to criminals while acting under the false belief that I was assisting Wells Fargo and federal investigators, I had " received the benefit '' of the cash advances and was therefore solely responsible for repaying the {$5600.00}. I respectfully disagree with that conclusion. The fact that I physically withdrew the funds does not change the reality that I was deceived through criminal impersonation, social engineering, and fraudulent representations into surrendering those funds. I did not receive any benefit from this transaction. I was manipulated into acting under the belief that I was protecting my accounts and assisting Wells Fargo and law enforcement in an active fraud investigation. What has been equally disappointing has been Wells Fargo 's handling of my complaint after the initial report. I spoke with numerous representatives within Wells Fargo 's Executive Complaint Department who repeatedly assured me that they would keep me informed throughout the investigation and maintain communication with me. Those promises were never fulfilled. Instead, after long periods with little or no communication, I received form denial letters stating that Wells Fargo found no basis to approve my fraud claim and that I remained responsible for the entire {$5600.00} balance. There was no meaningful discussion of the extensive evidence I provided, no explanation addressing the specific concerns I raised regarding the suspicious activity on my accounts, and no indication that the sophisticated nature of this fraud had been seriously evaluated. As a result, I have been left feeling ignored, dismissed, and treated as though I was at fault simply because I became the victim of a highly sophisticated criminal enterprise. Because I believe this matter raises significant concerns regarding customer protection, fraud detection procedures, and the handling of fraud claims, I have sought assistance from every available regulatory and consumer protection agency. In addition to this complaint to the XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, I have filed complaints with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency ( XXXX ) and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ). I have also sought assistance from XXXX 's XXXX XXXX XXXX and contacted local investigative reporters in the XXXX area in the hope that greater public awareness may help prevent other consumers from becoming victims of similar schemes. Finally, I am forwarding this complaint directly to the Executive Office of Wells Fargo, including Chief Executive Officer XXXX XXXX and the Board of Directors, because I believe senior leadership should be aware not only of the sophisticated fraud that occurred, but also of how my claim was handled after I reported it. My purpose in pursuing these complaints extends beyond recovering my financial loss. I want Wells Fargo to thoroughly examine whether its fraud detection systems, customer protections, and investigative processes are adequately protecting customers from increasingly sophisticated impersonation schemes. I also hope that my experience will lead to improvements that prevent other innocent customers from enduring the financial loss, emotional distress, and lasting impact that I continue to experience.

They say that they are in regulation except they falsified his account as abandoned even though there was a death certificate provided. The account was made and maintained here in Floridas Bank of America National Association Branch which National banks do not follow a single federal escheatment statute ; instead, they must comply with the individual unclaimed property and escheat laws of each state. These state statutes dictate the dormancy periods ( typically XXXX to 5 years ) and the due diligence procedures required before banks turn abandoned assets over to state custody. An inactivity window from XX/XX/XXXX to XX/XX/XXXX, is only 2 years and 8 months. Under Florida Statute Chapter 717, the statutory dormancy period required for a bank account to be legally classified as abandoned is 5 years Premature Escheatment ( Statutory Violation ) : The bank violated Florida 's unclaimed property timelines. They failed to hold the property for the legally mandated 5 years before declaring it abandoned Breach of Fiduciary Duty & Contract : By failing to honor a valid Florida probate court order ( Summary of Administration ) and instead moving the funds out of the estates reach, the bank breached its depository agreement. Negligence : The bank 's operations team failed to process the legal documentation provided on XX/XX/XXXX. Escheating the funds 10 days later shows a total breakdown of internal legal processing.

narrative: On XX/XX/year>, I used my Wells Fargo debit card at XXXX XXXX in XXXX, North Carolina. I authorized XXXX transaction for {$21.00}. The merchant swiped my card a second time and submitted a separate transaction for {$99.00} that I did not authorize or approve. I received no goods, services, or other benefit in exchange for the {$99.00} transaction. I immediately notified Wells Fargo and opened Claim Reference Number XXXX on XX/XX/year>. I clearly explained that the {$21.00} transaction was authorized and that the separate {$99.00} transaction was not. This is not a claim involving dissatisfaction with a purchase. It is a claim involving a second card transaction that the merchant processed without my authorization. The {$99.00} transaction qualifies as an error under Regulation E, 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( i ) and ( ii ), because it is either an unauthorized electronic fund transfer or an incorrect electronic fund transfer from my account. Regulation E defines an unauthorized electronic fund transfer as a transfer initiated by someone other than the consumer, without actual authority, and from which the consumer receives no benefit. 12 C.F.R. 1005.2 ( m ). The fact that I authorized a separate {$21.00} transaction with the same merchant does not establish that I authorized the additional {$99.00} transaction. The CFPB has specifically stated that a financial institution does not conduct a reasonable investigation when it summarily denies a dispute merely because the consumer previously conducted transactions with the same merchant, without considering the consumers statement that the disputed transfer was unauthorized or for an incorrect amount. Wells Fargo must promptly investigate my oral or written notice of error. It can not require me to first resolve the matter with the merchant or delay its investigation while waiting for additional documentation from me. Wells Fargo should obtain the merchants transaction records, receipts, authorization data, point of sale records, and any signature or tip documentation associated with both transactions. Wells Fargos XX/XX/year> claim confirmation states that it will make a determination within XXXX business days regarding whether the claim has been resolved, additional information is required, temporary credit will be issued, or additional investigation time is needed. Under 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( c ), Wells Fargo must either complete its investigation within the applicable XXXX business day period or provisionally credit the {$99.00} disputed amount if it requires additional time to investigate. I am requesting that Wells Fargo properly classify and investigate the {$99.00} transaction separately from the authorized {$21.00} transaction, refund the unauthorized {$99.00} charge, reverse any related fees or financial consequences, and provide its findings and supporting documentation in writing. If Wells Fargo can not complete the investigation within the applicable XXXX business day period, I request provisional credit as required by Regulation E.
